Summary: A person or animal eats a sacred book or its remains. During the ritual, this knowledge is actualised in oral speech, in the sounds of a musical instrument made from part of an animal's body, or in parts of an animal's body used for divination.

Title: The wet book.
Summary: A book containing sacred knowledge falls into the water at a crossing or gets wet in some other way. After that, the book disappears or the text becomes unreadable. Either the book is ruined (damaged) when it is dried. Or it is ruined while left unattended on the shore while the people who kept it are swimming; or it burns, although traces remain.

Title: The Lost Book.
Summary: In the past, the people possessed writing and knowledge, but these were lost, or the people missed the opportunity to acquire them.

Title: The "book" as part of the stomach.
Summary: Part of the stomach of ruminants is called a "book".

Title: Dog rights, ATU 200.
Summary: A document issued to animals (usually dogs) is lost through the fault of a cat (swallowed by a cat, burned, gnawed by mice). Since then, dogs and cats (usually also cats and mice) have been at enmity.

Title: Those who remain on earth become owls.
Summary: A character who was unable to reach the sky or returned from the sky to earth becomes an owl.

Title: The husband of a magical wife turns into a rooster.
Summary: A woman of non-human nature agrees to live with a man, but leaves him upon learning of his real or imagined infidelity.

Title: Winter hibernation of snotty creatures.
Summary: There are creatures that sleep in winter, and frozen snot hangs from their noses. (Motif identified by Evgenia Korovina).

Title: A little bird wants to fill the sea with stones.
Summary: A small bird carries pebbles and sticks, trying to fill the sea.

Title: Infants and birds.
Summary: Birds (cranes/storks, geese or crows) carry children away to another world or bring them back from there. See motif H6c3, "The Immortal Stork".

Title: A fly instead of a nail, ATU 772*.
Summary: A fly lands on the chest of the crucified Jesus. His persecutors, who intended to drive a nail into his heart, do not do so, believing that the nail has already been driven in.

Title: Indentation on the foot.
Summary: Ever since a piece of flesh was torn from a person's foot, a hollow has formed between the toe and the heel.

Title: Dent on the back.
Summary: Ever since a piece of flesh was torn from a person's back, a dent has remained along the length of the spine.

Title: Animals exchange characteristics.
Summary: The absence or presence of certain organs in animals (less often in plants) and the peculiarities of these organs are caused by the fact that during the era of creation, one species exchanged with another or, having borrowed a foreign organ, refused to return it. In some cases, a reverse exchange and return to the original state is described, as well as the transfer of part of one's body to another animal without compensation. Instead of one of the animals, there may be a human or a deity.

Title: The nightingale and the copperhead.
Summary: The nightingale (or, less commonly, someone else) takes the copper's eyes and does not return them, leaving her blind.

Title: A person going to a festival borrows someone else's organ.
Summary: A zoomorphic character goes to a festival and asks another to lend him a part of his body, which will make him look more attractive.

Title: The beaver and the muskrat swapped tails.
Summary: Previously, the beaver had the same tail as the muskrat now has, and the muskrat had the same tail as the beaver.

Title: Falling sky.
Summary: In the past, a catastrophic shift in the layers of the universe occurred or will occur in the future. Among the variants (sometimes combined): the sky fell to the earth; the present earth or underground world swapped places with the sky; the earth turned upside down; it fell into the underworld; the layers of the universe successively collapsed onto the earth or will swap places in the future.

Title: Flood and fire.
Summary: The inhabitants of the middle world (in part) are destroyed (or will be destroyed) once by fire or drought, another time by a flood, or the world is flooded with a stream of fire and boiling water.

Title: The Woodpecker's Fire.
Summary: Two characters meet a woodpecker and receive an object from it, which causes the ground to catch fire upon contact. The stronger and smarter of the two characters escapes, while the weaker and stupider one is burned or burned to death.

Title: The Burnt Moon.
Summary: The Sun and the Moon are caught in a fire. The strong and intelligent Sun escapes, while the weak and foolish Moon is burned or consumed, but the Sun revives it.

Title: The snake plugged the hole in the ark, A1853.1, (ATU 825).
Summary: The snake (eel, frog) saved the ship (or the whole world) by plugging the hole from which water was pouring with its body.

Title: The Flood: Falling Fruit.
Summary: During the flood or at the beginning of time, fruits, seeds, or other objects fall into the water one after another. As this happens, the water begins to recede, exposing the earth.

Title: The Flood: Salvation on a Tree.
Summary: During the flood, those who climbed trees were saved.

Title: Scout birds.
Summary: A bird, various birds, or people who then turn into birds are sent to explore the earth (whether it exists, whether it has dried up, whether there are any survivors, why smoke is rising from the earth, etc.) or with the task of bringing back a piece of solid substance to create dry land.

Title: Animals sent on reconnaissance.
Summary: After a global catastrophe or during the creation of the earth, animals run around, making the earth large, reporting on its condition, or are sent to find out how large the earth is.

Title: Obtaining valuables from the underworld.
Summary: In texts with an emphasis on authenticity, characters dive or otherwise descend into the underworld to bring back to earth something desirable that is located at the bottom (deep below) (aka "The Earth Diver" motifs) (cf. fairy tale motif k27x9).

Title: Diver – turtle/frog.
Summary: A turtle or toad (frog) brings a desired object from the bottom or from the underworld.

Title: Diver – muskrat (beaver, otter).
Summary: The desired object is brought up from the bottom by a muskrat (rarely a beaver or otter).

Title: The Diver – Bird.
Summary: The bird dives and brings up the desired object from the bottom. See motif C6.

Title: Birds: successful and unsuccessful divers.
Summary: Two or more different birds (in Siberia, often a loon and a duck) successively try to retrieve something from the bottom. Only one succeeds.

Title: The punished loon.
Summary: Birds must dive to retrieve soil from the bottom, from which land will emerge. The loon cannot reach the bottom, refuses to dive, or tries to hide the soil it has retrieved (usually punished for this).

Title: The loon – a successful diver.
Summary: The loon dives and brings back a piece of earth (grass, etc.), which turns into land (it is the only or the only successful diver).

Title: Duck – a successful diver.
Summary: A duck or similar waterfowl dives and brings back a piece of earth, which turns into land (it is the only or the only successful diver).

Title: Obtaining land from the underworld.
Summary: Land (earth) is formed from a small amount of solid substance (silt, sand, clay, mud) that characters retrieve from the underworld (usually from the bottom of the ocean).

Title: Diver – crab, shrimp.
Summary: A crustacean retrieves earth from under water or from the underworld.

Title: Retrieving a drowned person.
Summary: The characters attempt to retrieve a living creature or part of its body that has sunk to the bottom of the water. See motif C6.

Title: The diver – the boar.
Summary: The boar brings earth from the bottom and/or scatters it on the water.

Title: An insect brings soil.
Summary: The insect brings soil (from the bottom of the sea or from somewhere far away).

Title: Earth was taken from the belly of an invertebrate.
Summary: The earth brought from the underworld was found in the belly of a worm or insect, from where it was taken.

Title: Stuck mud turns into earth.
Summary: A zoomorphic character returns from the underworld covered in mud. He shakes himself off, or the mud is scraped off him, and earth emerges from it.

Title: A mound of earth rises above the water.
Summary: There is water everywhere. Earth is raked up from the bottom into a mound, its top rises above the water and turns into dry land.

Title: Obtaining land in connection with the creation of man.
Summary: In the same narrative, the story of the creation of man and the attempt to prevent it follows immediately after the story of obtaining earth from the bottom of the sea or from the underworld.

Title: The earth is brought by the antagonist of the deity.
Summary: An anthropomorphic deity sends someone to fetch earth from the bottom of his enemy. At first, the enemy or both characters sometimes have the appearance of birds. After the enemy brings the earth, a confrontation begins between the two characters, who now always have anthropomorphic appearances.

Title: The Flood: The Destroyed Barrier.
Summary: Initially or after the flood, an earthen or stone barrier, the body of a character or creature prevents the flow of water. Later, this barrier is removed or destroyed.

Title: Blood relatives give birth to people.
Summary: At the beginning of time or as a result of a catastrophe, the only human couple is a brother and sister (less often a mother and son, father and daughters). They marry and give birth to people.

Title: Millstones fall on each other.
Summary: Finding themselves alone and without other marriage partners, a brother and sister make it possible to marry each other by the occurrence of an incredible event. This event takes place, giving them a sign to become spouses. Among such events (alternatively or sequentially): 1) millstones rolling down from two different mountains fall on top of each other; 2) swords thrown from two mountains end up in the same scabbard; 3) objects thrown up join together; 4) smoke from two fires joins together (rising in a column); 5) two planted bamboo stalks join at the tops. See motif C8.

Title: Let the thread enter the eye.
Summary: Finding themselves alone and without other marriage partners, a brother and sister make their marriage possible by the occurrence of an incredible event: a thread far from the needle must enter the eye of the needle.

Title: Stone lion.
Summary: The lion (often stone) helps to survive the flood.

Title: Brother and sister give birth to humans.
Summary: At the beginning of time, or as a result of a catastrophe, the only human couple are a brother and sister. They marry and give birth to people.

Title: Brother and sister did not recognise each other.
Summary: A brother and sister (or mother and son) find themselves alone, without marriage partners. Both of them (or only the brother, son) refuse to marry, but do so after accepting each other (or the brother accepts the sister, the son accepts the mother) as strangers. They give birth to new people.

Title: Son and mother give birth to people.
Summary: After a global catastrophe, at the beginning of time or when settling a new land, a woman and her son give birth to humans.

Title: Father and daughter give birth to humans.
Summary: At the beginning of time or after the destruction of the rest of humanity, a father and daughter (daughters) remain. They marry and give rise to humans or certain ethnic groups.

Title: Having had smallpox, they did not recognise each other.
Summary: A brother and sister survived the flood. They married after having had smallpox and therefore did not recognise each other.

Title: Salvation in a pumpkin during the flood.
Summary: During the flood or at the beginning of time, people (usually a brother and sister) float in a large gourd.

Title: Salvation in a drum during the flood.
Summary: During the flood, a brother and sister float in a drum.

Title: Warning of the flood.
Summary: God, an animal, or a certain character warns one of the people about an impending catastrophe (usually a flood) in which most people will perish.

Title: The Flood: people turn into aquatic animals.
Summary: During the flood or when crossing a river, those who drowned or were saved turn into aquatic or amphibious animals.

Title: The Flood: Wet Tails, A2211.1.
Summary: During the flood, some birds or animals escape to a mountain, a tree, a boat, or by clinging to the sky; their tails or other parts of their bodies remain in the water and as a result acquire their current colour or shape. Cf. A2211.7 ("During the flood, birds cling to the sky; their tails acquire their current colour").

Title: Birds clinging to the sky, A2211.1.
Summary: During the flood, some birds save themselves by clinging to the sky with their beaks. Cf. A2211.7 ("During the flood, birds cling to the sky; their tails acquire their current colour").

Title: Revenge of the insulted father.
Summary: A father with magical powers destroys people (all or many) who have insulted or harmed his son.

Title: The Flood and the Dog.
Summary: The dog warns of an impending global flood or fire and advises what to do.

Title: People – descendants of dogs.
Summary: All people or individual ethnic groups, lineages, families are considered descendants of dogs (with which a man mated).

Title: Rebellion of things.
Summary: During or before the onset of a global catastrophe (flood, darkness) or (surui) at night, household items and/or stones, trees, domestic animals, and cultivated plants turn into wild birds and animals or come to life.

Title: Monsters destroy people.
Summary: During or on the eve of a global catastrophe (flood, darkness), animals or monsters attack people. (See motif C13A (rebellion of things: animated objects and/or domestic animals threaten people, attack them).)

Title: The walled-up jaguar.
Summary: A monstrous jaguar (puma) is locked in a cave or tree trunk.

Title: Products of labour become animals, E161, E168.
Summary: Contrary to human desire, processed skins, tools, and (meat) food (again) turn into (those) animals (from whose body parts they were made). Cf. motif M84.

Title: The offended mistress of animals.
Summary: The offended mistress of animals or fish takes them and food supplies away. See motif H32A.

Title: Fire pit for people.
Summary: The men of the community of the first ancestors destroy most of the people and/or themselves on a pyre or in a fire pit.

Title: Luring the sun.
Summary: A character embodying or controlling the sun hides or is hidden. In order to restore or obtain light and warmth for the first time, the character's attention is attracted or distracted by songs, music, dances, unusual gifts, indecent or strange behaviour, offers of sex, food and/or alcohol.

Title: The sun lures out the rooster.
Summary: The hidden sun is lured out by the rooster, or people believe that without the rooster's crow, the sun will not rise.

Title: Finding the sun.
Summary: The missing, hidden, concealed or stolen sun (daylight) reappears. See motif C18

Title: The child is playing with the sun
Summary: The character (except Quileut: Raven) turns into a child, asks for and receives heavenly bodies to play, or (Chukchi) comes to play with the little daughter of the owner of the stars.

Title: The drunken cannibal.
Summary: A dangerous character is killed, neutralised, and deprived of his (her) values after being cheered up at a party, lured into a trap with music, promises of alcohol, women, etc.; the same method is used to enlist the favour of a powerful helper.

Title: Drought.
Summary: During a severe drought, birds (and animals) go in search of the rainmakers and bring them back.

Title: The Toad in Search of Thunder.
Summary: During a severe drought or global fire, birds and animals are sent to the thunder gods living at the edge of the world to bring rain. The last of those sent achieves the goal. The toad plays an important role in the action.

Title: The tree blocks the sun.
Summary: The growth or fall of a giant tree determines the state of the sky and the celestial bodies in it (the tree blocks the light of the sun or threatens to destroy the sky, pulls the sun from the sky when it falls, etc.).

Title: The world is in danger of falling.
Summary: Someone is gnawing or chopping at the pillar supporting the sky or the earth; certain creatures are trying to destroy the barrier separating their world from the world of humans; if the work is completed, humans will perish.

Title: Eschatological expectations.
Summary: If a certain event occurs, the world will be destroyed.

Title: Cooking soup on the moon.
Summary: In the sky, on the moon, somewhere outside our world, a character (usually an old woman) cooks soup. The fate of the universe depends on his (her) behaviour.

Title: The Moon Spinner.
Summary: In the sky, on the moon (rarely – on the sun), somewhere outside our world, a certain character spins, weaves, knits, embroiders or makes bast fabric.

Title: The Big Dipper and the end of the world.
Summary: A change in the configuration of a certain constellation (usually the Big Dipper) or its disappearance from the sky will signal a global catastrophe.

Title: Guardian at the edge of a foreign world.
Summary: Monsters are ready to invade our world from another, but a powerful character protects people from the invasion.

Title: Monster under the ice.
Summary: The monster breaks the ice on a river or lake. Usually people walk on the ice, see a protruding horn (fin), and try to saw it off. The monster breaks the ice, and many people die.

Title: Rash promise.
Summary: A demonic character takes possession of a valuable item without which another character (and people) will perish. The demon is tricked into returning the valuable item.

Title: Overheard secret.
Summary: People (God) learn a secret by overhearing (spying on) a character talking to himself or his relatives (or performing actions that should be remembered). The knowledge gained is related to cosmogony or the acquisition of cultural values.

Title: Impossible condition.
Summary: In order to free himself from an obligation, the character sets a condition that is formally logical and uncomplicated, but in reality impossible to fulfil.

Title: A pound of flesh, ATU 890.
Summary: A man borrows money on the condition that if he fails to repay it by a certain date, he will have to give the lender a certain amount of his own flesh. The lender cannot cut off the flesh, because he is unable to fulfil the formally logical but essentially absurd demand made of him.

Title: Remove traces from the field.
Summary: In response to the claims of an animal or spirit, a person offers to remove their traces from the field or to walk without leaving any traces. The spirit is unable to do so.

Title: Drinking the sea.
Summary: A man promises to drink the sea (to count how many drops of water there are in the sea), but asks his opponent to first separate the sea water from the water of the rivers flowing into the sea.

Title: Not to spill a drop of urine.
Summary: The character agrees that his locus will be contaminated with excrement, but only on condition that not a drop of urine is spilled. It turns out to be impossible to fulfil this condition.

Title: The wise hedgehog (cosmology).
Summary: The hedgehog is wiser or more cunning than all the gods and animals; it possesses knowledge that is vital for human existence.

Title: Lights or fire promised to the devil.
Summary: The master (mistress) of the underworld receives (should receive) heavenly lights or fire. Due to a trick or accident, they are not given to him or are returned.

Title: The wise owl.
Summary: The owl is wiser and more intelligent than other living creatures.

Title: The wise bat.
Summary: The bat turns out to be smarter and wiser than other living creatures.

Title: A ship made of nails.
Summary: Demonic characters will make a ship out of nail clippings.

Title: Nails (hair) will be needed by the soul in the afterlife.
Summary: Nails will be needed in the afterlife to save oneself (to climb a steep mountain, climb into the sky, build a bridge, etc.).

Title: Nails – material for the devil.
Summary: Demonic characters will make something useful for themselves (and harmful to humans) out of nail clippings.

Title: Nails must be preserved.
Summary: Nails (and hair) have special significance for a person's fate, their soul or the world as a whole. (Compound motif).

Title: Prometheus (the chained strongman).
Summary: A strongman-god-fighter is chained to a rock or a pillar for centuries.

Title: The restored chain.
Summary: Throughout the year, someone tries to saw through or break the chain or rope that holds him or another character. On a certain day of the year, when the chain has become completely thin, it is restored to its former state, or the pole to which the chain is attached is reinserted into the ground. Cf. motif G8d.

Title: Bird pecking at the liver.
Summary: A bird of prey flies to the chained character every day and pecks at his internal organs. The character recovers overnight, and the cycle repeats itself.

Title: Ancient windlessness.
Summary: The demise of the first race is associated with the appearance of wind.

Title: The Flood: the wounded creature.
Summary: The flood begins after people kill (harm, maim) some kind of creature (usually aquatic).

Title: Buried in the sand.
Summary: A supernatural character goes with people to catch fish or lives on the sand by the river; he is buried in the sand or thrown into the river, into a swamp, or otherwise persecuted. Usually, he himself or his father sends a flood.

Title: The cosmic marriage will not take place.
Summary: It becomes known that if characters representing natural phenomena and parts of the universe marry, it will lead to disaster. The marriage is broken off.

Title: The good advisor is punished.
Summary: A zoomorphic character gives wise advice concerning the state of the Sun. The advice is accepted, but the advisor is punished by the Sun or is henceforth pursued by the Sun.

Title: Frogs – enemies of the sun.
Summary: The frog (toad) prevents more than one sun from shining in the sky.

Title: The Last Battle.
Summary: The gods and their powerful adversaries clash in a decisive battle that changes the fate of the world. See Bray 2000, especially pp. 360-361.

Title: The sloth's catastrophe.
Summary: The sloth causes a global catastrophe or saves people from it.

Title: People will appear soon.
Summary: Characters from the time of creation say that real people will appear soon, so we must do this and that.

Title: Repairing the sky.
Summary: When the sky split or partially collapsed, it was repaired.

Title: The sky was patched up with ice.
Summary: A hole in the sky or a crack in the ground was plugged with a piece of ice, which is why it is cold in the north (north-west, north-east).

Title: Stones fall from the sky.
Summary: At first, stones fell from the sky and crushed people.

Title: Why the sky is blue.
Summary: At first, the sky has no specific colour. After a character hangs a cloth on it or performs other actions, the sky acquires its characteristic colour.

Title: Woman-fire.
Summary: A woman (usually elderly) is the embodiment of fire – alone or together with her husband, the master of fire. Cf. motif D5 (woman possesses fire).

Title: Mother-in-law-fire.
Summary: A girl marries a man whose mother is fire.

Title: The old woman-fire takes the child away.
Summary: Because a woman offended the fire, its mistress takes her child away.

Title: A borrowed object does not burn.
Summary: The house of the person who insulted the fire burns down, but the property inside it or the child of another person (or that person himself) who treated the fire with respect is not harmed.

Title: The fire wife.
Summary: A man marries a woman who is fire. She is mistreated, or her husband does not like her, and the marriage breaks down.

Title: Conversation between two fires.
Summary: Two fires from different dwellings meet and converse.

Title: Man-fire.
Summary: The man is the master or embodiment of fire (alone or alongside the woman-fire).

Title: Birth of the sun/fire.
Summary: A woman gives birth to a son who is very hot.

Title: Mother dies giving birth to fire or the sun.
Summary: A woman gives birth to a son who is the embodiment of fire or the sun and dies from burns.

Title: The invention of fire.
Summary: The first fire was obtained by friction or striking; a certain character gives fire or shows how to obtain it, teaches how to cook food on fire; fire was obtained from lightning. {The section is incomplete, there is much more data. A specific plot of the invention of fire hardly exists. Variants involving abduction and invention are often intertwined in the same narrative}.

Title: Theft of fire, A1415.
Summary: Fire is stolen from its original owner, returned to people by the thief, or (the motif of theft is not expressed) brought with difficulty from a distant place.

Title: Luring fire.
Summary: A certain character possesses fire or steals it. His attention is attracted or distracted by singing, music, dancing, unusual gifts, indecent or strange behaviour, offers of sex, food and/or alcohol.

Title: The butterfly tries to steal fire.
Summary: Moths try to steal the fire that humans possess.

Title: Retribution for fire.
Summary: Those who stole or asked for fire and/or those who received fire are punished by the deity.

Title: Obtaining summer.
Summary: Characters obtain the warm season from its original owners.

Title: A floating elk distracts attention.
Summary: Animal-people come to steal summer from its owners. One of them, in the guise of an elk or caribou, distracts the owners' attention or floats a log or stump down the river, which the owners of summer mistake for an elk and rush after.

Title: The opossum obtains fire.
Summary: The opossum obtains fire for humans. See motif D4A.

Title: Coyote or fox obtains fire.
Summary: The thief or giver of fire, light or sun is a coyote or fox (indicated in square brackets). See motif 4A.

Title: Dog and fire.
Summary: The thief or giver of fire, light or sun is the dog. See motif 4A.

Title: Beavers or fish allow themselves to be roasted.
Summary: Once in the fire, the beaver (in North America) or fish (in South America) scatters and/or carries the fire away from its original owners. See motif D4A.

Title: The hummingbird obtains fire.
Summary: Hummingbird steals, finds or spreads fire. See motif D4A.

Title: The swallow obtains fire.
Summary: The swallow obtains fire for people. See motif D4A.

Title: The robin obtains fire.
Summary: A small songbird (redstart, robin, wren) obtains fire for humans.

Title: The beaver obtains fire.
Summary: The beaver obtains fire for humans. See motif D4A.

Title: The rabbit obtains fire.
Summary: The thief, the thief's assistant, or the owner of fire is a rabbit, a hare, or (ofaye) a guinea pig. See motif D4A.

Title: The deer obtains fire.
Summary: The deer obtains fire for humans. See motif D4A.

Title: Fire from the sky.
Summary: The first fire is brought down to earth from the sky; the first ancestors go to the sky and bring back fire or warmth. See motif D4A.

Title: The owners of fire dance.
Summary: The thief comes to the owners of fire or light. They feast or dance. He joins them and steals their valuables when the moment is right. See motif D4A.

Title: The weeping one demands summer.
Summary: A boy or (among the Kutené) a woman cries, demanding the absent elements - summer, fire, rain. See motif D4A (demand for summer).

Title: Dry by the fire.
Summary: In order to steal fire from its owner, the character pretends to be wet and cold, and after receiving permission to dry off, runs away, bringing fire to the people.

Title: The parrot obtains fire.
Summary: The parrot obtains fire for humans. See motif D4A. Australian data is not taken into account, as the common origin of the motif in America and Australia is excluded.

Title: The fly obtains fire.
Summary: The fly rubs its legs together and produces fire.

Title: The bat and fire.
Summary: The bat participates in obtaining fire.

Title: Woman controls fire.
Summary: The original owner or inventor (but not the embodiment) of fire is a female character.

Title: Fire in a woman's genitals.
Summary: The first fire is hidden in a woman's genitals or anus.

Title: Crocodile and fire.
Summary: The crocodile/caiman is the temporary or original owner of fire or lightning.

Title: The burned one becomes a caiman.
Summary: The one who is burned turns into a crocodile/caiman.

Title: Toad and fire.
Summary: The frog or toad possesses the first fire, steals it from its original owner, and tries to extinguish it or save it from dying out. See motif D4.

Title: Spider and fire.
Summary: The spider possesses the first fire or steals it from its original owner (texts in which the spider acts together with other animals and does not play the main role are not included).

Title: Predator and fire.
Summary: The first fire (or summer) is stolen from a large predator – a lion or leopard in Africa, a tiger in Asia, a bear in northern Asia and North America, and a jaguar in South America.

Title: Vultures and fire.
Summary: The raven or other large dark-coloured bird of prey is the owner, embodiment, spouse, provider or thief of fire, the sun or daylight.

Title: The fire drill is a pair of people.
Summary: A couple of people serve as the embodiment of a tool for obtaining fire.

Title: Food was heated on the body.
Summary: Before fire was known, food was prepared by warming it with the body (usually under the armpit); fire is kept under the character's armpit.

Title: Food was heated in the sun.
Summary: People in the past or inhabitants of distant lands cooked food in the sun; or the owner of the fire lies, saying that the food was cooked in this way.

Title: At sunrise, the sun's heat is sufficient to cook food.
Summary: People living in the east or west prepare food using the heat of the passing sun.

Title: Laughter.
Summary: A character loses their values (gives them away) and/or suffers damage/is healed/is transformed if they laugh or hear laughter.

Title: Obscene dance for the Sun.
Summary: To amuse the owner of fire or the Sun, others dance indecently, imitate copulation, display their genitals, or publicly relieve themselves.

Title: Menstruation passes to women.
Summary: Menstruation passes from men to women after women laugh at an old man.

Title: The trickster makes his brother's wife laugh.
Summary: Two companions or brothers live together. The older one has a wife, whom he hides. To discover her, the younger one, left alone in the house, makes her laugh.

Title: Making the hidden one laugh.
Summary: One character tries to make another character, who is hiding somewhere in the house, laugh in order to find them.

Title: Hunters laugh at the carcass of an animal.
Summary: Hunters perish because they laughed at the killed (and revived) animal.

Title: Laughter and fire.
Summary: Laughter causes the appearance or spread of fire or the sun. Usually, the owner of fire or the sun loses it after bursting into laughter.

Title: Meat on the teeth.
Summary: When the character starts laughing, people see his or her scary mouth (lots of teeth, human flesh on the teeth); they kill the monster or run away.

Title: He who goes to the dead must not laugh.
Summary: Those who have entered the world of the dead should not laugh.

Title: Those who visit another world should not laugh.
Summary: A person visiting another world should not laugh or show surprise when seeing strange things. Those who break this rule will perish or suffer harm.

Title: Broken tooth.
Summary: The character amuses the audience in order to identify the deceiver and thief by his broken tooth. The latter laughs and gives himself away.

Title: The one who showed his teeth was exposed.
Summary: The characteristics of a character can be determined by his teeth. By laughing and showing his teeth, the character reveals himself.

Title: The creation of man.
Summary: The first human being was created, made by a certain character, and did not exist initially (on earth, underground, in the sky, in a small container) and did not arise spontaneously. Only variants that specify the material from which humans were created, or that refer separately to the creation of the human figure and its ensoulment, rather than simply to the fact of "creation" itself, are taken into account.

Title: The first humans made of fragile materials.
Summary: The first humans are made of fragile materials (clay, wax, fire, honey, etc.) and prove to be unviable.

Title: Soaked by rain (why there are cripples).
Summary: A deity or ancestor moulds people from clay. Some of the figures got wet, which is why there are cripples among people.

Title: Man made of unsuitable material.
Summary: A character made of unsuitable material and turns out to be short-lived or poorly suited to performing his functions.

Title: Prohibited work for a daughter-in-law.
Summary: A man who has married an unusual girl is warned that she must not perform certain tasks or eat certain foods. Other members of his household ensure that the young woman breaks the prohibition, and as a result she dies or disappears.

Title: Man made of excrement.
Summary: Man made from human excrement or (Inupiat) from carrion.

Title: Clay boats.
Summary: (The first) boat is made of obviously unsuitable material.

Title: Son-stalk.
Summary: The son of the first human couple initially takes the form of a small plant that has grown from the ground, a stalk.

Title: People on trial.
Summary: When creating humans, the creator does not immediately achieve perfection. The first versions of the creation are rejected, then the appropriate form and material are found. See motif E1A.

Title: New people from the bones of the old.
Summary: After the destruction of the previous world, new people (rarely: new earth) are made from the remains of the dead.

Title: Creation from mud on the skin, A1263.3.
Summary: From mud on the skin (rarely: from under the fingernails), the character creates the earth, people or other creatures.

Title: The half-finished man tries to stand up.
Summary: God makes man out of clay. He must wait until it dries, but tries to stand up earlier.

Title: People from the underworld, A1234.
Summary: The first humans (or only the first men or first women) were not created by a demiurge, but emerged from under the ground (from a cave) or from a small object on its surface (a tree, stone, pumpkin, etc.). There are many emerging humans (or humans and animals). Cf. motif E5B: first ancestors from the underworld.

Title: People grew like grass.
Summary: The first people grew out of the ground like trees, grass, and mushrooms.

Title: First ancestors from the underworld.
Summary: The first human (a group of brothers) or the first human couple emerge from underground (from a cave) or from a small object on the surface (a mound, a reed, a tree, a stone, a pumpkin). Cf. motif E5A: people from the underworld.

Title: People from the sky.
Summary: The first humans or deities-ancestors descend to earth from the sky.

Title: The predator watches over those who leave.
Summary: The first people to arrive on earth and settle within a limited space are threatened by a predator or monster.

Title: The two-headed creature does not come out onto the ground.
Summary: People or animals come out from under the ground or descend from the sky. The two-headed creature following them gets stuck in the opening or is not allowed to come out.

Title: Because of a woman, the connection between worlds is broken.
Summary: When a woman of childbearing age (she is menstruating, miscarrying, pregnant, with a child, or simply fat) tries to pass from one world to another, the connection between the worlds is severed forever.

Title: The path through water.
Summary: People walk across a (frozen) body of water to reach their current place of residence, while some remain on the other side or drown.

Title: Stuck in a hole in the sky.
Summary: The path from one part of the world to another passes through a narrow opening. The character gets stuck in the opening, permanently severing the connection between the worlds.

Title: Wooden people.
Summary: The first humans or the wife of the first ancestor were made of wood.

Title: People in fruits.
Summary: Women or people in general emerge from fruits (often coconuts), or fruits or, less commonly, leaves turn into people or only women. Cf. motif k33c.

Title: Woman hides in a fruit.
Summary: A woman hides inside a fruit brought into the house and comes out when no one is around or when the fruit is cut open.

Title: Woman hides in a splinter.
Summary: A woman hides inside a splinter or branch brought into the house and comes out when no one is around.

Title: The Unknown Mistress, N831.1.
Summary: The character notices that someone is running the house in his absence and catches the person doing so by surprise.

Title: The magical wife - the fox.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of a fox.

Title: The fox wife in the burrow of all animals.
Summary: A man searches for a missing woman, who is a fox by nature, and comes to the burrow where she has hidden. Various bird or animal women come out of the burrow and offer themselves in place of the fox. Then they let him inside.

Title: The magical wife – the elephant.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of an elephant (elephant tusk).

Title: The magical wife – a hoofed animal.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of a large hoofed mammal (buffalo, antelope, moose, etc.).

Title: The magical wife – the dog.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of a dog or puppy (wolf cub).

Title: A puppy received as a reward.
Summary: An animal or object received by a young man from supernatural beings as a reward for his kindness, upon the young man's return home (to earth), turns into a girl.

Title: The magical wife – the parrot.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of a parrot.

Title: The magical wife - the vulture.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of a vulture.

Title: The magical wife - the dove.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of a dove.

Title: The magical wife – the swan.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) takes the form of a swan.

Title: The magical wife – the duck.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper, adopted daughter) takes the form of a duck.

Title: The magical wife – the goose.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) has the image of a goose.

Title: The magical wife – the crane.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife, helper) takes the form of a crane.

Title: The magical wife - the snail.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his wife takes the form of a snail.

Title: The magical wife – monkey.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife) has the image of a monkey, or the man hides the woman and pretends that the mistress is a monkey.

Title: Monkeys - ancestors of humans.
Summary: Humans are considered descendants of monkeys.

Title: Husband-honey (bee).
Summary: The husband or wife is the embodiment of honey or a human bee.

Title: The magical wife – mouse.
Summary: Before meeting the hero, his beloved (wife) has the image of a mouse (rarely: a rat).

Title: The magical wife – the bear.
Summary: A man marries a bear (white or grizzly) that takes the form of a woman, or a woman who takes the form of a bear.

Title: The magical wife – an aquatic mammal.
Summary: A man marries a female seal, seal or dolphin that has taken the form of a woman and lives with her among people.

Title: The magical wife – a frog or a toad.
Summary: A man marries a woman who has the appearance of a frog or toad.

Title: Young animals turn into children.
Summary: Characters who have shed their animal (plant, object) forms become the children of women or spouses who catch them off guard.

Title: Burnt skin.
Summary: The future family member reveals himself or remains with the person after the object that defines the character's non-human appearance is destroyed. After the person destroys (usually burns) the discarded animal skin, the character retains his human appearance. See motif E9.

Title: The living drawing.
Summary: A character draws an object or creature on sand, ash, a wall or the surface of water, and it comes to life.

Title: Tambourine – lake.
Summary: The shamanic tambourine is compared or associated with a lake.

Title: Knowledge from the underwater world.
Summary: Sacred knowledge, objects and rituals were first obtained by humans from the inhabitants of the underwater world.

Title: Knowledge from the sky.
Summary: Sacred knowledge, objects and rituals received from the celestials.

Title: Knowledge from the dead.
Summary: Rituals received from the spirits of the dead.

Title: Masks reproduce slain demons.
Summary: People kill demons, examine their bodies, make ritual costumes and masks, reproducing the appearance of the slain.

Title: Ducks and boats.
Summary: People learn how to build boats and row from birds; a bird or part of its body serves as a model for building a boat.

Title: The boat as a bird's breastbone.
Summary: The bow of the boat is modelled on a bird's breastbone.

Title: Birds sew a boat.
Summary: Bird women sew the birch bark covering of the hero's boat. See motif E15.

Title: Oars with edges.
Summary: When rowing, the character first tries to push off with the edge rather than the flat side of the oar.

Title: The origin of ornamentation.
Summary: People get the idea of ornamentation of vessels, baskets, bodies, etc., or of a sign system after someone manages to see a pattern on the body of a zoomorphic or supernatural creature or make an imprint of it.

Title: Vessels and snakes.
Summary: People learn to make or decorate ceramics or baskets (usually learning to apply patterns) thanks to a water creature.

Title: The origin of drugs.
Summary: Narcotic plants arise from the body of a human being torn to pieces by others.

Title: The origin of fish poison.
Summary: When a certain person enters the water, the fish die. A plant grows from parts of his body or on his grave, from which fish poison (timbó) is made.

Title: The victim of aquatic creatures finds revenge.
Summary: A child catches fish (with poison), or fish poison is secreted from his body. Fish or water snakes kill him. Death is avenged.

Title: The swallowed gains knowledge.
Summary: Once inside a certain creature, the swallowed character learns rituals, songs, ornamental motifs, obtains drugs or poison, and, once outside again, passes this knowledge on to people.

Title: Revival by fleas.
Summary: A handful of fleas or lice must be thrown at the character; only this will make him or her move, which is necessary for revival or for the existence of people.

Title: Knees and elbows.
Summary: Joints appeared in humans after the first ancestor (or several first ancestors) fell from a height, breaking their arms and legs.

Title: Arachne (spider weaver).
Summary: People learn the art of weaving from a spider or from a person who later becomes a spider; the spider makes fabrics for humans.

Title: Those who have become fish are turned back into humans.
Summary: People, or only women, go underwater and turn into fish. Men catch them with fishing gear. Those who are caught become human (women) again. (Narratives about the transformation of only one caught fish into the hero's wife are not included; see motif F7).

Title: People from drops of blood.
Summary: People arise from drops of blood from a wounded anthropomorphic creature.

Title: The blood of the Moon pours onto the earth.
Summary: People shoot at the Moon, its blood spills onto the earth.

Title: The lizard makes hands for humans, A1311.1.
Summary: Two characters (usually a coyote and a lizard) argue about whether human hands should be shaped like paws or end in fingers.

Title: Wooden substitute spouse.
Summary: A man has no wife or a woman has no husband, and uses a wooden substitute as a spouse.

Title: The ersatz spouse is replaced by the real one.
Summary: A man without a wife or a woman without a husband uses a substitute spouse made of wood or other material until a real spouse appears.

Title: Pygmalion.
Summary: A man makes a figure or receives a woman. She comes to life and becomes his wife.

Title: Imaginary Pygmalion.
Summary: A man makes a wooden doll and behaves as if it were alive. It does not come to life, or comes to life only partially or temporarily. A real woman replaces the figure and marries the carver.

Title: Creators and saviours of girls, ATU 653, 653A, 653B.
Summary: Several men (women) participate in the rescue, creation or revival of a girl (man), or mourn her (his) death. The question arises as to whom the revived person should belong to or who contributed more to the revival. Alternatively, three men create something valuable, each contributing their part. The question arises as to whose contribution is more important.

Title: Who will be the husband of the created girl? ATU 653C.
Summary: Three (rarely four or two) men participate in the creation of the girl: one carves the figure out of wood, another dresses her, and the third brings her to life. To whom should the animated girl belong?

Title: One is her father, another is her brother, and this one is her husband.
Summary: The girl must be given to one of several men. She herself or someone else explains that one of the suitors can be called her father, another her brother (etc.), and only one can be her husband.

Title: Female saviours of men.
Summary: Several women participate in reviving a dead man and argue about who did more to revive him.

Title: Rescuers of the Abducted Maiden, ATU 513A, ATU 653.
Summary: Several men, each possessing a unique skill, bring a (kidnapped) girl from a distant country.

Title: Progenitor plants.
Summary: The first humans or the first woman (progenitor, goddess) are born from trees, emerge from a tree, stump, flower, or reed.

Title: People from grains.
Summary: People arise from grains, seeds, dough.

Title: Sacred flutes made from the ashes of a cannibal.
Summary: The cannibal is killed. From his ashes arise musical instruments taboo for women, used in male rituals.

Title: Webbing between the fingers.
Summary: The first humans or creatures created by the Creator's rival were incomplete, not fully anthropomorphic (they resembled larvae, had webbing on their fingers, etc.).

Title: Hard covering of the body.
Summary: The human body was or could have been covered with a protective layer (bone, rarely wool), but it has only been preserved on the nails (head).

Title: Growing nails.
Summary: Nails grow constantly, or the human body is covered with a hard crust only on the nails, because only they were washed with living water.

Title: People made of sticks.
Summary: The creator collects many sticks, feathers, reeds, etc., and turns them into people (either people of both sexes and all ages, or no mention is made of gender or age).

Title: People made of pieces.
Summary: A woman gives birth to a pumpkin, a sack, a sack of eggs, a piece of meat. The newborn is cut open, chopped up, and the pieces turn into new people; numerous people (usually tribal ancestors) emerge from the pumpkin or sack. Cf. motif F47.

Title: People from a pumpkin.
Summary: After a global catastrophe or at the beginning of time, a pumpkin appears on earth, from which the ancestors of humans emerge.

Title: The first humans are mute.
Summary: The first humans were mute and began to speak after being struck by something, made to laugh, etc.

Title: Pig ancestor.
Summary: The child of a pig or boar is a woman or man – the ancestor of a certain group of people.

Title: A female animal conceives from human urine.
Summary: An animal (snake, pig) conceives from a man's urine and gives birth to a human child (or twins).

Title: Nostrils facing upwards.
Summary: The first humans had nostrils facing upwards, into which rain poured.

Title: The blacksmith kneads iron with his hands.
Summary: A skilled blacksmith, as a special gift, can take iron heated in a furnace with his bare hands, knead it like dough, and shape it as desired. Usually, he breaks a certain taboo and loses his gift. (The motif was identified and the material collected by Ruslan Doutalieyev).

Title: How ticks were invented.
Summary: The first ticks were made as a result of observing animals (a dog's crossed paws, two snakes, snake jaws, etc.).

Title: The appearance of female breasts.
Summary: Women have two breasts because the original breast was cut in half.

Title: Transformed man.
Summary: The first woman, female deity, or female animals were originally men (males) who then changed their gender.

Title: Birth from the leg T541; V52.
Summary: The child is born from a tumour on the character's body, either placed there temporarily or emerging from blood that has flowed from a cut.

Title: Improper birth.
Summary: The child deliberately leaves its mother's womb in an unusual way, making a hole in her body and often killing her. This is a sign of its malice and/or supernatural power.

Title: The husband gives birth after eating what was intended for his wife (ATU 705A).
Summary: A man accidentally eats a magical remedy intended for a woman to become pregnant and gives birth to a child. The child comes out of a tumour on the man's leg, or in some other way, but the man remains alive.

Title: Pregnant man.
Summary: A man carries a child like a woman.

Title: Child in a vessel, T561.
Summary: In the days of the first ancestors, children were conceived not through sexual intercourse, but in vessels, piles of earth, lumps of clay, etc.

Title: Brides for the first humans.
Summary: The character does not want to or cannot give all the suitors his daughters in marriage and turns them into girls of various animals. (Usually after the flood or at the beginning of time, men want to marry the only daughter of a deity or patriarch).

Title: Woman from a tail, ATU 798.
Summary: God was going to make Eve from Adam's rib. The rib was stolen by a dog (cat, fox, monkey, devil). God (or an angel sent by him) chased after the thief, grabbed him by the tail and tore it off. God made Eve from this tail. Either God first made a woman from edible material and the dog ate this figure. He had to make a new one from Adam's rib. Or God cut off Adam's tail and made Eve from it.

Title: Artificial bride.
Summary: The character (listed in square brackets in the list of ethnic groups) offers another woman. Not having one or not wanting to give her away, he makes a bride out of wood, snow, etc., turns an animal into a girl, sends a servant instead of his daughter, turns himself into a woman, or confesses to the lie when the trouble is over. See motif E8.

Title: Hollowed-out vagina.
Summary: (The first) woman does not have a vagina at first. Usually, it is made for her by a bird, animal, fish, etc.

Title: Woman from the underwater world.
Summary: A man catches, grabs, meets, or receives a woman associated with the aquatic-chthonic world (a fish, mermaid, snake, crab, seal, etc.) and takes her as his wife. Cf. motifs E26 and K25.

Title: Meeting of men and women.
Summary: In the beginning (.55.60.67.73.) women and men lived separately from each other, then came together. Cf. motif F45 (Amazons).

Title: Dangerous woman.
Summary: For various reasons, sexual intercourse with a woman is deadly dangerous for a man, or so it seems to him: Teeth, blades or sharp stones in the vagina or on the inside of the thighs; the vagina is a toothy mouth. See motif F9A.

Title: Toothy womb.
Summary: There are teeth, blades or sharp stones in a woman's vagina or on the inside of her thighs; the vagina is a toothy mouth. (Only texts with a focus on authenticity are taken into account, not anecdotes).

Title: The pike's mouth, ATU 1686A*.
Summary: A girl or young woman says (pretends) that she has a predatory mouth in her vagina. {Unlike variants characteristic of the circum-Pacific region, the corresponding texts do not suggest that the female womb is actually dangerous}.

Title: Piranha in the vagina.
Summary: A biting piranha in a woman's genitals.

Title: Snake in the vagina.
Summary: Snake (in Oceania – moray eel) in the vagina; vagina – snake's mouth; snake crawls out of a woman's mouth and bites off a man's penis during intercourse; woman with a toothy womb is associated with a snake.

Title: Scorpions in the genitals.
Summary: Small stinging creatures dangerous to the partner are found in the genitals of women or men.

Title: Mice in the vagina.
Summary: Small mammals with sharp teeth are found in a woman's vagina.

Title: Dangerous animal in the vagina.
Summary: A woman's womb is dangerous because it contains a toothy or stinging animal (not just its mouth) or many such creatures.

Title: Asmodeus.
Summary: Without the woman's knowledge, the demon regularly kills her suitors on their wedding night.

Title: Snake inside a woman.
Summary: Inside the woman there is a snake (snakes, scorpions, just poison) that comes out of her mouth. {Motifs F9f1 and K100C are almost identical, but the first can be included in the cosmological-etiological category and is associated with the idea of a dangerous woman, while the second belongs to the adventure category}.

Title: The cobra's hood in the wife's handbag.
Summary: A woman places a piece of flesh from her slain snake lover in her handbag and poses a corresponding riddle. If her husband fails to guess the answer, she has the right to kill him. The husband accidentally learns the secret and kills his wife.

Title: Brünnhilde, ATU 519.
Summary: A powerful woman defeats and kills her suitors. The hero or his assistant defeats her (usually on their wedding night, subduing her with rods or a whip). The hero marries the heroine.

Title: The heavy hand of the bride.
Summary: On her wedding night, the bride-heroine throws herself on her groom to crush him.

Title: Teeth knocked out.
Summary: A woman has a second mouth (usually in her vagina) with sharp teeth. A man inserts or throws a stone, bone, stick, etc. into this mouth, knocking out the teeth or extracting toothy animals from it in this way.

Title: Biting penis.
Summary: The penis burns, bites, eats food.

Title: A husband kills his wife with his lover's penis.
Summary: A husband kills his wife by inserting her lover's severed penis into her body.

Title: The red penis of primates.
Summary: The genitals of humans or monkeys acquire their current shape and colour as a result of copulation with a girl who had a toothy womb or no vagina.

Title: Son of a man and a stone.
Summary: The hero is born as a result of the union of a man with a stone or rock.

Title: Birth from stone.
Summary: An anthropomorphic character emerges from stone.

Title: Character sticks his penis out of the ground, K1315.2.1.
Summary: The character sticks his plant-like penis out of the ground (provoking a woman to sit on it).

Title: Men and women: exchange of characteristics.
Summary: Men possessed biological characteristics that are now characteristic of women, or vice versa (beards, menstruation, breasts, childbearing).

Title: Genitals out of place, A1313.3.
Summary: Human genitals were initially located, should have been located, or could have been located under certain circumstances not where they are now; either there were no genitals initially, or people did not know their purpose and copulated using other parts of the body.

Title: Long penis.
Summary: The penis of a male character is much longer than normal or becomes so. During intercourse, it usually crawls towards the woman like a snake. (Only texts with a focus on authenticity are included, not anecdotes).

Title: Long penis after forbidden sex.
Summary: After intercourse with a forbidden partner (incest, intercourse with an animal or spirit), a man's penis becomes so long that he is forced to carry it in a basket, etc.

Title: Girls across the river, K1391.
Summary: The character sees a girl on the other side of the river and copulates with her in an unusual way (sends his penis across the river; turns it into a bridge for the girl to cross the river; into a dam that blocks the river in front of her; dives, swimming up to the girl underwater; sends an object into the girl's vagina). See motif F18B.

Title: Long clitoris.
Summary: Female genitals were enormous in size.

Title: Dangerous relationship with a frog.
Summary: After copulating with a frog, a man's penis is crippled (unless otherwise stated: it becomes long, see motif F18A).

Title: Lovers stuck together.
Summary: After copulation, the man and woman are unable to break their embrace.

Title: People and dogs.
Summary: At first, people mated as dogs do now, but then it became as it is now.

Title: Penis stuck in a tree.
Summary: While the character copulates with a woman, she turns into a tree or a rock. His penis gets stuck in her.

Title: Studying the partner's body.
Summary: The character asks a person of the opposite sex about the purpose of the part of the body used for sexual intercourse (usually after asking questions about other parts). Alternatively, the character tries out different parts of the body for sexual intercourse or for placing the genitals. Cf. motif M63.

Title: Names of body parts.
Summary: The character repeatedly asks the woman about the names and/or functions of her body parts until he reaches the genitals.

Title: Cause of menstruation: sexual intercourse.
Summary: Blood spilled during sexual intercourse or artificial defloration at the time of creation is the reason why menstruation occurs to this day.

Title: Cause of menstruation: bite.
Summary: Women lose blood when they are bitten by fish, snakes, etc.

Title: The reason for menstruation: someone else's blood.
Summary: Women have been stained with someone else's or their own blood, or with blood-like paint, ever since women began menstruating.

Title: Cause of menstruation: loss of sacred objects.
Summary: The transfer of sacred musical instruments (horns, trumpets) from women to men is associated with the onset of menstruation in women.

Title: Girls and water spirits.
Summary: It is dangerous for girls or women to approach water (water creatures drag them away or swallow them; a girl who approaches water dies; she becomes pregnant by a snake; through her fault, a flood or other disaster occurs; water spirits themselves come to a girl who has her first period).

Title: Monstrous penis.
Summary: There is a separate penis character with whom the first women, Amazons, or simply some woman copulate.

Title: A monstrous penis grows out of the ground.
Summary: A penis grows out of the ground or out of the water in a lake. Women summon it as needed.

Title: Jumping penis.
Summary: The living penis is a dangerous creature that attacks people.

Title: Penises grow in the field.
Summary: The owner of the field, either intentionally or having misheard the question, replies that he grows penises. After that, penises grow in the field instead of crops.

Title: Pleasant for girls, dangerous for others.
Summary: A girl (woman) possesses an object that is pleasant (useful). Once in the hands of others, it becomes harmful (dangerous).

Title: Penises on plants.
Summary: The fruits or stems of plants are penises.

Title: The penis and vulva as separate beings.
Summary: The penis and vulva (in the singular or plural) are separate beings and characters.

Title: Penis made of wax.
Summary: A woman uses a penis made of wax, wood, fruit or root. Usually her husband or male relative smears it with pepper, and the woman is maimed or killed.

Title: Bear penis in the hands of an old woman.
Summary: A woman masturbates with the penis of a large animal that one of the men killed while hunting.

Title: Children are born from a wooden penis.
Summary: By masturbating with an artificial penis, a woman conceives children.

Title: A girl sits on the ground.
Summary: A girl (woman) sits on the ground and copulates with a snake, worm or eel that crawls out of the ground towards her. This usually happens when she is busy with housework (cooking, weaving, etc.).

Title: The worm is scalded with boiling water.
Summary: To kill a woman's lover, who has the appearance of a worm or snake and crawls into her vagina from under the ground, boiling water, resin or hot coals are poured on him.

Title: The snake lover.
Summary: A girl or woman takes a snake, eel, moray eel, lizard or worm as a lover or spouse. People kill or maim the lover, the woman and/or their offspring, or she herself turns into a snake. Cf. motif K76B (the snake-husband becomes and remains a handsome man). See motif F29.

Title: Child-worm.
Summary: A woman nurses a worm (caterpillar, reptile, fish) instead of a child; people kill the monster.

Title: Snake egg.
Summary: A girl or woman becomes pregnant, without knowing it, by a reptile when she unknowingly touches a dead reptile or when a liquid that has leaked from the reptile gets inside her (usually when the contents of a snake egg accidentally flow between her legs).

Title: The snake son gathers fruit.
Summary: Small children or a single infant, who temporarily transform into adult men and/or emerge from their mother's womb, or a snake living in a woman's womb, climb a tree and help her gather fruit, bark, tree mushrooms, etc.; or a father discovers his daughter's connection with a snake when he climbs a tree to gather fruit for her.

Title: Connection with a water creature.
Summary: A woman or group of women take a water animal or water monster as their lover. The husband(s), brother(s) or (adopted) children of the woman(s) kill or maim the lover and (in some cases) the woman(s).

Title: Connection with terrestrial quadrupeds.
Summary: A woman takes a large land animal as her lover. Her husband, brother or (adopted) children kill or maim the lover and (sometimes) the woman herself. Sometimes there is mention of a group of women and their husbands. (Unlike motif K102, "The Demon's Mistress," the lover is not dangerous to the hero and plays a passive role, and the woman, if she becomes hostile and dangerous, does so only after the lover's death. Unlike motif K76, the woman and her husband/lover of non-human nature are clearly evaluated negatively).

Title: The common husband of the first women.
Summary: All women of the community of the first ancestors or all Amazons have a common lover of non-human nature or simultaneously mate with animals of a certain species, summoning them with a conventional signal.

Title: Lover of non-human nature.
Summary: A girl, woman or group of women voluntarily take as their lover a penis that exists as a special creature, snake, moray eel, lizard, worm, crab, large aquatic animal or aquatic monster, or large terrestrial mammal. People kill or maim the lover, the woman and/or her offspring, or she herself loses her human nature. The woman's behaviour is condemned.

Title: Feeding meat from a lover.
Summary: A character offers another person the meat of his sexual partner, and the other person, unaware, eats or cooks it.

Title: Feeding meat from a relative.
Summary: The character, unaware of this, eats or prepares meat (slowly kills) a member of his household (a relative, rarely a servant or spouse) or feeds it to his acquaintances, or uses its bones for household needs.

Title: Children against the lover.
Summary: (Adopted) children of a woman or man kill the lover (or spouse of non-human nature) of their father or (adoptive) mother.

Title: Calabash on the water.
Summary: To summon her lover, the character taps on a calabash placed on the water.

Title: Women and secret knowledge.
Summary: Women were the keepers of secret knowledge, shrines, or ritual objects that are now forbidden to them; they attempted to regain this knowledge or these objects.

Title: Women's time.
Summary: In the past or in distant lands, women dominated men, were the active party in marital relations, and engaged in male activities. Men engaged in female activities. Later, the situation changed. Either women missed the opportunity to gain superiority. See motif F38.

Title: The common husband of the first women.
Summary: A male character, androgynous, with a monstrous penis, single-handedly possesses all women, rules over them or leads away the first women.

Title: A man in a village of women.
Summary: A single man finds himself in a village of women. Usually, he is forced to satisfy a woman against his will, or each woman demands to have sex with him.

Title: The patriarch kills the boys.
Summary: An authoritative man systematically kills the boys born to his wives or his sister.

Title: Husbands kill wives.
Summary: Ancestral men kill women who behave contrary to social norms.

Title: Men leave.
Summary: Feeling wronged, men leave their wives or sisters.

Title: Men turn into birds.
Summary: In the community of the first ancestors, young men or boys turn into birds or bats and fly away.

Title: Disappearance of women.
Summary: The women of the community of the first ancestors kill or abandon the men.

Title: Women kill men.
Summary: In the community of the first ancestors, women kill, attempt to kill, or transform men.

Title: Women hide underground.
Summary: Leaving the men, the women of the community of the first ancestors hide in a hole underground.

Title: Husbands of women - animals.
Summary: The husbands of the first women, Amazons or single women are small animals - usually flying foxes.

Title: Quarrel between men and women.
Summary: In the community of the first ancestors, women and men quarrel, leave, kill, maim each other, etc.

Title: Amazons.
Summary: There are or were settlements where only women lived or live (cf. motifs F8, F45C).

Title: Intentional conception by the wind.
Summary: A woman or female animal conceives by deliberately exposing her genitals to the wind.

Title: Accidental conception by the wind.
Summary: A woman, against her will, conceives from the wind.

Title: Conception by the sun.
Summary: A woman gives birth to a son conceived by (the rays or light of) the sun.

Title: Men without wives.
Summary: There were men who lived separately from women. See also motif F8.

Title: One for all.
Summary: At the beginning of time, two or more men (human-animals) had only one woman.

Title: Woman in a tree.
Summary: Men (human-animals) discover a woman at the top of a tree and copulate with her there.

Title: People made of pieces of flesh.
Summary: Pieces of a creature cut into many parts or a lump of living flesh are scattered or dispersed. After that, people emerge from them. Cf. motifs E38A and K98.

Title: Parts of the female body.
Summary: Men use each part of the body of a single woman for copulation, or each man takes a part of her body cut into pieces.

Title: New people in the same place.
Summary: In order to create new people (new women) to replace those who have been destroyed, the character leaves something (feathers or pieces of flesh) in each empty hut (in the hearth, in the hammock, in the village), from which new people (new women) appear.

Title: Why women are different.
Summary: Individual women differ physically because the pieces of flesh divided from the first woman were not identical, or because the males who copulated with the first woman were animals of different species.

Title: Caesarean section, T584.
Summary: Women had their stomachs cut open to remove the baby. Someone explains how to give birth or makes childbirth possible.

Title: An animal teaches how to give birth.
Summary: A small animal (mouse, rat, rabbit, two-wombed animal, bird) explains how to give birth. See motif F49.

Title: In a distant land, they do not know how to give birth.
Summary: The hero comes to a people whose women do not know how to give birth. See motif F49.

Title: The first humans do not know how to give birth.
Summary: In the beginning of time, women do not know how to give birth. See motif F49.

Title: Children born multiple times.
Summary: Children have the ability to leave their mother's womb and return to it again.

Title: Secret lover, H58.
Summary: Someone under cover of night/incognito approaches a person of the opposite sex. The marriage partner deliberately (to determine who it is) or accidentally (thereby exposing the visitor) makes a mark on his/her body (clothing). See motif A31.

Title: Aggressive sister.
Summary: After incest is discovered, the sister openly demands her brother as her husband, turns into a monster, and kills people.

Title: Finds by the thread.
Summary: To find out the nature or location of a character's locus, another person secretly attaches a long thread to it and follows it.

Title: Provocative behaviour after incest.
Summary: Upon learning that her unknown lover is her own brother, the girl shows him her genitals or bare breasts, offering him what he so desired. After that, she runs away, and he rushes after her.

Title: Ginseng child.
Summary: Ginseng roots – boys or girls who help the hero.

Title: Bird's crest made of pubic hair.
Summary: The first ancestor bird puts pubic hair or part of a woman's genitals on its head; since then, birds of this species have had a crest.

Title: The ugly husband.
Summary: An unattractive man marries, but hides his face. When he is seen, the marriage is dissolved.

Title: The Bat or Owl hides its face.
Summary: The husband hides his face from his wife because she does not know that he is a bat or an owl.

Title: Oedipus, ATU 931, 933.
Summary: Unaware of this, the son and mother (Konkani: daughter and father) engage in sexual relations and later learn of the incest they have committed. Cf. motifs c8c, f54e.

Title: The invisible scar (the husband turns out to be the son).
Summary: In her husband's appearance, the woman discovers signs that are not immediately noticeable, indicating that he has hidden his true nature from her and is not the right marriage partner (he is an animal, or her son, brother or father); or the husband discovers in the same way that his wife is his sister.

Title: Stuck feathers.
Summary: A young man or boy copulates with his mother or sister. This becomes known from the remains of paint or feathers with which he was covered during sexual intercourse.

Title: Recognised by nail marks.
Summary: A husband sees someone's fingernail marks on his wife's body and gathers the men to find out who left the marks.

Title: Conceives after drinking urine.
Summary: A woman gives birth to a boy after accidentally drinking animal urine, or a female animal gives birth to a boy after drinking a man's urine.

Title: Unintentional killing of a father.
Summary: Not knowing who is in front of him, a young man kills his father.

Title: What do you want?
Summary: Not understanding what her interlocutor of the opposite sex wants, a woman or girl names or shows various objects and body parts. The interlocutor is satisfied when she names or exposes her genitals. Cf. motif f55a.

Title: Placing on the naked body (demon and woman).
Summary: A demonic character persuades a woman to expose a certain part of her body, because that is the only place where a certain object should be placed. The demon kills the woman, tearing off that part of her body. Usually, the woman uses or names various locations, and the character rejects each one in turn until he finds the right one.

Title: Temptation and incest.
Summary: Upon seeing the vagina of his mother, daughter, daughter-in-law, sister, niece, or mother-in-law, a man or boy thinks about incest or commits it.

Title: Shavings in the fire.
Summary: To see a woman's genitals, a man throws something that flashes brightly into the hearth. The woman recoils, exposing her genitals.

Title: Persephone picks a flower.
Summary: A girl or her father (rarely: mother) picks a plant (usually a flower) and as a result encounters a character with a non-human appearance and/or inhabiting the underworld. The girl becomes the character's wife. In some cases, the picked plant is the character's hair, but more often there is no direct association of this kind.

Title: The trickster and women.
Summary: The character spends the night with a group of women, concealing his nature and/or intentions. In the end, he is either identified and punished, or he slips away to continue his mischief.

Title: Man in woman: modelling the figure.
Summary: Pretending to be a woman, the trickster transforms part of his body, another character, or some object into a swaddled baby, female genitalia, or a female household item, or disguises an animal or object as a baby born to a new husband.

Title: The trickster heals the girl.
Summary: A girl or woman falls ill. A character comes to heal her. The treatment consists of him copulating with her or attempting to do so.

Title: A woman carries a trickster.
Summary: A male character pretends to be sick, weak, unconscious; a woman carries him on her back, he copulates or tries to copulate with her on the go.

Title: Incognito at a festival.
Summary: A (supposedly) sick (weak, unattractive, poorly dressed) character is left alone when others leave for the festival; he (she) arrives there later in the guise of a handsome man or beautiful woman; those who arrived earlier do not recognise him (her) and take an interest in him (her). (This motif is also found in texts containing the motif k57, Cinderella).

Title: Man marries, K1321.1, ATU 1538*.
Summary: A male trickster transforms into a woman and gets married. In the end, he is exposed or runs away from his husband.

Title: Incestuous parent, T411.1.1.
Summary: The character is presented as another person in order to mate with a close relative in the descending or (less commonly) ascending line.

Title: Describes the future spouse.
Summary: Leaving or pretending to be dying, the character gives instructions to a relative regarding what he or she should do to get married, indicating a partner with certain characteristics, or the character indicates the place of a future meeting with this partner; or (Philippines) describes a person who should be accepted as a guest; comes himself under the guise of the person mentioned. See motif F64.

Title: Incestuous woman.
Summary: A woman pretends to be someone else in order to seduce her son, brother, daughter or grandson. See motif F64.

Title: The imaginary dead man.
Summary: To satisfy their secret desire, which involves breaking social norms (forbidden sex, refusing to share food with relatives), the character pretends to be dying, abandoned at the burial site.

Title: The Imaginary Dead Man: Meeting with a Lover, ATU 885A.
Summary: The spouse leaves the character at the burial site; the (pretend) dead person comes back to life and leaves to be with their lover.

Title: The imaginary dead man: eats alone, K1867.
Summary: The character fakes death in order to eat greedily alone.

Title: The imaginary dead man: the boy reveals the deception.
Summary: A man pretends to be dead (in order to marry his daughter or to be able to eat the meat of hunted animals alone). One of his younger children recognises their (adoptive) father or notices that the supposed dead man is alive (he runs away from the funeral pyre, laughs, etc.).

Title: The fake dead man: the wife doesn't believe it.
Summary: The character pretends to be dying and is left at the burial site. However, his wife (mother, aunt) finds out about the deception and provokes the supposed dead man, forcing him to reveal himself.

Title: False house.
Summary: In order to commit incest with his daughter, grandmother, sister (brother), father, grandson, brother (sister), the man pretends to be a stranger, or the husband takes on the appearance of his wife's brother so that she treats him as a blood relative. To do this, the character secretly moves to another house for a while, where the object of his desire mistakes him for someone else.

Title: An old woman pretends to be a man.
Summary: An old woman lives with her (adopted) daughter, niece or daughter-in-law. She (supposedly) turns into a man, marries a girl or tries to do so.

Title: The supposed dead woman dresses up as a man.
Summary: A woman pretends to be dead or actually dies. Her (former) lover comes to her grave. She goes with him, trying to avoid exposure, puts on men's clothes, but is eventually recognised.

Title: Indecent invitation.
Summary: A woman's husband (male relative) invites her through her children to come and make love to him; the invitation is made in a veiled form; the woman comes.

Title: Potiphar's Wife, K2111, T418, ATU 318.
Summary: A woman falsely accuses a man of assaulting her.

Title: Scratches his body.
Summary: Accusing a man or young man of assaulting her (usually sexually), a woman presents fabricated material evidence (tearing her clothes, scratching her body, etc.). See motif F70.

Title: Revenge of the rejected.
Summary: A woman takes revenge on a man who rejected her love (but does not necessarily pretend that the man tried to force himself on her).

Title: The castrated becomes a man (ATU 318).
Summary: A young man loses his male organ, but restores it with magic (and marries happily). Cf. ATU 750K. In ATU 318, this episode is described as one of many possible ones related to the theme of the unfaithful wife.

Title: The disgraced informer.
Summary: A girl pretends to be a man or a eunuch, or a girl hides a disability, or a man pretends to be a girl. Someone reveals a secret. At the last moment, the hero or heroine magically gets rid of the disability (acquires male or female nature), the informer is disgraced (executed).

Title: Girl turns into a man, ATU 514.
Summary: A girl pretends to be a man, magically acquires male nature and lives with his wife. Cf. motif K137 (in Uther 2004, plot 514 mistakenly includes a Karakalpak text with our motif K137).

Title: Daughter in the role of son, AT 884B.
Summary: An old man needs a son to do men's work. (Only the youngest) daughter takes on this task (successfully passing the test set by her father), pretending to be a man.

Title: Father tests his daughters or sons.
Summary: The father sends his daughters or sons on a difficult task one by one. At the very beginning of the journey, their courage is put to the test. Only the youngest son or daughter passes the test. Usually, the father stands in their way, taking the form of an enemy or a predator, but only the youngest son or daughter bravely enters the fight.

Title: Accidental change of gender.
Summary: Finding themselves in a deserted place, people accidentally change their gender.

Title: Susanna and the Elders, ATU 883A.
Summary: After being rejected, the man falsely accuses the woman of promiscuity; others believe him and try to punish her severely.

Title: Imitation of rape.
Summary: A woman asks a man to tie her up before intercourse so that it looks like she is being raped.

Title: Imaginary wound.
Summary: The character mistakes the vulva or anus for a wound. See motifs F73A, F73B. (In the traditions of South and Central America, it is impossible to distinguish local variants from European borrowings).

Title: The vulva as a wound (first humans).
