Summary: A young man comes to an old man (less often – to an old woman), who teaches him how to get a magical wife by hiding her bird clothes. Usually, the young man gives away the clothes for the first time and lives with the old man until the girls fly back.

Title: The magical wife.
Summary: A man consciously marries a woman who belongs to the non-human world.

Title: Found clothing.
Summary: A magical wife leaves her earthly husband when she finds her clothes, which he has hidden (often feathers, if she is a bird woman), persuades him to give them back, makes new ones or receives them from her relatives. (The variant in which the wife leaves her husband because she is offended is not entirely alternative, but in most texts it does not fit with the motif of found clothing).

Title: Discarded feathers.
Summary: An anthropomorphic character flies away or tries to fly away, attaching feathers shed by birds flying in the sky to his body.

Title: Collected feathers.
Summary: The magical bird-wife flies away when she makes herself new feather clothing from feathers collected on the ground.

Title: Escape from the siren, ATU 316.
Summary: A man (rarely a woman) finds himself in the power of an aquatic-chthonic creature (usually a siren, fish, sea monster, sometimes a sorcerer). The captive is lifted above the water (above the ground; usually after the antagonist lifts him) several times. After that, the captive escapes (most often by flying away as a bird).

Title: Rescue from the underwater world (broken chain).
Summary: A young woman finds herself in the power of a water creature, and when she comes ashore, she is chained. To free the woman, the chain must be broken.

Title: Two brothers and bird maidens.
Summary: The older brother is a hunter, the younger brother (rarely a sister) is a housekeeper. Learning that bird maidens come down to the younger brother, the older brother teaches the younger brother what he must do so that the older brother can catch one of them and make her his wife. The wife finds feather clothing and flies away (often the younger brother, out of simplicity, gives it to her), and the husband sets off in search of her.

Title: The magical wife does not forgive infidelity.
Summary: A woman from another world agrees to live with a man in his earthly world, but leaves him when she learns that he has broken a taboo (often his infidelity). Cf. motif F94 (the hero betrays his magical wife in her world); motif K12B (the hero visits his world alone, contrary to the warning of his magical wife).

Title: Two brothers and a winged maiden.
Summary: The older brother hunts, the younger brother takes care of the household. After catching the winged maiden, the older brother takes her as his wife, while the younger brother, out of naivety, returns her wings to her. The older brother sets off in search of his wife.

Title: A woman follows a porcupine.
Summary: A woman climbs a tree trying to catch a porcupine and ends up in the sky.

Title: The boy under the onion.
Summary: While digging roots, gathering shellfish, etc., a woman finds a baby. He grows up and enters into a struggle with dangerous characters.

Title: The forbidden tuber in the heavens.
Summary: After digging up the root, a person pierces the sky or the earth, sees the world below, and descends there. Usually, the hole is made by a woman who has fallen into the sky; her husband, a sky dweller, or his relatives forbid her to dig up a certain root; breaking the ban, the woman sees the earth below and decides to descend. See motif K19B.

Title: The magical wife – ancestor of humans.
Summary: Humans in general or a specific ethnic, tribal or social group are considered descendants of an earthly man and woman of supernatural origin.

Title: The earth seen from the sky.
Summary: Approaching an opening or making one, the character sees the world below (usually seeing the earth from the sky). See motif K25.

Title: A stone covers the opening.
Summary: The hole in the sky is covered by a flat stone. Moving it aside, the character sees the earth. See motif K26.

Title: Tasks and competitions.
Summary: The character receives tasks that are deadly dangerous or can only be accomplished with supernatural abilities or helpers; the hero completes the tasks and/or miraculously survives. The confrontation between the characters unfolds as a game or competition in which the loser loses their life or status.

Title: Night in the cold.
Summary: Test: spend the night in the cold (the antagonist tries to destroy the hero in this way). See motif K27. Compare motif M35: two zoomorphic characters compete to see which of them will sit out the night in the cold.

Title: Smoking a pipe.
Summary: Test: smoke a huge or poisonous pipe or breathe in clouds of poisonous smoke. See motif K27.

Title: Knives and spikes.
Summary: Test: to remain alive when coming into contact with piercing, cutting, or crushing instruments. See motif K27.

Title: House with dangerous creatures.
Summary: The test: to stay alive in a room full of predatory, poisonous and other dangerous creatures. See motif K27.

Title: Eat or drink a lot, ATU 1088).
Summary: The character is offered to eat or drink an unusually large amount or poison.

Title: To obtain a woman.
Summary: An authoritative character demands that the hero obtain a woman.

Title: Building a bridge.
Summary: A character builds a bridge (usually from precious materials) in an implausibly short time.

Title: Get the same shoes.
Summary: A girl demands that her fiancé get her the same pair of shoes (or other items) as hers. These items either exist in a single copy, or it is not known what they look like. Having become invisible, the hero either steals the items (and the owner has to make new ones herself), or finds out what they look like.

Title: Fill the feather bed with feathers.
Summary: The character must quickly obtain enough feathers to fill a feather bed or pillow.

Title: Build a house.
Summary: Task: to erect a building. See motif K27.

Title: To bathe in boiling water.
Summary: The character is ordered to bathe in (hot) milk, in boiling water, to jump into the fire; he remains unharmed, while his opponent usually perishes.

Title: Task: clean out the stable.
Summary: The character must quickly clean the stable or barn of the manure that has accumulated there over a long period of time.

Title: Roof made of feathers.
Summary: The character must build a house out of bird feathers or cover the roof, bridge, etc. with feathers.

Title: One falls – all fall.
Summary: To fell all the trees in the forest, a man fells one (lightly touching it with an axe), after which all the trees fall.

Title: Sow, reap and bake bread in one day.
Summary: The character must complete all field work in an unimaginably short time and present the products of the new harvest.

Title: Wooden axe.
Summary: A person tries or must try to chop or dig with a wooden (lead, felt) tool instead of a steel one. Cf. motif L84.

Title: Depict a head that is not shown.
Summary: The hero must carve an image of the character's head, which he never shows. It usually adorns a wooden bench.

Title: Bringing fruit.
Summary: The character is tasked with bringing the fruits of a tree that is difficult to reach.

Title: Sorting grain, Th H1091.
Summary: The character is tasked with quickly separating small particles of different types (usually seeds of different plant species) mixed together in a single vessel, or counting the number of grains, or gathering scattered or already sown grain.

Title: Drain a body of water.
Summary: Task: to drain a large body of water.

Title: Dive long or deep.
Summary: Test: to dive underwater for a long time or deeply. See motif K27.

Title: The water body is covered with ice.
Summary: After the hero dives in, the antagonist freezes the water body or covers the surface with a net.

Title: Frozen in ice.
Summary: Voluntarily subjecting himself to trials, the character allows himself to be frozen in ice and cannot free himself.

Title: Obtain an animal of unusual colour.
Summary: Task: to kill and bring an animal of a certain (often unusual) colour or shape. See motif K27.

Title: Tasks of relatives, H310, H331.
Summary: A young man must complete difficult tasks or win a competition in order to obtain permission to marry. The person giving the tasks is indicated in square brackets. See motif K27.

Title: The one who gives tasks – a king or a chief.
Summary: A character who gives the hero tasks that are impossible for an ordinary person (subjecting the hero to difficult trials), or a character who requires the suitors of his daughter to fulfil certain conditions, is the head of a community or supra-community collective and is neither a member of the same family collective as the hero nor a mythical creature. See motif K27.

Title: The task giver – a mythical character.
Summary: The character who gives the hero difficult tasks or subjects him to trials is a mythical creature or animal. See motif K27.

Title: The task giver – the Sun, Moon, Thunder or Wind.
Summary: The character who gives the hero difficult tasks or subjects him to trials is associated with the sun, moon, thunder or wind (cloud, downpour). See motif K27.

Title: The hero in battle with the elements.
Summary: In the course of his courtship, the hero enters into a struggle with characters (more than two) who embody the elements, celestial bodies, and parts of the universe.

Title: The one who gives tasks dwells in the sky.
Summary: The character who gives the hero or heroine difficult tasks or subjects them to trials lives in the sky, but is not associated with the sun, moon, thunder or wind. See motif K27.

Title: The one who gives tasks – a zoomorphic creature.
Summary: A character who gives the hero difficult tasks or subjects him to trials is associated with a land or water animal or a fish. See motif K27.

Title: The hero's adversaries – polar bears.
Summary: The inhabitants of the polar bear village – relatives of his wife – set the hero difficult tasks and trials.

Title: The enemy – the father-in-law bear.
Summary: The hero's father-in-law, the bear, sets him difficult tasks and trials.

Title: The Envious Vizier.
Summary: Someone from the entourage of a powerful figure seeks to destroy the hero and persuades others to give him difficult tasks.

Title: Ball game.
Summary: The confrontation between heroes and antagonists unfolds in the form of a ball game.

Title: Ball – human head.
Summary: Severed human heads are compared to balls. Either a character plays with a severed human head or skull as a ball.

Title: Playing with a dangerous ball.
Summary: To destroy the hero, his opponents play ball with him, throwing a heavy dangerous object (a ball made of ice, bone, stone, iron, a walrus head, a biting skull, etc.).

Title: Competition between two teams.
Summary: Two groups of characters compete in overcoming trials or play a game, divided into two teams (at least two episodes with different characters on both sides). The participants are either anthropomorphic but possess different unusual abilities, or they are different animals (natural phenomena, elements, etc.). Cf. motif K27xy (Characters with different properties in opposing camps).

Title: The antagonist mourns his assistants.
Summary: The antagonist sends the hero to places where he is attacked by dangerous creatures; the hero kills them and brings them to the antagonist. The creatures turn out to be relatives, pupils or helpers of the antagonist, whom he (or his close relatives) mourns or revives. See motif K27.

Title: The enemy father-in-law takes the form of an animal.
Summary: The father-in-law (less often the mother-in-law) orders the hero to kill or tame a dangerous animal or not to kill a certain animal while hunting. This animal is himself or his daughter (wife).

Title: The enemy father-in-law takes the form of a bear.
Summary: Demanding that the hero kill the bear, the father-in-law (rarely: mother-in-law) himself takes on the form of a bear or turns his daughter or wife (husband) into a bear (bear).

Title: Milk of a wild animal.
Summary: Task: to obtain the milk of a wild animal or milk possessed by a dangerous creature. See motif K27.

Title: Lioness's milk in a lion cub's skin.
Summary: The hero is sent to bring lioness milk in a wineskin made from a lion skin (usually from a lion cub's skin).

Title: Gusli-samogudy.
Summary: The hero is sent to obtain a musical instrument, usually a gusli-samogudy.

Title: Passing away.
Summary: The person giving the task requires an item or message to be brought from the world.

Title: The supposed burnt.
Summary: The antagonist believes that the hero was burned, but returned safely from the afterlife, so he orders himself or his representative to be burned.

Title: Dancing apples.
Summary: Task: bring objects (fruit, wood, water, etc.) that perform actions characteristic of humans (sing, dance, yawn, laugh, etc.).

Title: Running, racing.
Summary: Competition: running, racing. See motif K27.

Title: Overtake (an old) woman.
Summary: A strong man must overtake a woman, often an old woman. This is difficult or impossible to achieve.

Title: Competition: climbing a pole.
Summary: Competition: climbing a pole. See motif K27.

Title: Hide, ATU 329.
Summary: Task: to hide (the hero finds the antagonist, and/or the antagonist cannot find the hero). See motif K27.

Title: From conception to birth day.
Summary: Some people demand that the child be born the morning after conception or speak immediately after birth.

Title: News from the tumbleweed.
Summary: An authoritative character orders to find out where the tumbleweed is rolling or what news it brings.

Title: Shooting a bird.
Summary: The character must hit the bird with an arrow or a stone. (Cf. motif K27M, where it is not the accuracy of the archer that is important, but the unusual appearance of the creature that needs to be caught).

Title: To hit a needle with an arrow.
Summary: The character must hit the eye of a needle with an arrow (the eye of a needle).

Title: To hit a copper object with an arrow.
Summary: The character must hit an object or creature made of copper with an arrow.

Title: Shooting an arrow through a ring.
Summary: The character must hit a small ring with an arrow or shoot it through several rings. (The main materials were identified by Y.V. Vasilkov and presented in Vasilkov 2018).

Title: The monster kills the person giving the tasks.
Summary: The task giver demands that a dangerous creature be brought to him or that something belonging to a monster or deity be brought to him. The hero fulfils the task, but the beast, monster, deity or the object itself kills the task giver. See motif K27.

Title: The former husband of a magical wife.
Summary: A man marries a woman from another world; the wife leaves for her world, the man follows her; there, the woman has another fiancé(e) or husband, or the woman's brothers want to destroy the man; he undergoes trials and brings his wife back. See motif K27.

Title: The invisible servant ("Bring me that, I don't know what"), (ATU 465A).
Summary: Having received a difficult task (usually: to bring an object or creature that has no specific characteristics, such as "something, I don't know what," "a strange wonder," etc.), the hero meets an invisible man who serves others; he is kind to him, and the man becomes his assistant. (This motif is certainly present in some texts of the ATU 465A plot, but it is not specifically highlighted in the definition). (Cf. motif K131B).

Title: Getting an egg from under a bird, ATU 1525H 1 .
Summary: The character is able to get an egg or chick (and put them back) from under a bird in a nest, or change the bird's feathers (pluck feathers), or get a fruit from an animal's womb so that the bird or animal does not notice.

Title: The king and the hero's wife, ATU 465.
Summary: The ruler seeks to take possession of the wife or bride of a man of lower social status and, in order to get rid of him, gives him impossible tasks or secretly kills him. {Both ATU and some regional indexes (e.g., Cardigos 2006: 110) list texts that do not meet the definition of plot 465: the king's desire to take possession of the hero's wife is not explicitly stated as the reason why the king seeks to get rid of the hero}.

Title: Recognise by the scarf.
Summary: When a husband sets off on a difficult mission, his magical wife gives him her towel or scarf, instructing him to use only those items (usually so that her relatives will recognise him as their son-in-law).

Title: Not spilling water, climbing a tree.
Summary: The character is told to climb a tree (pole, mountain, etc.) while holding a full open vessel in his hand and not spilling a drop from it.

Title: Helpers of different ages.
Summary: When setting out in search of a woman or miraculous objects, a person consistently encounters characters of a non-human (often demonic) nature who help him. The characters are similar, but usually each subsequent one is older (younger) than the other.

Title: The stars and the wind guide the hero.
Summary: Setting out in search of a marriage partner, the hero or heroine successively encounters the embodiments (masters) of celestial bodies and atmospheric phenomena (the sun, moon, stars, wind).

Title: The character encounters the mother of the sun.
Summary: The character comes to the mother of the Sun when the Sun itself is not there. Cf. motif b33h ("Mother of the Sun").

Title: Greeting addressed to the wind, ATU 298A*.
Summary: Upon encountering the sun, moon (frost) and wind, a person greets only the latter. (In progress)

Title: The lord of the animals summons them and questions them.
Summary: On the way to their destination, people meet characters who have power over animals (birds, fish) or demons. They summon the animals (demons) and ask if anyone knows the way to a certain place. Only one person knows, usually the last to appear.

Title: The guiding frog.
Summary: Only the frog (toad) knows the way to the object that is unattainable for ordinary people, which the hero is looking for (and helps him get there).

Title: Retrieving an object from the bottom of the sea.
Summary: The hero must retrieve a small object (often a ring or signet ring) thrown into deep water (often the sea). Cf. motif C6 ("The Diver").

Title: Characters with different properties in the enemy camp.
Summary: Several men (animals), each of whom can do something better than the others, work together to accomplish difficult tasks set before them by their opponents. The competition is not intended to find a worthy suitor for a girl or to get rid of an unwanted suitor. Cf. motif K27o3 (Competition between two teams).

Title: Obtaining material for arrows.
Summary: The hero is sent or, knowing the danger, goes himself to obtain various (at least two) materials for making a bow and arrows (shafts, feathers, bowstring, flint for arrowheads, paint for colouring arrows, resin and fibres for attaching the arrowhead or feather to the shaft, etc.). See motif K27.

Title: Coal arrowheads.
Summary: The character believes or pretends that arrowheads should be made of bark, coal, grass, and similar materials.

Title: Approach a dangerous tree.
Summary: The hero is sent to a tree that is supposed to fall on him.

Title: Obtain the feather of a dangerous bird.
Summary: The hero brings the feather (feathers) of a dangerous bird.

Title: Catching the chick of a dangerous bird.
Summary: The hero is sent to bring the chick of a dangerous bird.

Title: Obtaining the fruits of a dangerous tree.
Summary: The hero must bring the fruits growing on a tree that is dangerous to approach.

Title: Obtaining tree bark.
Summary: The hero must obtain tree bark, which is fraught with danger.

Title: Gambling for life and death.
Summary: A character gains power over another by winning a game of chance or an intellectual game (not a sporting competition). The motif includes all texts with motif K27z4.

Title: Don't take the cage, don't take the bridle! ATU 550.
Summary: The assistant teaches how to steal the desired object, but not to take anything else (take the bird, but not the cage, the horse, but not the bridle, etc.). The character takes what he should not, is caught, released on the promise to deliver another object, then the girl. In the end, the hero keeps both the girl and everything he stole. {ATU 550 includes a much wider range of texts; in particular, the Indian, Burmese and Persian variants mentioned in Uther 2004 do not correspond to our definition}.

Title: Separated from her son, she avoided incest, ATU 674.
Summary: A noble woman is forced to leave her home, gives birth to a son, and is separated from him. The young man grows up and almost marries his mother, but at the last moment everything is explained. {The Sudanese text, attributed to this plot in el-Shamy 2004 and subsequently in Uther 2004, does not fit the definition; it is quite possible that the Latvians, Romanians and Ukrainians are also mentioned incorrectly in Uther 2004}.

Title: Meeting for one night.
Summary: Noticing the woman's pregnancy, her relatives or in-laws accuse her of promiscuity, because, according to their calculations, she could not have conceived by her husband or fiancé. After severe trials, the woman meets again the father of the boy she gave birth to.

Title: An innocent woman is accused of promiscuity.
Summary: Noticing that a woman is pregnant, her relatives or in-laws accuse her of promiscuity, because, according to their calculations, she could not have conceived by her husband or fiancé. After severe trials, the woman meets again the father of the boy she gave birth to.

Title: The unrecognised wife visits her husband, ATU 891.
Summary: The husband leaves his wife without agreeing with her. The wife visits her husband incognito, and in the end he realises who is with him. Usually, the wife spends the night with her husband, gives birth to a son (three children), and the husband is convinced that the son is his.

Title: The Murdered Doll, ATU 879.
Summary: The complicated relationship between a simple girl and a prince leads to the prince intending to kill his bride on their wedding night. The girl substitutes a doll for herself, the prince stabs the doll with his sword, mistakes the spurting juice (syrup, honey) for blood, and repents of the murder. The real girl appears, and the young couple are happy.

Title: Marries to lock up his wife.
Summary: After marrying a poor girl, the prince locks her up. She turns out to be more cunning than him.

Title: The sparrow's quarrel with her husband.
Summary: A conflict arises between a pair of birds (sparrows, pigeons, etc.), in which the male is more likely (and more often clearly) to be at fault. This episode serves as the starting point for a story about the relationships between people of noble origin.

Title: Lost objects and meeting at the end, ATU 434.
Summary: During a meeting (sometimes not in their true form), a young man or woman takes certain objects (jewelry) from the other. One of those who met falls ill. A new meeting leads to the healing of the sick person, the identification of the objects, and a wedding.

Title: The Biting Doll, ATU 571C.
Summary: A poor girl buys a doll (goose) that defecates gold. When the neighbours take the doll, it only dirties their house. They throw it away, and the prince uses it to wipe himself, and it sticks to his backside. No one can help, but the poor girl easily solves the problem. The prince marries her.

Title: The Cat with the Lamp, ATU 217.
Summary: The character taught the cat (monkey, dog) to hold a candle (lamp) or to extinguish it on command. Seeing a mouse (rat), the cat rushes after it and as a result drops (does not extinguish) the candle.

Title: The dice player's trained animal.
Summary: The character always wins bets or outplays others thanks to a trained cat (mouse, rat) that holds (or extinguishes in time) a lamp, turns dice, etc. The hero releases the mouse (or cat, mongoose, respectively), the cat rushes after it (or the mouse is afraid to come out), and the character loses.

Title: The cripple demands the return of his leg, ATU 978.
Summary: The cripple claims that the father of the visitor is to blame for his physical disability. The man's wife or the man himself, on someone's advice, promises to return the leg (eye) if the cripple gives him the other one as a sample or brings him a part of a dead person's body and demands money.

Title: Dressed as a man, the wife rescues her husband.
Summary: The husband leaves, meets a swindler and loses everything he has to him. The wife comes disguised as a man, punishes the swindler and rescues her husband.

Title: Agreement to marry children, (926C*).
Summary: Two men agree to marry their children if one has a son and the other has a daughter. The girl's parents do not fulfil the agreement. The boy grows up and finds his betrothed.

Title: The Stone of Patience, ATU 894.
Summary: Having fallen victim to injustice and endured suffering, a young woman tells her story to certain inanimate objects (often a "stone of patience"), or her husband tells the story after learning of his wife's fate. The woman is saved, justice is restored.

Title: To learn what the rose of the heart is.
Summary: The character promises to fulfil a request if the other person reveals the secret behind someone's strange behaviour.

Title: He who learns the family secret will die.
Summary: A man is going to kill the person who found out why he severely punished his ex-wife.

Title: Riddles that cannot be solved, ATU 851, 927.
Summary: A person poses a riddle that can only be solved by knowing the circumstances in which he found himself.

Title: Why the fish smiled (ATU 875D).
Summary: (Dried) fish (water, satyr, etc.) laughs, smiles or spits. The reason is that there is a man dressed as a woman in the house.

Title: The hero between two cannibals.
Summary: A young man (woman) lives in the house of a cannibal (witch). In order to destroy him or her, the cannibal orders that a certain object be brought from other cannibals (often from his or her mother or sister). The hero or heroine escapes (and destroys all the cannibals).

Title: The Cannibal and the Blinded Wives, ATU 462.
Summary: A man does not suspect that his (new) wife (less often his mother) is a cannibal/witch/treacherous woman; she persecutes (former) wives (his wife) and/or blinds them or throws them into a pit, or her husband does so at her instigation. Contrary to the cannibal's plans, the son of one of the wives survives, kills the cannibal, and rescues his mother and sisters.

Title: Preserving her child.
Summary: Several wives are thrown into a dungeon (banished), each gives birth to a child, but only one manages to save hers. The boy grows up and rescues the women.

Title: Blind in one eye.
Summary: Several wives of one man (several sisters) go blind – the older ones in both eyes, and the younger one in one eye.

Title: The pit by the apple tree.
Summary: The father or stepmother (werewolf) pushes/locks the sisters (the girl and her servants) into a pit. The heroine manages to escape and triumphs over her antagonists.

Title: The wife who cannot be beaten (ATU 888A).
Summary: A conceited prince (the son of a merchant) beats his wife every day (he marries on the condition that he will beat his wife every day). She saves him by demonstrating her superiority.

Title: Father or uncle – enemy and rival.
Summary: The uncle on the mother's side or the father of the young hero (or grandfather, if he replaces the father, who is not mentioned) is his enemy and rival, giving him difficult tasks with the aim of destroying him.

Title: Unharmed by fire.
Summary: The hero demonstrates his magical abilities or cunning by remaining alive in a hot bath, oven, fire, or among burning vegetation.

Title: Safe in the pit, K959,6.
Summary: The hero is asked to climb (or is thrown) into a pit, which is immediately filled with earth or into which a pole or stones are lowered, K959,6 (Posthole murder). The hero proves his magical abilities by climbing out of the pit alive.

Title: Brings a tree.
Summary: They hope to kill the hero by knocking a tree down on him or tying him to a tree. He comes back alive, dragging the tree behind him.

Title: Drunken elephants.
Summary: To catch an animal or supernatural character, the water in a reservoir is replaced with wine, honey, etc., or containers with alcohol are left in plain sight. The creature, having lost control of itself, is captured.

Title: The flying enemy carries off the woman.
Summary: A flying creature carries a woman away. The kidnapper is killed and/or the woman escapes from him. See also motif L102A (Escape from a seagull husband).

Title: The chief's wife and the vultures.
Summary: The wife of the first ancestor flies away with the vultures (usually voluntarily, after she has already cheated on her husband), and the chief (Uito: her brother) brings her back. See motif K30.

Title: Went out for a walk and disappeared.
Summary: A woman or girl is forbidden to go outside. As soon as she does, a flying creature kidnaps her.

Title: Wooden seal.
Summary: The character makes a marine mammal or fish out of wood. It kills his enemies or drags them out to the open sea.

Title: The Substituted Woman, K1911; ATU 403, 404.
Summary: The man does not (immediately) notice that another woman, an evil spirit or (in Chaco) a male trickster has replaced his wife or bride, who is banished, imprisoned in the underworld, killed, etc.

Title: A man leaves on a journey.
Summary: A man is carrying his wife or daughter. Another woman or demonic character replaces her when the man leaves on a journey (rarely: falls asleep).

Title: Mother-in-law replaces daughter-in-law.
Summary: The man's mother takes on the appearance of his wife in order to take her place.

Title: Mother replaces daughter.
Summary: The man's mother-in-law takes on the appearance of her daughter to take her place. See motif K32.

Title: The real wife becomes an owl.
Summary: The deceiver takes the place of the real wife, and the real wife becomes an owl. See motif K32.

Title: The replaced one grazes cattle.
Summary: As a result of the antagonist's intrigues, a noble girl (young woman) or boy (young man) is turned into a servant or servant, sent to graze cattle or chase birds in the field. Everything is revealed – usually after people hear a song in which the hero or heroine tells about the substitution. Most often, the hero or heroine goes to relatives or (less often) to the groom. The deceiver accompanies her or him and is accepted as a relative or bride. The deceiver is executed. Comoros: the deceiver becomes the mistress, turning the girl's parents into peacocks.

Title: Gold, silver, wood.
Summary: A negative character, object or locus is contrasted with one or two positive ones, such as wood with gold and silver.

Title: The bird son saves his mother.
Summary: A woman or girl raises a bird of prey chick, which brings her food and fire. This usually happens after an evil spirit leaves the girl or young woman in a tree or on an island.

Title: Torn apart by horses.
Summary: The antagonist is executed by being tied to a horse (camel, bull), which drags him along the ground or tears him to pieces.

Title: Forty horses or forty knives?
Summary: The guilty party is offered a choice of items of utilitarian value (often forty, seven, three, etc. horses or the same number of knives). The person usually does not understand that these are methods of execution.

Title: The daughter's meat is sent to her mother.
Summary: An authoritative character marries, and an evil woman replaces her with her daughter. After the false wife is exposed and executed, the woman receives cooked meat as a gift, not immediately realising that it is her daughter's body parts.

Title: What does the perpetrator deserve? .
Summary: The villain is asked what punishment he deserves for committing the crime in question. Not knowing that they are talking about him, he decides for himself how he should be executed.

Title: Buried alive.
Summary: The antagonist is executed by being buried alive.

Title: Placed in a barrel with nails.
Summary: The antagonist is executed by being placed in a barrel (with nails) and rolled down a hill or tied to a horse.

Title: Left to be eaten by ants.
Summary: A man executes his wife by leaving her to be eaten by ants.

Title: The antagonist is burned.
Summary: The antagonist is executed by being burned alive. (Episodes in which the burning of the character is not a punishment but a means of getting rid of him are not taken into account).

Title: Two nurses beside a sleeping man, ATU 894.
Summary: A girl finds the body of a young man who shows no signs of life and must sit next to him for a certain amount of time so that he comes back to life and takes her as his wife. Usually, she leaves at the last moment and an impostor becomes the wife of the revived man.

Title: The brother of the changeling is accused of deception (ATU 403).
Summary: Upon learning from a young man that he has a beautiful sister, the ruler wants to marry her. The bride is replaced by an ugly woman. Usually, the ruler accuses her brother of deception and throws him into prison. The deception is revealed.

Title: False wife – beetle or larva.
Summary: The false wife, replacing the real one – a foul-smelling beetle or larva.

Title: Horses are given for fattening.
Summary: The ruler distributes horses (cows) to his subjects for fattening. Only the heroine returns hers well-fed.

Title: The heroine is transformed into an animal (not drowned).
Summary: To take the heroine's place, her rival turns her into an animal or bird without pushing her into the water. Cf. motif k33.

Title: The false wife - a supernatural character.
Summary: The false wife, who replaces the real one, is a supernatural character - a zoomorphic creature, a deceased woman, a female spirit, etc. See motif K32.

Title: The Living Drowned Woman, Th D688, E323.1; ATU 450.
Summary: When a malevolent woman pushes another woman into a body of water (a well), the latter drowns or loses her human form, but manages to return to the world of humans. Cf. motif k32m

Title: Brother Goat, ATU 450.
Summary: Young siblings (most often a brother and sister) leave home. One of them (rarely: several brothers) accidentally breaks a taboo and is transformed into an animal (usually a hoofed animal) or (rarely) a bird; later, the spell is usually broken.

Title: Born in a well, T581.2.0.
Summary: A woman is thrown into a well (pond, pit, etc.) or becomes a water bird. In the water, she gives birth to a child (twins, triplets) or is thrown into the water with her baby. She is rescued along with her children.

Title: Heroine in the belly of a whale.
Summary: A woman thrown into the water finds herself in the belly of a fish (whale), but is then rescued.

Title: The witch distorts what is said.
Summary: A brother takes his sister to her fiancé. She cannot hear her brother's words, and the witch distorts them (as if the brother is telling his sister to throw herself into the water, to blind her, etc.). Having got rid of the heroine, the witch replaces her with her own daughter.

Title: The heroine is turned into a turtle.
Summary: A woman, turned into a turtle because of her rival's intrigues, tries to establish contact with her children or husband.

Title: Heroine transformed into a forest animal (ATU 409).
Summary: A woman, transformed into a medium-sized forest animal (lynx, wolf, vixen) by the machinations of a rival, tries to establish contact with her children or husband.

Title: The heroine is turned into a duck.
Summary: A woman who has been turned into a duck (goose) by her rival's scheming tries to establish contact with her children or husband.

Title: Knives are sharpened, cauldrons are boiling.
Summary: A kid (lamb, gazelle, etc.) runs up to a pond into which its owner has pushed it and says that knives are being sharpened and water is being boiled to slaughter and cook it.

Title: The widower, his daughter (son) and the teacher.
Summary: After the death of a woman, her daughter or son advises her father to marry a neighbour, teacher, etc., who usually persuades the teenager to give such advice. After marrying the widower, the new wife begins to tyrannise her stepdaughter or stepson.

Title: The heroine is transformed into a dove.
Summary: A woman transformed into a dove by the machinations of a rival tries to establish contact with her children or husband.

Title: Friends abandon a beautiful woman.
Summary: A girl goes with her friends to the forest, to the river; everyone returns home, but she is forced to stay or return. She escapes from a dangerous creature, becomes the wife of a supernatural character, a leader, etc., or dies, but is avenged.

Title: Girl found inside a foetus, (ATU 408).
Summary: A young man obtains a girl who is inside a fruit or (rarely) a flower, stem, leaf, or egg.

Title: Transformation into a lotus.
Summary: A character thrown into the water is transformed into a flower (usually a lotus).

Title: Girl in a pomegranate.
Summary: A young man obtains a girl who is inside a pomegranate.

Title: The girl in the orange.
Summary: A young man obtains a girl who is inside an orange or other citrus fruit.

Title: Girl in a pumpkin.
Summary: A young man obtains a girl who is inside a pumpkin, eggplant or cucumber.

Title: Girl in an egg.
Summary: A young man obtains a girl who is inside an egg.

Title: Only one girl survived.
Summary: A young man receives several fruits (eggs, reeds). When he opens the first one, the girl who comes out of it disappears, either because the necessary provisions (usually drinking water) have not been prepared for her, or because the fruit has been cut incorrectly. Only the one who comes out of the last fruit (egg, reed) remains. Cf. motif k33c7.

Title: One fruit and a girl inside it.
Summary: A young man obtains a fruit from which a girl emerges (rarely: two girls from two fruits, both remain with the young man). There is no episode of the loss of the girls who were in the other fruits. Cf. motif k33c6.

Title: Girl in a walnut.
Summary: A young man obtains a girl who is inside a nut (walnut or hazelnut, but not coconut).

Title: The girl in the apple.
Summary: A young man obtains a girl who is inside an apple.

Title: Donkey Skin, ATU 510B.
Summary: A man discovers that a beautiful girl is hiding under the guise of an ugly hag or under the skin of an animal.

Title: Hidden in a lantern, ATU 510B*.
Summary: The young man does not know that a beautiful girl is hiding inside the object brought to his house.

Title: Chosen and returned children (Griselda), ATU 887.
Summary: Newborn children disappear (die) one after another, but are returned to their wife or husband grown up and in good health.

Title: Stream of honey and stream of oil.
Summary: Sources of at least two valuable liquid edible products (honey, oil, etc.) are available or imagined. Cf. motif N34.

Title: Source of oil according to a vow.
Summary: A person promises to create a source from which a valuable product (most often oil) flows and honestly fulfils their promise (rarely: promises to distribute a large amount of such a product).

Title: Two kinds of fruit, ATU 566.
Summary: The person who eats the fruit (leaf, etc.) grows horns (long nose, etc.) or turns into an animal, while the other fruit (leaf, etc.) returns to its normal appearance.

Title: Cat, dog and magical object, ATU 560.
Summary: A person finds a magical object that grants any wish. This object is stolen. It is returned by animals (which the hero had previously saved).

Title: Replace the old ring with a new one.
Summary: The hero's wife (mother, servant) is unaware of the magical properties of an object kept in the house and exchanges it for something more attractive, but in reality incomparable in value.

Title: Dangerous swings, K855.
Summary: The character puts others on the swing and, after swinging them, throws them (or threatens to throw them) into the water, onto rocks, etc.

Title: A rival lures a woman onto a swing.
Summary: A rival puts a woman on a swing to get rid of her by throwing her into the water. She (almost) drowns or temporarily loses her human form, but manages to return to the world of humans.

Title: The replaced man.
Summary: The deceiver pretends to be a hero in order to take his place (to possess his woman). (This motif includes all texts with motif K35a3).

Title: The hero brands his rivals, ATU 530A.
Summary: In exchange for improving his current situation, the character agrees to have his body injured or branded.

Title: Do not pick up the feather of the firebird.
Summary: Setting off on a journey, a person (often against the advice of their horse) picks up a precious feather. Upon learning of this, an authoritative character gives them difficult tasks.

Title: Beast with a glowing skin.
Summary: A man kills an animal with glowing fur. Upon learning of this, an authoritative figure gives him difficult tasks.

Title: The master becomes a servant.
Summary: In order to obtain the privileges enjoyed by the hero, the deceiver manages to swap status with him.

Title: Thrown into the sea.
Summary: In order to get rid of the hero and take his place, the deceiver pushes him into the sea or leaves him on a distant island. The hero survives and returns.

Title: A sign by which the patron recognises the visitor.
Summary: An authoritative character leaves an object (a letter) for a little boy, by which he will be able to recognise him when he grows up and comes to him.

Title: Glowing feather.
Summary: The character illuminates the room with a light-emitting object (usually a feather) that he has found.

Title: The magical feather.
Summary: A character finds a feather, the touch of which brings health and beauty.

Title: The most delicious dish.
Summary: The hero gives his rivals the food that the king sent them all to get, but what the rivals got turns out to be poisonous, useless, or tasteless, while what the hero brought, regardless of how it looks, gets praised.

Title: The Dev in the Well, ATU 677, 677*, 986.
Summary: The dev (ajdaha, sea king) did not kill the man who descended to him, as people assumed, but rewarded him because he greeted him and/or answered his question correctly.

Title: Better the one you love (ATU 677).
Summary: The young man is not killed, but rewarded, because he answered correctly (evasively) the question of a powerful character – which of the two women he should marry, which is more beautiful, which object or material is more valuable, etc.

Title: The hero in the underwater kingdom, (ATU 677).
Summary: When the ship unexpectedly stops, the hero descends to the bottom of the sea, behaves correctly with the local inhabitants, and returns to the ship.

Title: The ship stopped.
Summary: For reasons that are not immediately clear, the ship stops in the middle of the sea (rarely: a horse stops in the middle of the road).

Title: Turned into an animal, (ATU 449).
Summary: The hero (heroine) is temporarily transformed into an animal (usually a dog/coyote or a donkey, with the face of the former]: 151-152t to the ground; and the strength of 99 men; if she had taken the hundredth, she would have remained a woman; if the young man had ground, a horse). When he or she is helped to regain their former appearance, the antagonist is transformed into an animal. In some texts, either only the hero or only the antagonist undergoes metamorphosis. Cf. motifs K62B, J62b1 (the character transforms many people into animals).

Title: Recognising one's own among similar ones, H62.1, H161, H324.
Summary: In order to return or obtain a wife, son or husband (in Africa also a domestic animal or object), a person must identify her or him among several identical people or animals (objects).

Title: Recognising a man.
Summary: The character must identify his son or husband among many identical people or animals. See motif K37.

Title: Recognising a woman by her missing little finger.
Summary: A man must identify his chosen one blindfolded. He does this by touch, knowing that one of her fingers is damaged or missing.

Title: Identifying an animal or object.
Summary: The character must identify an animal or object among several identical ones. See motif K37.

Title: Recognised by teeth marks.
Summary: The character recognises the presence of another by noticing traces of their teeth or nails on fruit or leaves.

Title: Three-legged cast-iron bird.
Summary: The clairvoyant cannot identify the person who revealed the secret, because that person does so while hiding among objects that are never found together in everyday life.

Title: The hero helps the chicks, B364.4.
Summary: For doing good to chicks (rarely: young of non-ornithomorphic flying creatures), their mother or father does a favour for the person.

Title: White and black rams, F67.
Summary: Upon arriving in the underworld, the hero sees white and black horses, rams, etc. The white ones will take him to the upper world, while the black ones will take him even lower. Usually, the hero accidentally touches the black one. Sometimes a third ram or horse is mentioned, red or grey. Or the hero grabs the left horn of the animal instead of the right, and as a result ends up not where he wants to be.

Title: The serpent threatens the chicks, B364.4.
Summary: A snake or monster of aquatic-chthonic or indeterminate nature eats or maims the young of a bird or other flying creature – in most cases, the chicks of a huge bird. A man kills the snake (monster). See motif K38.

Title: A bird steals foals, a hero kills a snake.
Summary: Every time a mare gives birth to a wonderful foal, a bird carries it away. Setting out in search of the foals, the hero kills the snake that was devouring the bird's chicks. The bird returns the foals.

Title: A bird carries away the hero, the hero kills the snake.
Summary: A character (almost always a giant bird) brings the hero to its nest, after which the hero accidentally or at the bird's request kills the monster that was devouring the character's children (usually chicks).

Title: The hero cares for the chicks.
Summary: A powerful bird or other flying creature helps a person for taking care of its chicks/offspring: feeding them, sheltering them, decorating them, etc.

Title: The hero feeds the chicks.
Summary: A mighty bird helps a man for feeding its chicks.

Title: The hero shelters the chicks.
Summary: A mighty bird (rarely – another creature) helps a person for sheltering (warming) its chicks (offspring, children).

Title: The hero shields the sleepers from the sun.
Summary: Seeing sleeping fairies or their children, the hero covers them from the scorching rays of the sun. For this, they do him a favour.

Title: The serpent emerges from the water.
Summary: The nest of a mighty bird is located on a tree in the middle (at the edge) of a pond, from where a snake (monster) emerges, threatening the chicks.

Title: A bird carries a hero.
Summary: After the hero helps the bird (usually by doing good to its chicks), it takes him to the place he desires, or instructs its chicks to do so. (This does not involve movement between levels of the universe; in the Sumerian version, the bird gives the hero the ability to move with lightning speed and directs him to his goal).

Title: The serpent covers the water.
Summary: A powerful and dangerous character prevents others from using water (or causes floods), but in most cases allows them to take water (promises not to cause floods) in exchange for people or valuables {italicised in the list of traditions}.

Title: Girl sacrificed to the dragon.
Summary: Fearing a monster living in the water or wishing to end a flood or drought, a girl is sacrificed or voluntarily hides in the waters.

Title: Copper, silver, gold.
Summary: Locations or objects made of three (rarely four) materials of varying degrees of value, but all valued positively (copper, silver, gold; silver, gold, diamonds, etc.) are mentioned.

Title: The Copper Forest, (ATU 511).
Summary: Characters pass through a forest with metal trees of two or more types (copper, silver, etc.).

Title: The collapsed kingdom.
Summary: Returning from the underworld to earth, the princess places the objects surrounding her (clothes, house, "kingdom") into a small object (egg, ball of yarn, etc.), which she takes with her.

Title: The Diamond Kingdom.
Summary: Among three (less often two or four) loci or objects associated with materials of high but varying degrees of value, the highest belongs to precious stones (usually diamonds, but also glass and crystal).

Title: Palace made of gold and silver bricks, F771.1.1.2.
Summary: The narratives (in various contexts) mention a palace (castle, crypt, church, bridge, causeway) built of gold and silver modules – usually bricks, less often planks.

Title: The dragon slayer, ATU 300.
Summary: A reptilian monster demands human sacrifices (devours people; kidnaps a girl; blocks water sources). The hero kills it. The monster's victims do not play an active role in the action.

Title: Severed tongues.
Summary: After killing a monster or animal, the hero cuts off and hides a part of its body, usually the tongue. (In most cases, the deceiver takes credit for the feat, after which the hero presents the hidden item, thus exposing the deceiver).

Title: A mark made with dragon's blood.
Summary: The girl saved by the hero smears him with the blood of the monster he has slain. When the deceiver claims that he killed the dragon, the hero shows the bloodstain on his body, thus proving that he is the victor.

Title: Sword strike from a pit.
Summary: To kill the dragon, the hero digs a pit and hides in it. When the dragon crawls nearby or over the pit, the hero strikes it with a fatal blow of his sword.

Title: Fire-breathing monster, B11.2.11, B19.1, B742.3, B742.4.
Summary: Flames burst from the mouth and/or nostrils of a monstrous character hostile to the hero; his breath is fire.

Title: Fire-breathing horse, B15.5.1.
Summary: Flames burst from the horse's mouth and/or nostrils, or the entire horse is engulfed in fire.

Title: Fire creature.
Summary: A creature consisting of fire is mentioned.

Title: Wild animals serve the hero.
Summary: The character acquires wild animals (at least two different species) that serve him like dogs.

Title: Feeding the Simurgh bird, B322.1.
Summary: The character must feed a powerful creature by regularly throwing it pieces of meat. When the prepared meat runs out, he cuts off the last piece from his own flesh. See motif K38 (the bird carries the hero where he needs to go; on the way, he throws pieces of prepared meat into its beak; when the supplies run out, he gives the bird a piece of his own flesh).

Title: One will be eaten today, another tomorrow.
Summary: Two (rarely more) characters consider themselves doomed to death, but the one whose death will come later rejoices, while the one whose death will come earlier grieves. Cf. motif N30.

Title: Thunder against the snake.
Summary: A character representing a thunderstorm or a giant bird fights a snake or other large creature living in water or underground.

Title: Bird woman kills men.
Summary: A young bird woman energetically searches among a group of men for one she likes, takes him by force and makes him her husband; she turns into a monster, pursues and kills men, but is ultimately killed herself.

Title: The abandoned survives and triumphs, S300.
Summary: People leave a boy, a girl, a sister and brother, a young woman or young spouses alone and leave, or drive them away. Those who are abandoned or expelled discover unusual abilities or helpers, obtaining blood and food. [Materials on European fairy tales are mostly not yet included]

Title: A kind person leaves the fire.
Summary: People leave a boy, a girl, a sister and brother, a young woman or young spouses alone and depart. Someone sympathises with those who have been abandoned and secretly hides fire for them.

Title: The bird brings meat.
Summary: People leave a boy, a girl, a sister and brother, a young woman or young spouses alone and leave, or drive them away. Those who are left behind or driven away discover unusual abilities or helpers, obtaining blood and food. Those who are abandoned eat their fill, while those who abandon them go hungry. A character (often a bird - a crow, magpie, seagull, etc.) visits the abandoned and brings a piece of fat or meat to the camp of the starving.

Title: The dog unties the children.
Summary: The bound children (a young man and his sister) are left alone in an empty camp, and the animal frees them.

Title: The false mother is rejected.
Summary: The character kidnaps the boy or hides him from his mother or father, pretending to be his mother or father. The kidnapped boy learns the truth and leaves the kidnapper.

Title: The frog pretends to be a mother.
Summary: A frog or toad (coastal Koryaks: triton) kidnaps or finds a boy and lies that she is his real mother. See motif K44.

Title: Upon returning, throws food.
Summary: The hero or heroine returns after a long absence. Seeing (usually from the roof of the house) his or her parents (mother, husband) languishing in poverty, he or she throws food at them, extinguishes the fire, pushes them, etc. At first, they usually do not understand what is going on.

Title: Sedna (severed fingers).
Summary: A man and a woman belonging to different generations (father – daughter, son – mother) come into conflict. The man sails away from the woman in a boat or on a raft, or leaves her on a sledge. When she tries to grab the edge of the boat (raft, sled), he cuts off her fingers. (The common motif among the Warrau and Eskimos was first noted by O. Zerries [Zerries 1954: 346, 376]).

Title: Fingers turn into aquatic animals.
Summary: A man sails away from a woman or girl in a boat or on a raft. When she tries to grab the edge of the boat (raft), he cuts off her fingers. The fingers turn into aquatic animals.

Title: A woman becomes an aquatic animal.
Summary: A man and a woman belonging to different generations (father – daughter, son – mother) come into conflict, as a result of which the woman turns into a marine mammal, the mistress of marine mammals, or a frog.

Title: A woman throws herself into the sea.
Summary: In a fit of fear or shame, a woman or girl runs to the sea, throws herself into the water or hides on the shore. The suitor tries in vain to catch up with her.

Title: Woman and dog: the origin of humans.
Summary: A woman mates with a dog. Her children grow up to be humans and usually become the ancestors of certain ethnic groups.

Title: The dog becomes handsome.
Summary: A woman marries a man who originally had the appearance of a dog. The birth of children from a dog is not essential to the plot.

Title: The origin of dogs.
Summary: The marriage of a woman and a dog gave rise to dogs – friends and helpers of humans.

Title: The dog fulfils the condition of marriage.
Summary: A girl gives herself to a dog because it fulfils the condition of marriage set by her or her father for her future husband. See motif K47A.

Title: The hero's singing bird, ATU 550.
Summary: The antagonist orders the wonderful bird captured by the hero to sing or talk, but it remains silent or cries out inappropriately. The bird begins to sing (talk) after the hero has triumphed over his opponents.

Title: Birds on a cap.
Summary: The hero's costume and/or headdress are decorated with live birds or animals. Usually, the antagonist steals the clothes and pretends to be the hero, but the birds and animals on his headdress remain silent or cry out differently. See motif K48.

Title: Dead mother nursing a baby, E323.1.
Summary: A woman who has been transformed into an animal or found herself outside the human world returns to her child to feed and care for it. Cf. motif K33.

Title: An imaginary wife cuts off the head of an enemy.
Summary: A man approaches the enemy disguised as a woman and kills him at night (usually cutting off his head and taking it with him).

Title: The deceived wife.
Summary: The husband feigns death, disappears or leaves home for a long time. The wife learns that he has married another woman, finds and, as a rule, kills her husband and/or rival, who often turns out to be a creature of non-human nature.

Title: Pushes a rival into boiling water.
Summary: One woman comes to another in the absence of a man and kills her by pushing her rival's head into boiling liquid or pouring boiling water or hot fat into her ear. See motif K51.

Title: Smiles on the faces of the dead.
Summary: The bodies of the slain are left in such a position that it seems as if they are rejoicing – smiling, laughing, dancing.

Title: In pursuit of the kidnapped to the bottom of the sea.
Summary: A woman or young man who approaches the shore is carried away by predatory sea creatures to the bottom of the sea; a character descends to rescue the kidnapped person and brings him or her back with the help of cunning and shamanic powers.

Title: The slave pours water into the hearth.
Summary: The hero goes to the bottom of the sea for a woman. The slave pours water into the hearth in the house of the water dwellers. Hiding behind clouds of steam, the hero takes the woman away. See motif K52.

Title: Broken axe.
Summary: The hero comes to capture the daughter of a supernatural creature. He sees a slave breaking an axe (adze, wedge). The hero repairs the axe, and the slave helps him in return. See motif K52.

Title: Flooding in the home.
Summary: Demonstrating his power, a shaman, sorcerer or other character with magical abilities causes the dwelling in which he and other people are located to begin to fill with water. Sometimes it is said that this water is an illusion and that those present also see animals (waterfowl, fish or marine mammals).

Title: Penis instead of fish.
Summary: Demonstrating his power, a shaman, sorcerer or other character with magical abilities causes the dwelling in which he and other people are located to begin to fill with water. Sometimes it is said that this water is an illusion. One episode: the magical specialist orders those present to catch the birds or fish that have appeared with the water, or they begin to catch them on their own initiative; when the water disappears, people see that they are holding not caught animals, but their penises or something else.

Title: Animal skins – a means of transformation.
Summary: A character temporarily transforms into an animal or bird of a certain species by putting on its skin, or skins taken along with them come to life and serve the hero.

Title: Two giants.
Summary: When encountering a giant or a snake, a person is afraid of it, but it becomes his friend and asks for help when he is fighting another giant or snake. The person fulfils the request.

Title: Blow to the legs.
Summary: A man and a friendly giant live together. The friendly giant fights another giant and asks the man for help. The help consists of the man damaging the enemy's legs.

Title: Rewarded chastity.
Summary: A powerful character finds out whether his guest has made love to his daughter or wife (if the character is a woman: whether he has attempted to have sexual contact with her). A man who is impotent or (successfully pretends to be) chaste is rewarded (at least not punished). In most cases, the other character engages in sexual contact or is unable to hide what he has done and is punished as a result.

Title: The worthy are rewarded, the unworthy are punished, ATU 480, 480D*.
Summary: One of the girls, young women or young girls (wives of one man) meets a character who is able to reward and punish. She behaves correctly and receives a reward. Another (others) tries to repeat everything, but behaves incorrectly and is punished (rarely: not rewarded).

Title: The unworthy fail, the worthy succeed, ATU 431.
Summary: Two or three sisters successively go to a powerful character. The first or the first two act incorrectly, perish or fail to achieve their goal. The last one acts correctly, is saved or rewarded.

Title: Mother-in-law performs the work of her daughter-in-law.
Summary: The groom, the bringer of prosperity, orders the girl who has come to perform work that she herself is unable to do. The groom's mother performs the work, and the girl is accepted by the groom. See motif K56A. Except for the Ket people: the work is performed by tiny women sitting in or behind the mother-in-law's ear.

Title: Asks to do worse.
Summary: A character (usually a girl) comes to another (usually an old woman). The latter asks the visitor to perform absurd and harmful actions (to mess up the house, bring dirty water, etc.). The visitor does the opposite of what is asked (cleans the house, brings clean water) and is rewarded. The other character does everything literally and is punished.

Title: Washing in red water.
Summary: A girl becomes beautiful or ugly after washing herself with water of a certain colour.

Title: Wash lizards and beetles.
Summary: A supernatural character asks a girl to redeem (feed) his (her) children. These are snakes, beetles or wild animals. The girl does everything she is asked and is rewarded.

Title: Do not tie shoelaces.
Summary: A wandering girl or young girl should not tie her shoelaces or the laces on her shoes or clothing. If she does so, she will get into trouble.

Title: The messenger dog.
Summary: When a kind girl returns home, an animal or bird (usually a dog) announces that she is well, but when an unkind girl returns or when her dead body is brought back, the dog (rooster, crow) announces that something is wrong with her.

Title: While the demon brings clothes, ATU 480A.
Summary: Left alone with the demon in the bathhouse (mill, etc.), the girl demands that he bring her new clothes, jewellery, etc., and while the demon is fetching them, morning comes.

Title: The wind carries away the yarn.
Summary: A girl is told to clean the yarn, or to spin and weave. The wind blows the yarn (cloth, spindle) away, the girl goes in search of it, and comes across a character who rewards her.

Title: Wash black until white.
Summary: A person is tasked with washing something black until it is white or something white until it is black (yarn, clothing, a board, etc.).

Title: Ashes turn into flour.
Summary: A stepmother sends her stepdaughter to a house in the forest, giving her ashes, sand, etc. instead of food. The stepdaughter turns them into flour, groats, etc.

Title: The stepmother's daughter burned to death.
Summary: After meeting a supernatural character, a kind person receives valuables, while a greedy person burns to death upon returning home.

Title: The evil girl becomes ugly.
Summary: After meeting a supernatural character, the unkind girl becomes ugly.

Title: Ugly girl: growths on the face.
Summary: After meeting a supernatural character, growths (tail, horns, warts, etc.) appear on the face (back of the head) of an unkind girl.

Title: The Old Woman Becomes Beautiful, ATU 877.
Summary: An old or ugly woman unexpectedly becomes a young beauty or acquires wealth. Usually, another woman tries to repeat her actions and either dies or suffers damage.

Title: Skinning oneself to rejuvenate (ATU 877).
Summary: To become a young beauty, an old or unattractive woman asks to have her skin stripped off. Cf. motif H4.

Title: Any weather is good.
Summary: A person who responds kindly to the questions of characters representing the weather during certain periods of the calendar cycle is rewarded. Another person who scolds these characters is punished.

Title: Conversation with the months.
Summary: A man who kindly answers the questions of characters representing the weather in certain months of the year is rewarded. Another man scolds them and is punished.

Title: Conversation with Moroz.
Summary: A person responds kindly to a question from a character embodying cold, praises him, and is rewarded. Another expresses dissatisfaction and is punished.

Title: Food asks her to taste it.
Summary: On the way to another world, people or objects ask a child (girl) to taste the food they offer or to do some work. The child (girl) does everything (rarely does not do) and therefore achieves the goal.

Title: Greenery in winter.
Summary: In winter, a girl (rarely a boy) is sent to bring something that is normally only available in summer. She brings it.

Title: An animal mistakenly taken for a groom.
Summary: A girl marries an animal (brings it with her), and it turns into a handsome man. Another girl tries to do the same, but dies or suffers harm.

Title: The good girl returns with her fiancé.
Summary: A girl goes to another world, behaves correctly, returns with an animal or an object, inside which her groom is found. Usually, another girl behaves incorrectly and suffers damage.

Title: A girl's hand in a cobra's hole.
Summary: A virtuous girl (usually the daughter of a dog) wants to kill herself and puts her hand in a snake's hole. The snake does not bite her, but rewards her.

Title: Married to a dog.
Summary: A young man brings an animal to his home, and it turns into a girl. Imitating him, another man marries a dog (pig), but it remains an animal.

Title: Eaten by a boa constrictor.
Summary: A girl agrees to become the wife of a snake, which turns into a handsome man. Another girl (or her mother or father) brings the snake to her or offers it to become her husband, but it does not turn into a man and kills her.

Title: The mouse helper rings a bell.
Summary: When a small animal (usually a mouse) rings a bell, beats a drum, etc., a blind or distant antagonist believes that these sounds are made by the hero (heroine). Thanks to this, the hero (heroine) is saved.

Title: The dog-groom tests the bride.
Summary: Two or three sisters successively become the dog's brides. The first or the first two act incorrectly, perish or fail to achieve their goal. The last one acts correctly and succeeds.

Title: The girl takes off her shirts, the snake takes off its skin (ATU 433B).
Summary: A girl marries a monster. On their wedding night, he orders her to take off her shirt, and she orders him to take off his skin. The girl survives, and the monster becomes handsome – usually because she has more shirts (or skins worn in advance) than he does.

Title: A row of stones and a row of logs.
Summary: A girl finds herself in a forest hut, where a bear arrives. He orders her to make him a bed out of stones and logs.

Title: The worthy are rewarded, the unworthy are punished.
Summary: Two men take turns meeting a character who can reward and punish. One behaves correctly and is rewarded, the other (or two others) behave incorrectly and are punished (rarely: not rewarded).

Title: The Old Man with Golden Coals, ATU 751B*.
Summary: A poor man goes in search of fire. An old man by the fire gives him coals. At home, they turn into gold. An envious neighbour (brother) deliberately extinguishes the fire in his house and asks the old man for coals. His house burns down.

Title: Clenched jaws.
Summary: A supernatural creature (object) bestows wealth upon a modest person. A greedy person, trying to take more than their fair share, is caught and cannot free themselves (for a long time). Usually, the creature pinches the outstretched hand.

Title: Stench instead of fragrance.
Summary: A man's intestinal gases become fragrant. An envious person tries to achieve the same result, but the outcome is the opposite.

Title: The Golden Axe, ATU 729.
Summary: A man loses his axe. A spirit or chief offers him a golden one, but the man says that the axe is not his and for this he receives axes of gold and silver as a reward. Another man deliberately loses his ordinary axe, seeking to obtain a golden one, but suffers a fiasco.

Title: Broken leg.
Summary: One man treats a bird, which brings a seed, and something valuable grows. Another deliberately cripples a bird, then treats it, and it brings a seed, and something harmful and terrible grows.

Title: Treasures in a pumpkin.
Summary: A pumpkin or watermelon (grown from gifted seeds) given to a person turns out to contain treasures.

Title: Two Hunchbacks, ATU 503.
Summary: Two people have the same physical defect (a bump, a hump). The first one finds himself in a place where spirits gather, and they rid him of his defect. The second comes to the spirits, and they double his defect, giving him what they took from the first person. (Uther 2004 mentions Kasevich, Osipov 1976, No. 171; the Karen text is published there and does not correspond to the definition of the motif).

Title: Song mentioning the days of the week.
Summary: A man sees dwarves (spirits, witches) having fun. Their song mentions the names of the days of the week. The man sings along, naming the days that the dwarves like. He is rewarded. (Usually, someone else tries to get the same reward, but names the wrong days of the week and is punished).

Title: The division of the rooster, ATU 1533.
Summary: A man divides a roasted rooster (goose) according to the social ranks of those present (the head to the host, the wings to the daughters, etc.), usually taking the least prestigious but meatiest part for himself.

Title: The division of roosters, (ATU 1533.2).
Summary: Five chickens (geese, etc.) must be divided among six eaters (other numbers are possible). The solution is to give each pair of participants one chicken and take two for oneself (two chickens and one person – three, two people and one chicken – also three).

Title: Woman, two men, five eggs, ATU 1663.
Summary: In order to divide a certain number (often five) of eggs equally among people of different sexes, a cunning woman takes into account that each of the men already has two eggs.

Title: Cinderella, ATU 510A.
Summary: A girl hides her beauty and/or lives in poverty, a man of high status sees her in her true form/in luxurious attire and takes her as his wife, recognising her by an item he gave her or she lost, usually a slipper or shoe, or by seeing her change her clothes. {All texts with this motif are also considered to contain the f62 motif}.

Title: The Beauty from the Land of Soap, (ATU 510B).
Summary: A noble young man, who treated a lowly servant girl rudely and contemptuously, does not recognise her in the guise of a magnificent beauty and does not understand her hints about the relevant episodes. Or the younger brother responds to the hints of his older brothers after they first beat him and then fail to recognise him in the guise of a handsome hero.

Title: The stuck-on shoe.
Summary: To stop a beautiful woman from running away, a man in love with her smears resin or glue on the threshold (porch). The shoe sticks, and all the girls try it on to find its owner.

Title: The ring in the pie.
Summary: The prince puts a ring on the finger of a beautiful girl, not knowing that she is the very girl who works in his kitchen. The girl slips the ring into the prince's food, and he recognises it.

Title: Tight shoe, cut-off toes.
Summary: The prince marries the girl who fits the shoe. The girl cuts off her toes or heel so that the shoe will fit.

Title: Daughter is persuaded to kill her mother.
Summary: Due to her naivety or by accident, a young girl causes her mother's death.

Title: Canal builder.
Summary: To win the hand of his beloved, the character builds a canal or aqueduct or digs a well. Usually, the woman does not end up marrying the person who completed the work, and either she herself or the suitor perishes.

Title: Water in exchange for love.
Summary: The character brings water for irrigation or a fish river to the place where the girl agrees to meet him, and does not bring water if she refuses. (The parallel between the myths of Peru and Oregon was first noted in Lehmann-Nitsche 1935a; 1936).

Title: Turn of the watercourse: failure.
Summary: The character builds a canal, bridge, or dam. For some reason, the work cannot be completed as planned.

Title: Osiris's chest.
Summary: One person places another in a box and closes the lid, or ties the other to a board, a boat, etc., and throws them into the water. The coffin (box, board) is nailed to a distant land, where the captive is freed. Usually, he returns and takes revenge on his enemy.

Title: Are the bonds strong?
Summary: Unaware of the danger, the character allows himself to be tightly bound.

Title: Invitation to the Coffin, ATU 330B, G514.1.
Summary: The character is invited to find out whether the box or pit is the right size for him, whether he can crawl through the opening, climb into the bag, etc., after which he is locked in a coffin, box, barrel, buried, etc. Cf. motif M56D.

Title: Stropiva with the king, patient with the groom.
Summary: The stubborn wife of a worthy man goes on a date with a demon or a servant. He beats her, but she patiently endures her lover's beatings.

Title: Learn the secret, ATU 500*.
Summary: In order to find out the exact number, a specific object in a certain set, the name of a specific character, or the reason for a certain phenomenon, the character tries to surprise (or unintentionally surprises) the owner of such knowledge. The latter begins to talk to himself, involuntarily revealing the necessary information to the hero standing nearby.

Title: Two heads in a sack.
Summary: A dangerous character mistakes two people sleeping (hiding) in a sack or two people lying with their feet towards each other for a single creature.

Title: Learning names.
Summary: In order to learn the names of strangers, the character finds or creates a situation in which they call each other by name aloud.

Title: Find out the name, ATU 500.
Summary: A demon agrees to help (agrees not to harm) a person on condition that the person guesses his name. At the last moment, the person accidentally learns the demon's name, and the demon disappears or rewards the person.

Title: Overheard secret of a demon, (ATU 500, ATU 1091A).
Summary: A person will die if they cannot find the answer to the demon's question. A person or their acquaintance accidentally learns the answer by overhearing the demon talking to himself or to another demon. See motif C29.

Title: From work became a beetle, ATU 501.
Summary: A young woman accidentally gives her fiancé, husband or mother-in-law the impression that she works a lot. To prevent the deception from being revealed, she or someone else makes others believe that women's work makes them ugly or turns them into animals. The husband forbids his wife to work.

Title: The one who laughs rewards.
Summary: Seeing an absurd situation, a powerful (supernatural) character laughs and is thereby usually cured of his ailment. For this, the people involved in the situation are rewarded and saved from danger.

Title: The Living Doll, ATU 459.
Summary: Fearing her husband's wrath, a childless woman pretends to have given birth. Her husband believes that he has a daughter or son, and after some time marries her off (marries him off). During the wedding ceremony, a doll or animal is placed under the veil (in the palanquin), but at the last moment, a supernatural character transforms the supposed bride (groom) into a girl or boy.

Title: War of animals, Th B260-B263.
Summary: Animals, birds, etc. fight or play with each other, divided into two hostile camps. The stakes are high, often life itself. {Data incomplete}. ATU 222. B261, war between birds and animals. ATU 222A. B261.1, the bat joins first one side, then the other. K2323.1, the raised tail of a fox serves as a signal.

Title: The Quarrel of the Mouse and the Bird, ATU 222B.
Summary: A mouse (rat, mole, etc.) and a bird quarrel after failing to divide their winter supplies. (This episode usually serves as the beginning of a story about a war between birds and animals).

Title: A man nurses a wounded eagle.
Summary: A man saves (spares) and nurses a wounded bird. Having regained its strength, the bird puts him on its back and carries him to a distant land or to the sky.

Title: Fish babies and deer people.
Summary: A man comes to people who hunt humans or catch fish-people. For them, these are wild animals or fish.

Title: Escape from the cave of the herd owner, ATU 1137, K521.1, K603.
Summary: Finding himself in the dwelling of the master of the herds or the owner of wild animals, the character fears that the master will kill him. To escape to freedom, he clings to the underside of one of the animals leaving the pen or cave.

Title: The Blinded Cyclops, ATU 1137, K521.1, K603.
Summary: A man blinds a sleeping or immobile giant-cannibal and escapes from him.

Title: Sticky object.
Summary: The hero's opponent provokes him to touch an object that turns out to be sticky. The hero sticks to the object (see Miller 1890: 41). See motif K64.

Title: The blacksmith blinds the cyclops.
Summary: The person who gouges out or burns out the cyclops's only (sighted) eye is a blacksmith.

Title: Spirits of loci.
Summary: Having been cast out, discarded, or born of the first ancestors, creatures of a certain category acquire individuality, transforming into spirits who are the masters of various loci.

Title: Spirits fall from the sky.
Summary: After being thrown from a height or expelled, various creatures end up in different locations, acquiring corresponding functions and names.

Title: People and spirits.
Summary: Spirits (deities) or unpleasant animals (snakes, frogs, worms, etc.) are generated by the same first anthropomorphic pair or the same pair of first ancestors as humans (deities).

Title: Eve's Unwashed Children, ATU 758.
Summary: A woman (rarely a man) hides some of her children (less often, all of them) or some of her domestic animals from God. According to God, the hidden children become either poor people or creatures of a non-human nature, and the hidden domestic animals become wild.

Title: Division into servants and masters, (ATU 758).
Summary: A woman gives birth to many children, but hides some of them from God. Those who are hidden become the progenitors of people of low social status, and those who are shown become the progenitors of people of high status. {The definition of plot 758 in Uther 2004 largely coincides with ours, but the references also include traditions in which children hidden from God become spirits rather than people of low status}.

Title: Man and tiger.
Summary: A woman or female animal gives birth to several sons, including a human and a tiger.

Title: Eve is ashamed of her large family.
Summary: A woman (alone or with her husband) hides some of her children from God because she is ashamed of having given birth to so many offspring.

Title: Incorrect marriage rites and the birth of spirits.
Summary: The first human couple initially only have miscarriages, or their children are spirits or unpleasant and dangerous animals. After performing a formal marriage ceremony or repeating it according to new rules, the woman gives birth to real people or gods.

Title: Midwife in the demonic world, ATU 476**, (ATU 156B*).
Summary: A woman is invited into the non-human world, where she delivers a child for one of the creatures (or serves as a nanny for a certain period of time, baptises the child). Then she returns to the human world.

Title: Midwife to a toad.
Summary: A woman delivers a baby (baptises a child) for a creature that in the human world has the appearance of a toad or frog.

Title: Which eye do you see with? (ATU 476**)
