Summary: Once in the locus of demons, a person sees them in their true form. Upon returning, the person sees the demon again, which ordinary people are incapable of doing. The demon blinds him.

Title: Bogatyrs with different abilities, ATU 513, 653, F601.
Summary: Each of several companions or brothers excels others in some way (sees, hears, runs, etc. better than anyone else). Cf. motif K2B, "Gorynya and Dubyna".

Title: The flying ship as a condition of marriage, ATU 513B.
Summary: The princess (inheritance) is given to the one who builds (obtains) a ship capable of moving on land (flying through the air).

Title: Princesses given to companions.
Summary: Travelling from one place to another, the hero leaves one of his companions in each place (usually marrying them to the princesses he has received as a reward), and continues on his way. When he gets into trouble, his companions come to his aid.

Title: Bear marriage.
Summary: A bear (lion) takes a woman away, or a she-bear takes a man away. They have children who are either human or bear-like in appearance. Less commonly, a woman gives birth to a son in a den because she was pregnant at the time of her abduction by the bear.

Title: Bear fosterling.
Summary: A boy who grew up (was conceived) in a bear's den (lion's cave) becomes a bogatyr.

Title: Burnt moccasins, K1615.
Summary: At night, one person intends to throw another person's shoes or clothes into the fire, but ends up burning his own shoes or clothes. Usually, the father-in-law throws his son-in-law's shoes into the fire at night in order to freeze him out, but the son-in-law has already switched shoes, so the father-in-law burns his own.

Title: The Drowned Wife, ATU 1120.
Summary: A character of low status annoys characters of high status. Learning of the intention of the characters of high status to drown him or his property (rarely: to strangle him), he arranges for one of them or their property to be drowned instead.

Title: Agreement not to be angry, ATU 1000.
Summary: A character of low social status (without supernatural abilities) takes a job with a character of high social status (with supernatural abilities) on the condition that the employer will not get angry with the employee. By repeatedly annoying the employer, the employee causes him to become angry and, as a result, be severely punished or pay a large sum of money.

Title: Skin torn from the back.
Summary: The character agrees that under certain conditions another person may tear the skin from his back or cause him some other bodily harm.

Title: Escape from the worker, ATU 1132.
Summary: The worker (rarely – the husband) annoys the master (wife) so much that he or she decides to run away, taking his or her property with him or her. The worker hides in a sack (chest) with his or her property and ends up back where he or she started.

Title: Before the First Cuckoo, ATU 1029.
Summary: Someone promises to fulfil their duties until they hear a bird singing at a certain moment in a temporal cycle (annual or daily). Another character imitates the bird. The first recognises the deception.

Title: Slaughter the sheep that looks at you.
Summary: A fool or a rogue is instructed to slaughter the sheep (cow, bull) that looks at him, i.e. any one. He slaughters them all, because they all looked at him.

Title: Smiling sheep.
Summary: Pretending to carry out his master's orders, the worker cuts off the animals' lips (to make them look like they are smiling).

Title: Bear in the barn
Summary: When a worker is sent to a place where he is to be torn apart by a predator, he tames it and lets it into the barn (stable) at home. As a result, the predator destroys the owner's livestock.

Title: Cows carried in pieces.
Summary: The worker is instructed to follow a straight line or overcome the obstacle without breaking it. He kills and cuts up the animals entrusted to him, throws the pieces over the fence or breaks the fence, even though there is a passage nearby.

Title: A clot of blood protects the father. T541.41.1.
Summary: A strong man takes food from a weak man and forces him to work for him (usually a son-in-law mistreats his father-in-law). A boy appears in the house of the wronged man from a clot of animal blood that has been collected. He kills the offender.

Title: Pilgrims to the deity.
Summary: Several men walk towards the horizon to ascend to the sky and visit the Sun or another supreme deity. Usually, one or more of them perish along the way, while others reach their destination. They return by a shorter route than they came.

Title: Two daughters-in-law: a girl and a frog.
Summary: One man marries a girl, another (usually the brother of the first) marries a frog or a toad, or the girl and the frog are the wives of one man. Usually, the wives are given certain tests, and the girl is recognised as a worthy wife, while the frog is recognised as worthless.

Title: Coyote betrays and saves his brother.
Summary: The coyote's brother successfully defends himself against enemies until the coyote breaks a certain taboo. The enemies kill the brother; the coyote comes to the enemy camp, retrieves his brother's remains and either flees from the enemies or kills them. The brother comes back to life.

Title: Three maidens.
Summary: A character of high status meets or marries three (less often two or four) women. One (promises to bear and) bears him a son (children) with unusual qualities, the other two (promise to engage in and) engage in crafts or housekeeping, or intend to marry men of lower status.

Title: Prohibition on lighting fires.
Summary: The king notices that his prohibition on lighting fires at night has been violated.

Title: Children of the younger wife, ATU 707.
Summary: A young wife (promises to give birth and) gives birth to wonderful children (or one son). In the absence of her husband, attempts are made to kill the wife or her child (usually by slandering them to the husband), but they remain alive. (For medieval European variants, see Newell 1906).

Title: Child substitution.
Summary: Malicious women replace the newborn with an animal or an inanimate object (they tell the baby's father that his wife gave birth to an animal or an object). See motif K73.

Title: The child is replaced by an inanimate object.
Summary: After hiding or discarding a newborn baby, the woman's rivals replace it with an inanimate object and/or inform the father that his wife has given birth to a stone, a broom, etc. See motifs k73a2, k73a2a, k73a3.

Title: The child is replaced with a broom.
Summary: The ill-wishers of the new mother replace the baby with a broom (they tell the father that his wife has given birth to a broom).

Title: The child is replaced with a log.
Summary: After hiding or discarding a newborn baby, ill-wishers replace it with a piece of wood and/or inform the father that his wife has given birth to a piece of wood.

Title: The child is replaced with a doll.
Summary: The midwife's ill-wishers replace the baby with a statue or doll (telling the father that his wife has given birth to a doll).

Title: The child is replaced by a puppy.
Summary: Malicious women replace the newborn with a puppy (telling the father that his wife has given birth to a puppy). See motifs K73, K73A.

Title: The child is replaced by a kitten.
Summary: Malicious women replace the newborn with a kitten (telling the father that his wife has given birth to a kitten). See motifs K73, K73A.

Title: A baby is replaced by a monkey.
Summary: Malicious women replace a newborn baby with a monkey (telling the father that his wife has given birth to a monkey).

Title: A child turns into a tree.
Summary: Malicious women kill (throw away) her wonderful children. Trees (flowers) grow from their remains, later reincarnating into humans.

Title: Miraculous children: a sister with two brothers.
Summary: A woman gives birth to three (not two or many) miraculous children – two boys and a girl. They grow up and triumph over their enemies.

Title: Miraculous children: brother and sister.
Summary: A woman gives birth to a miraculous boy and girl. They are replaced by animals or objects and thrown away, but they escape and triumph over their enemies.

Title: The talking bed.
Summary: Lying on the marital bed, the deceiver, who has taken the place of the real wife, hears the conversation of her rival or her children, and in the morning orders the bed to be destroyed.

Title: Punishment of the innocent.
Summary: A woman falsely accused of murdering her newborn child, or of giving birth to a puppy instead of a child, etc., is subjected to cruel and humiliating punishment or execution. See motif K73.

Title: Mother and child in a barrel.
Summary: A woman with her newborn son (pregnant with a boy) or a girl with a young man are placed in a barrel (box; rarely: in a boat) and lowered into the sea (river).

Title: Boil the kettle with a story.
Summary: It is necessary to boil the pot by telling an incredible but nevertheless true story.

Title: Throw a nut for good luck.
Summary: A person who is asked to count the nuts in a barrel (taking them out one by one) accompanies his actions with a revealing story.

Title: Fill the bag with truth.
Summary: A person is asked to fill a bag (cauldron) with truth (lies, fairy tales). He fulfils the request by telling a revealing story.

Title: And so the mother could not eat her child.
Summary: A woman is accused of actions that she could not have committed by her very nature. To refute the accusation, an example of something equally absurd and impossible is given, or it is pointed out that the interlocutor accepts the impossible but does not believe in the possible.

Title: The hero flies to his mother's enemies to eavesdrop on their conversation.
Summary: The wife of a powerful character gives birth to wonderful children. Her jealous sisters conspire to make her husband order her to be disposed of (usually by locking her and the child in a barrel and throwing it into the water). The boy immediately grows up and rescues his mother and himself. He himself (in the form of a bird, animal, insect, or flying in on a miraculous object) or his puppy brother enters his father's lair and, eavesdropping on the conversation, learns of the existence of miraculous objects. Upon returning, he obtains them or already possesses them and demonstrates them to his father when they meet (the objects may include the young man's brothers).

Title: The hero kills the enemy of his enchanted wife.
Summary: The hero saves the magical wife from her enemy at a time when both the future wife and the enemy have zoomorphic appearances. Later, the rescued woman becomes a woman.

Title: The girl in the bird's nest, (ATU 705A, 709A).
Summary: A girl finds herself in a bird's nest (usually the bird carries the baby girl away). The bird takes care of the girl, who grows up to be a beauty.

Title: Brothers and the dwarf.
Summary: Of two or more characters, each one stays at home or goes to fetch fire for cooking or brings food to the house. Each time, a certain character appears who eats the food and/or defeats the one who stayed behind or came to fetch fire.

Title: Only the hero defeats the demon and follows in his footsteps.
Summary: A demonic character arrives and mocks one of the men remaining in the house. When the hero remains, he defeats the demon and follows in his footsteps to where he dwells. Cf. motif K74 (an unassuming and weak-looking man approaches a warrior preparing dinner; he eats everything, ties up, beats or kills the cook. When the hero remains to cook, he defeats the demon).

Title: The younger daughter agrees, ATU 433B.
Summary: The girl (usually the youngest of the sisters) does not reject the hero, who temporarily takes the form of an animal, a freak, an old man, a poor man, or a loser, or she picks up the hero's remains and he comes back to life. After some time, the hero reveals his true nature.

Title: Throwing an apple at a suitor, H316.
Summary: The character chooses one of many suitors (a woman chooses a husband, a boy chooses a father, a young man chooses a bride) by throwing an object (often an apple) at him. Cf. motif K113A (throwing an object at random, not at a person who is nearby).

Title: The younger brother-in-law's place is in the barn.
Summary: The ruler orders his youngest daughter (and her chosen husband) to live in conditions that do not correspond to her status. He does not know that her chosen one is not a poor wretch, as he seems, but a mighty warrior and a handsome man.

Title: Gardener.
Summary: Appearing incognito to an authoritative figure, the hero works for him as a gardener.

Title: Groom.
Summary: Appearing incognito to an authoritative character, the hero works for him as a groom.

Title: Three melons from three daughters.
Summary: Wanting to show that it is time for them to marry, daughters of different ages send their father fruits of varying degrees of ripeness (bread baked in different ways).

Title: The Unwashed Woman, ATU 361.
Summary: The devil promises a person wealth if he does not wash (cut his hair, etc.) for a certain period of time; both keep their promises.

Title: The Strange Son, ATU 425A, 441.
Summary: A boy who is born or found has a strange or ugly appearance (ball, nut, sack, half-human, dwarf, animal), but then demonstrates magical powers and turns out to be handsome (usually getting a bride of high status). The princess's magical spouse initially has a non-human or ugly appearance.

Title: The frog son and the frog husband.
Summary: A frog or toad marries a beautiful woman, or a handsome young man marries a frog.

Title: Son-snake and husband-snake.
Summary: The son or foster son of snake spouses. He turns into a human. The snake is the princess's magical spouse, lost and returned.

Title: Pumpkin child.
Summary: The son (rarely – daughter) or foster child of a married couple emerges from a pumpkin (rarely: watermelon, nut) or is found inside it.

Title: A woman gave birth to a pumpkin.
Summary: A woman gives birth to a pumpkin, inside which there is a person (many people) or which turns into a person.

Title: The Hedgehog Son, ATU 441.
Summary: The son or foster child of a married couple is a hedgehog. He marries a princess and turns into a handsome man.

Title: Son (daughter) as a piglet.
Summary: The son (daughter) or foster child of a married couple is a pig. He marries a princess and turns into a handsome man (she marries a handsome man).

Title: The calf-boy.
Summary: A young man with the appearance of a calf marries and then turns into a handsome man.

Title: The crab son.
Summary: The son or foster son of a married couple – a crab. He marries a princess and turns into a handsome man.

Title: The magical groom threatens disaster.
Summary: A young man, temporarily having a strange or monstrous appearance (freak, animal, etc.), woos a princess, but is rejected. Then he causes natural disasters or creates personal troubles for the king, who is forced to give up his daughter.

Title: Verlioka, ATU 210.
Summary: Various objects and animals (rarely: only animals, but including those that are safe in reality) defeat a strong enemy (usually joining the hero who is going to take revenge on the strong enemy for an insult and hiding in the house where the enemy is supposed to appear), attacking him in turn; he dies or flees. Either someone or the attacked character himself places objects in his dwelling that then harm that character.

Title: Bremen Town Musicians, ATU 130.
Summary: Having left their owners, domestic animals find an empty house or build a house. Robbers or predatory animals come there. Domestic animals attack or simply scare them away. Predators do not understand who they are facing and flee.

Title: Wolf's Head, ATU 125.
Summary: When they see predators, domestic animals consciously or accidentally behave in such a way that the predators flee in fear.

Title: Weapons of the goat.
Summary: The goat (goat, ram, etc.) responds to the predator's questions in the sense that parts of its body are weapons and other objects designed to kill the questioner, or that the goat is actually armed.

Title: The goat with three bellies.
Summary: Goats encounter a wolf. One goat has one stomach, the second has two, the third has three, and so on. The goat with the most stomachs kills or scares away the wolf.

Title: Those hiding in the house frighten the enemy.
Summary: Various objects and/or animals hide in the house where a strong enemy is expected to appear. They take turns attacking or frightening him, and he either dies or flees. See motifs K77a and K77b.

Title: Swallowed, extracted from the little finger.
Summary: The cannibal swallows people. When he is killed, it turns out that they are not in his belly or that they are dead there. They are found alive not in the belly, but in the cannibal's finger, or there is a means of reviving them in the little finger, or the cannibal's finger must be cut or severed to find the people.

Title: Swallows and heals.
Summary: A demonic character swallows cripples and regurgitates them healthy and beautiful.

Title: The snake shows how to recover.
Summary: Finding himself in a helpless situation, a man sees how a small animal finds a cure for itself or another animal. The man uses the same cure, saves himself or saves another.

Title: The indestructible woman.
Summary: The character transforms into objects or creatures, which another character systematically destroys. However, the character (usually a young woman) is reborn each time in a new form and eventually in her original form.

Title: A bird or object tells of a crime, ATU 720, 780, 780B.
Summary: An object or creature that has emerged from the remains, jewellery, etc. of the murdered person tells about the murder, exposing the criminal. The East Slavic texts in this section were mainly provided by K.Y. Rakhno.

Title: The bird tells of the crime.
Summary: A bird (usually arising from the remains of the murdered person or embodying their soul) tells of the crime committed or takes revenge on the murderer itself.

Title: The pipe tells of a crime, ATU 780.
Summary: A part of the victim's body or a plant that grew at the site of the murder tells people about the crime that was committed, usually after it has been made into a musical instrument.

Title: To the forest for berries.
Summary: Members of the same family (girls, young women or children) go to the forest to pick berries and kill (bewitch) the one who is the object of their envy.

Title: Hair turns into grass, (ATU 780A).
Summary: The hair on a character's head turns into grass (thorns, bamboo, bushes).

Title: The boar and the fratricides.
Summary: Brothers, competing as suitors or heirs, must hunt a boar. The younger brother succeeds. The older brothers kill him and take the boar for themselves. The truth comes out.

Title: Talking pipe made from a plant that grew there.
Summary: A musical instrument is made from a plant that grew where the character was killed (fell, touched the ground). When played, it produces a text with a specific meaning.

Title: Mother killed, father ate, ATU 720.
Summary: The mother or stepmother kills the boy (rarely a girl) and usually feeds her husband, i.e. the child's father, his flesh. The boy is reborn, usually (at first) in the form of a bird that tells the story of what happened. Cf. motif K80A. Traditions in which the boy is killed by his own mother are highlighted in bold.

Title: Grown from the remains of the slain.
Summary: A boy is killed and eaten. His sister gathers his remains, from which a tree grows, and on it â€“ the dead boy, often in the form of a bird.

Title: Ivico's cranes, ATU 960, 960A.
Summary: Before dying, the murderer's victim turns to birds (stars, animals, plants, etc.). Later, seeing these birds (the moon, the sun, this plant, etc.), the murderer recalls his deed aloud or otherwise gives himself away. Or the birds, being the only witnesses to the crime, lead the investigators to the murderers.

Title: Melon and severed head, ATU 780C.
Summary: Someone brings meat or fruit to another person or keeps it for themselves. At the decisive moment, the food turns into the remains of a (supposedly) murdered person. The owner is executed or is about to be executed. Cf. motif K168A.

Title: Those who find treasure kill each other, ATU 763.
Summary: Two (or more) people find (steal) valuables. Unwilling to share, one kills the other, but dies himself, poisoned by the poison that the victim manages to slip into his food.

Title: A name helps solve a murder.
Summary: Before his death, a man asks his murderer to tell his pregnant wife to give their newborn a certain name. Upon hearing the unusual name of the child, a powerful figure begins to investigate the case, and the murderer confesses to his crime. (All texts containing motifs K80c3 and K80c4 also contain the more general motif K80c)

Title: Silent witnesses to crime, ATU 960, 960A.
Summary: In a deserted place, one person kills another. After some time, he is exposed thanks to facts and circumstances that do not seem important and do not directly tell about the crime (the victim's last words; objects or living beings that were or appeared at the scene of the murder). (All texts containing motifs K80c3 and K80c4 also contain the more general motif K80c).

Title: The stuck pin.
Summary: A young woman or man is enchanted (turned into a bird, animal, immobilised) when a pin or other sharp object is stuck into their body.

Title: Bezruchka, ATU 706.
Summary: For a minor offence or on false charges, a young woman is maimed and expelled from her home (rarely: she is killed or maims herself). The cripple miraculously recovers (the dead woman is resurrected).

Title: Bezrucha in the prince's garden.
Summary: A girl with severed hands comes to a fruit tree (garden) to find food. Seeing her there, the prince takes her as his wife.

Title: The evil sister-in-law.
Summary: A man's wife or another woman tries to destroy his sister.

Title: Pregnancy from snake eggs.
Summary: A malevolent woman forces a woman to swallow a snake egg (snake, something else) so that a man will think that the woman is pregnant out of wedlock (rarely: so that snakes will suck the juices out of her). Cf. motif L89.

Title: Sick Father, ATU 550, 551.
Summary: To heal, rejuvenate or save one's father, father-in-law or sister, one must bring medicine (bring a doctor) from a distant country. The medicine is brought and the sick person recovers.

Title: Where the father did not go.
Summary: To fulfil the task, the character's sons must travel to a place where he has never been (or once was).

Title: Sisters married to animals, ATU 552.1.
Summary: A young man gives his sisters to the first ones who come to woo them (less often, unknown creatures kidnap the sisters one by one, demanding a ransom for them). These are animals or demons, which then usually help him.

Title: Give to the first person who asks.
Summary: On his deathbed, a father instructs his son, without specifying any conditions, to give his sister (sisters) to whoever comes for her.

Title: Horse brothers.
Summary: The antagonist owns the fastest horse. The hero obtains an even faster horse (usually the brother or sister of this horse), which is the only one that surpasses the antagonist's horse and usually orders the antagonist to throw off his rider.

Title: The horse-thought and the horse-wind.
Summary: When assessing the speed of a horse, the speed of thought (lightning, or something else) and wind are compared.

Title: Three-legged horse.
Summary: The three-legged horse is distinguished by its strength and speed, and is ridden by a rider of non-human nature.

Title: Four legs are faster than three.
Summary: A three-legged horse is strong and fast, but its four-legged brother is faster.

Title: A horse whose skin cannot be bitten through.
Summary: Covered with skins (coated with resin and sprinkled with sand, etc.), the mighty horse becomes invulnerable to the bites of other horses.

Title: Sea horses.
Summary: Magical horses live in water.

Title: The Crying Child.
Summary: A small (usually capricious) child is ignored, sent away from home, abandoned on the road, or given to another person for a time. As a result, the child is carried away by an animal or a spirit.

Title: Marriage to an animal ends badly.
Summary: A woman becomes the wife of an animal (rarely another non-human creature). The husband takes care of her, but the marriage ends with the murder of the husband, the woman, their offspring, the woman's relatives, the transformation of the woman herself into an animal, leading to hostility between humans and animals, etc.

Title: The stolen boy.
Summary: A forest woman receives or kidnaps a little boy and raises him to be her lover.

Title: The child is handed over.
Summary: A demonic woman asks the baby's mother to let her hold him or secretly replaces another person who was supposed to take the child. Once she has the baby, the demon takes him away.

Title: A woman steps in bear droppings.
Summary: A woman is picking berries, steps in bear droppings, and scolds the bears. The offended bear takes her away and marries her.

Title: Two Travellers (Truth and Falsehood), ATU 613.
Summary: Two people set off on a journey or argue about which is stronger: truth or falsehood (stinginess or generosity, etc.). The evil one abandons the good one, crippling or robbing him, but the good one regains his health and achieves success. The villain usually perishes.

Title: Blinded heroine, ATU 404.
Summary: The stepmother (aunt, rival) blinds a young woman. The latter regains her eyesight (often by exchanging them for some valuable item).

Title: Food in exchange for eyes.
Summary: The character suffers from thirst or hunger. His companion promises to share water or food with him (to make him rich) if he allows himself to be blinded.

Title: The blood of a dog will cure the princess.
Summary: The character learns that the blood (brain, etc.) of the dog guarding the neighbouring herd will cure the princess (prince). He uses this medicine and is rewarded.

Title: The girl and the witch: gifts from relatives.
Summary: After getting married, the heroine and her rival (witch, frog) must bring gifts from their relatives. The heroine finds her brother, brothers or sister who went missing at the beginning of the story and receives rich gifts from them, while the gifts brought by her rival are worthless.

Title: Where to leave the sister?
Summary: Having escaped danger, the girl or boy goes with their sister or brother. The sister or brother is crippled, rejects a number of places where they are to be left, and remains in the last place offered. See motif K89.

Title: The brother left on the tree.
Summary: At the beginning of the story, the sister parts with her brothers (or one brother), who die, remain on trees, on a hill, ascend to the sky, etc. Usually, after a successful marriage, the sister meets her brothers again, who have acquired superhuman nature.

Title: Brother-helper is married to a bear.
Summary: A girl parts with her brother or sister. He or she becomes the wife or husband of a bear and helps the girl.

Title: Hides, turning into a needle.
Summary: Left alone in the house or finding herself in a stranger's house, a girl (less often a male character) hides by turning into a needle (a pin) or another tool for sewing or spinning.

Title: Black and red, (ATU 156B*).
Summary: A person sees two opposing monsters or animals (usually of contrasting colours: red and black, black and white) and helps one of them, or one of the combatants helps the person. (Cf. ATU 156B, 738).

Title: Aimed at the black one, hit the white one.
Summary: Seeing two snakes of contrasting colours fighting, a man tries to strike one, but accidentally hits the other. The relatives of this snake gather to punish him, but upon learning what happened, they reward him.

Title: Deer antlers in the dragon's mouth.
Summary: The antlers of a deer or the tusks of an elephant, which a snake or dragon is trying to swallow, get stuck in its mouth.

Title: The invisible battle.
Summary: Dogs, the hero's horse, or the hero himself fight the enemy in the underworld. Those watching from a distance judge the course of the battle by the colour of the water or foam rising to the surface, the colour of the first animal to emerge, etc.

Title: King Lear, ATU 923, 923B.
Summary: The father asks his children a question, the answer to which seems obvious (does his daughter love him, who is the eldest in the family, etc.). The youngest daughter (less often – son) gives an unexpected answer, the father drives her away (deprives her of her inheritance), and later becomes convinced of her intelligence and nobility.

Title: A woman builds a house, ATU 923B.
Summary: A girl who has been driven from her home or has become the wife of an insignificant pauper becomes rich and respected.

Title: I love you like salt, ATU 923.
Summary: A daughter tells her father (rarely her brother) that she loves him like salt (or that salt is more important than him, etc.). He sends his daughter away (gets angry with his sister), but then realises she is right.

Title: The wife weaves, the husband sells.
Summary: A princess or sorceress turns out to be the wife of a poor man. She weaves or embroiders a scarf (or other item) and sends her husband to sell it. This marks the beginning of their path to success.

Title: Twins and a woman, ATU 303.
Summary: After a series of adventures and victories, the hero finds himself in trouble. His twin or brother follows in his footsteps, meets the same characters, but when he encounters the final enemy, he defeats him and revives (frees) the hero.

Title: Sword on the marriage bed, T351.
Summary: When lying down with a woman, a man places a sharp or pointed object between her and himself as a sign that he will abstain from sex during the night (sometimes the woman places the sword herself).

Title: Conception from eaten fish.
Summary: After eating fish, a childless woman gives birth to a boy or twins.

Title: Conception from an eaten fruit.
Summary: A childless woman conceives a child after eating a fruit (usually an apple; in northern traditions also cabbage, eggs, peas, etc., in India – mangoes).

Title: Boys, foals, puppies: born together.
Summary: To have a child, a woman eats fish, an apple or something else. Part of it (often the peel, broth, skin, etc.) is eaten by a mare, dog or other animals. The woman gives birth to a son (twins), the mare to a foal (foals), the dog to a puppy (puppies).

Title: A woman, a mare, and a dog give birth to boys.
Summary: When a woman gives birth to a son, at the same time a mare (dog, and/or other domestic animals) give birth to a boy. These boys grow up together and then set off on a journey.

Title: Disguised as a puppy.
Summary: The character infiltrates the enemy camp disguised as a kitten or puppy. Usually, one of the enemies suspects deception, but the others believe that the cute animal is harmless.

Title: A sword grown in the garden.
Summary: The fish eaten by the woman gives birth to sons, and what is buried in the garden are objects or items that are further associated with these young men. These are either weapons (swords, sabres, rapiers) or objects whose appearance allows one to judge what is happening to the young men.

Title: The bird of happiness (eaten head), ATU 567, 567A.
Summary: Those who eat a miraculous bird, fish, animal or fruit gain wealth and power.

Title: Together and after death, ATU 970.
Summary: Two people who love each other (usually a man and a woman) die prematurely and are buried in the same grave or nearby. After or during the burial, something unusual happens that is connected with the story (special plants grow in that place, the smoke from the two funeral pyres joins together, the dead turn into two birds, two stars, etc.).

Title: Burdock among rose bushes.
Summary: The lovers are buried in the same grave or nearby. Two plants grow in this place, reaching towards each other, and between them is a thorny bush, embodying the character who separated the lovers.

Title: Fifty Sons, ATU 303A.
Summary: Several (more than three) brothers marry or must marry in such a way that their wives are sisters.

Title: Tested fear, ATU 537.
Summary: A man prepares to kill a large bird, but does not kill it. When the bird later carries him, it pretends to leave him on a rock or throw him down. In doing so, it makes it clear how frightened it was. Either the bird first drops and catches the man, and later he makes her experience fear herself (the Volyn variant is slightly different).

Title: The slain man turns into a camp.
Summary: An animal or (less commonly) a woman who gave birth to a hero or helped him turns into a house and property.

Title: The Untold Dream, ATU 725.
Summary: A person dreams about an upcoming celebration for himself or a member of his family (rarely: he daydreams about it). Either another person buys the dream and becomes the protagonist of the story, or the person who saw it hides its content from everyone, or he is persecuted for excessive conceit, as evidenced by the content of the dream. The meaning of the dream is revealed at the end of the story. Often, the young man ascends to the throne and marries the heiresses of two kingdoms (in the dream, these were two suns or the sun and the moon).

Title: Father will serve his son, ATU 517, (725).
Summary: A young man or woman (often after having a dream) declares that a great future awaits him or her (usually that his or her father, parents, brothers, or sisters will show him or her signs of respect). The young man or woman is expelled, but the prophecy comes true.

Title: The condemned riddle-solver is freed.
Summary: A man thrown into prison is released and exalted because he alone manages to solve the riddles set by the king or save the princess (king, prince, etc.).

Title: The sold dream. 26.29.30.32.33.
Summary: One person has a dream, and another buys it and obtains what was predicted in the dream.

Title: Happy dream: sun, moon and stars.
Summary: A person sees the sun, moon and stars (all together or some of them) in a dream. At the end of the story, the meaning of the dream becomes clear: these are people who love or worship him (often two wives and a child).

Title: Midnight escape: change of partner, (ATU 856).
Summary: A girl and a young man agree that he will take her away at night. The young man is late or falls asleep, and the girl is taken away by someone else who happens to be at the appointed place.

Title: The Faithful Servant, ATU 516.
Summary: A person learns about the dangers threatening another (and usually that by warning his friend/master, he will turn to stone). The person eliminates the dangers, despite the fact that his behaviour upsets the person he has saved.

Title: Tobiah, (ATU 505).
Summary: Setting off on a journey, a young man releases a caught fish or animal, or he or his father does someone a favour. As a reward for their help, a person or creature in the guise of a stranger or animal comes to the young man, becomes his companion and protector.

Title: The Grateful Dead Man, ATU 505.
Summary: A person helps to bury a dead man (pays his remaining debt, honours a saint). The revived dead man (saint) helps him overcome difficulties. See motif K100A.

Title: The snake bites the girl's suitors, ATU 507 (main part, variant 2).
Summary: A woman (rarely a young man) does not know that inside her (him) there is something dangerous for her (his) marriage partner (usually a snake), or that on her wedding night she will turn into a snake, or that a snake will crawl in on her wedding night. The hero or his companion eliminates the danger. {Motif K100C is similar to F9f1, but the latter belongs to the cosmological-etiological category and is associated with the idea of a dangerous woman, while K100C is adventurous}.

Title: The helper turns out to be a prince, ATU 314.
Summary: At the end of the story, the animal helper (horse, lion, etc.) turns into a prince (princess) itself.

Title: Dangerous tales.
Summary: Fairy tales act as separate characters: they usually try to harm people, believing that a certain person does not treat them with due respect. Cf. motif L94d, "The Tale with a Tail".

Title: The young man releases the fish.
Summary: A man catches an unusual fish (rarely: a bird or some kind of aquatic creature). His son (a worker) releases it. For this, the father (king) drives him away, or the one who released the fish leaves on his own. The rescued fish helps him.

Title: The Wild Man, ATU 502.
Summary: A man (king) catches a strange (anthropomorphic) creature. His son releases the wondrous captive (after which he flees from his father's wrath or is banished). The freed captive helps him. Cf. motif K161.

Title: The thirst-quenched breaks his chains.
Summary: A captured supernatural character breaks his chains and escapes to freedom after being given water (or wine, etc.) to drink.

Title: Sacrifice a son, (ATU 516C).
Summary: In order to revive or heal a friend (to heal oneself, to fulfil a vow), the character agrees to sacrifice his son (children). The slain person usually comes back to life, or the person's willingness to make the sacrifice is sufficient to satisfy supernatural forces.

Title: The test of gratitude, ATU 750D, 751C*.
Summary: A supernatural character fulfils the wishes of one or more people and later visits them again. The beneficiary or most of them turn out to be ungrateful and chase him away. In response, the character deprives them of what they have gained.

Title: Intoxication and immobilisation of a strongman.
Summary: A powerful character loses his strength (self-control) after being intoxicated and then admits that the hop is stronger than him. (See Neklyudov 2025a; 2025b).

Title: Night dances of girls, ATU 306.
Summary: A girl or boy disappears at night. Usually, the girl's clothes or shoes are worn out overnight, or the boy looks sick and tired in the morning. The girl or boy is followed and seen spending the night in another world.

Title: The girl rising from the coffin, ATU 307.
Summary: A man spends several nights next to a dead girl who has become a dangerous demonic creature. As a result, the girl is exorcised.

Title: Three Nights of Trials, (ATU 400).
Summary: A girl or young man is freed from a spell after the hero endures three nights of torment or fear inflicted by demons. The girl or young man themselves are not dangerous to the hero; they help him.

Title: Black becomes white.
Summary: The enchanted character (the castle where the action takes place) gradually changes its appearance over several days as the spell wears off: it acquires human features, turning from black to white, from ugly to beautiful.

Title: By day in the palace, by night in the sky.
Summary: The bride stipulates that she will only be with her husband during the day. The husband discovers that at night she meets with heavenly maidens (and usually flies away to dance in the sky). He follows her and in the end she stays with him on earth.

Title: The hero's woman helps his enemy, ATU 315 (sister), 590 (mother).
Summary: A woman who is initially friendly to the hero (his sister, mother, less often his wife or lover) then tries to destroy him by acting in concert with his enemy. To this end, she persuades the hero to take actions that are fatal to him.

Title: Father knew what he was doing.
Summary: A man orders the killing of a young man's sister, wife or mother. The young man does not allow such an order to be carried out, and then repents of this.

Title: Imaginary grave.
Summary: To hide the truth, a person buries an animal or an inanimate object and says that the grave supposedly contains the remains of another person's wife (bride, mother, daughter, sister, children).

Title: Conflict between son and mother.
Summary: The mother seeks to destroy her son (children) because he interferes with her love affair. Cf. motif L86: Children flee from their demon mother.

Title: Dead tooth.
Summary: Someone (usually a woman) places a poisonous tooth (bone, nail, etc.) in the hero's bed. The young man dies, but is then revived.

Title: The wolf across the river.
Summary: A hostile young character is located behind a water barrier. The young man's sister or mother helps him cross and becomes his lover.

Title: Fill the vessel with tears.
Summary: A woman must fill one or two vessels with tears (less often with blood). Usually, after this, her punishment must end, or the punishment depends on which of the vessels contains more tears.

Title: The enemy and a woman blind the hero.
Summary: The hero's wife, sister or mother participates in a conspiracy against him and helps to blind him.

Title: Ride for the last time, B184.1.6.
Summary: In order to destroy the hero (heroine), the antagonist must first get rid of his beloved animal (usually a horse). When the animal is about to be slaughtered, the hero (heroine) mounts it, rides away and escapes.

Title: Having changed his appearance, the hero recovers the magical object (ATU 318).
Summary: The enemy seizes the object that makes the hero invulnerable and kills him. The hero is revived. Changing his appearance, he provokes the enemy to put the magical object on the ground, seizes it again and kills the enemy.

Title: A splinter turns into a duck.
Summary: The enemy systematically destroys the objects and creatures into which the hero is reincarnated. The hero wins after turning from a splinter into a waterfowl (duck, goose).

Title: The cow as helper, ATU 511.
Summary: A domestic animal (horse, cow, bull, goat, ram, sheep) helps an orphan, a lonely child, or an unfortunate young woman.

Title: The tree raises its branches.
Summary: A suddenly grown plant (tree, vine, lotus) bends (raises its branches, etc.), allowing only the hero or heroine to climb it or pick its fruits (flowers).

Title: The tree follows its mistress.
Summary: A tree that suddenly grows allows only the heroine to enjoy its fruits and follows her when she moves to a new place.

Title: The spinning cow.
Summary: A cow (goat) miraculously spins or weaves: it chews tow, turning it into thread, orders the yarn to be wound onto its horns, put into its ear, etc.

Title: The bull-helper fights in the copper forest.
Summary: Sitting on a bull or a cow, a young man or woman runs away from their stepmother's house. Along the way, the bull fights other bulls (monsters), the last of which usually kills it.

Title: Enter the horse's ear and take it out of the cow's ear.
Summary: An animal (rarely a demonic creature) orders the hero or heroine to retrieve necessary items from its ear or to enter its ear in order to transform, fall asleep, etc.

Title: The red swan.
Summary: The youngest of the brothers stays at home, wounds a red swan or duck, and follows its trail.

Title: The wonderful son and the rat children.
Summary: A despised wife gives birth to miraculous children, while other wives give birth to animals.

Title: Thrown to the cows.
Summary: The hero (a miraculous infant, a magical rooster) is thrown at the feet of animals, but they do not trample him.

Title: The Returned Husband, ATU 425A, 425B, 425D, 425E, 432.
Summary: A magical husband leaves his wife. She finds and returns him.

Title: Wear out iron shoes, Q502.2.
Summary: Before reaching their goal, the character must wear out iron shoes or an iron staff.

Title: The head of the household brings the promised gifts, (ATU 425C).
Summary: When the head of the household leaves on business, those left behind ask him to bring them gifts. The elders ask for something of obvious value (usually clothing and jewellery), while the youngest ask for something unusual and, at first glance, of little value (a flower, a bird, etc.). As a result, it is the youngest who, having overcome trials, achieves success in life.

Title: Shepherdess instead of princess.
Summary: A nobleman (king) is forced to promise his daughter or son to a demon (monster, predatory beast). He tries to replace her or him with other girls or boys, but this does not work.

Title: Beauty and the Beast, ATU 425C.
Summary: When her father leaves, the daughter asks him to bring her a flower (leaf, etc.). The father picks it in the garden of an enchanted prince who has a monstrous appearance. The monster demands the daughter from her father and, thanks to the girl, regains his princely appearance.

Title: The daughter asks for a magical groom to be brought to her.
Summary: When her father leaves, the daughter asks him to bring her an object or creature that embodies a magical groom. The father does not understand the meaning of her request.

Title: Prohibition on lighting candles.
Summary: One spouse forbids the other from seeing them. When the other willingly or unwillingly breaks the prohibition, the first disappears (gets into trouble). (In the Tuscan version, the prohibition is broken by the woman's mother).

Title: Knives on the Window (Finist the Bright Falcon), ATU 432.
Summary: A magical spouse who arrives in the form of a bird or appears in some other way meets a woman. Jealous sisters (stepmother, brother, etc.) wound him (usually by placing razors, glass shards, etc. in his path). The wounded young man disappears, and the woman goes in search of him.

Title: Trying to wake up a wonderful spouse.
Summary: After overcoming difficulties, a girl (rarely a boy) finds a magical spouse, but at first cannot wake him (her) up.

Title: The magical wife cannot wake the young man.
Summary: Waiting for his magical wife, the young man falls asleep. The wife cannot wake him up and leaves (this episode is often repeated).

Title: Delayed childbirth.
Summary: A woman remains pregnant for many years and gives birth only after her wonderful husband, who has left her, or someone else allows her to do so.

Title: Blood on the shirt.
Summary: When a magical husband leaves his earthly wife, his shirt is stained with blood. Only his new wife manages to wash it clean.

Title: The revived wife cheats on her husband, ATU 612.
Summary: Wife dies, husband revives her, she leaves him for another man, punished.

Title: He who kills his wife loses everything.
Summary: A man acquires a magical wife. Another woman orders him to kill her or divorce her, then she will become his wife. Having fulfilled the request, he loses everything.

Title: Wife – puppy or object.
Summary: The hero is advised to ask supernatural characters for something insignificant (a puppy, a cup) in return for his service. What he receives turns out to be the daughter of a deity. Another character unsuccessfully tries to take the hero's wife away from him.

Title: Reflection of the golden sword.
Summary: The character is asked to retrieve treasure from the bottom of a pond. He does not understand that he is only seeing a reflection and that the treasure is located above.

Title: Animal suitors rejected, Sun accepted.
Summary: The girl's mother consistently rejects birds and animals that propose to her daughter, but accepts the proposal of a heavenly anthropomorphic character.

Title: The worker takes revenge on the Sun.
Summary: A man accuses the Sun and other characters responsible for the weather, wild animals, etc. of causing him to lose his property; he punishes his offenders.

Title: Animal princess, ATU 402.
Summary: Young men (usually three brothers) find wives (usually by shooting arrows or other objects at random, see motif K113A). The wife of the youngest brother is initially ugly or appears in the form of an animal (often a frog or snake), but turns out to be a beauty and a sorceress. Alternatively, the girls choose their husbands, and the wife of the youngest brother is a sorceress.

Title: The bride where the arrow fell.
Summary: A young man throws an object, shoots an arrow, etc. Where the arrow lands (where the object falls), the young man finds a wife or a means of obtaining one.

Title: The Frog Princess – Mistress of the Storm.
Summary: The younger prince marries a frog. She must first arrive at his parents' house. A thunderstorm begins. Rain, lightning, and thunder signify that the prince's wife is washing, dressing, travelling, etc.

Title: Brothers leave after the birth of their sister (ATU 451).
Summary: Several brothers leave home immediately after or shortly before their mother gives birth to a girl (usually they want a brother and wait for news about who their mother has given birth to, but accidentally or maliciously a signal is given that a boy has been born). The girl grows up and goes in search of her brothers.

Title: Spider web at the entrance, B523.1, ATU 967.
Summary: When a character hides in a shelter, a spider immediately weaves a web at the entrance. Enemies decide that no one has entered the cave or room for a long time and leave.

Title: Dove at the entrance.
Summary: When a character hides in a shelter, a dove builds a nest there. The enemies decide that no one has entered the cave or room for a long time and leave.

Title: Choosing a companion (ATU 516C).
Summary: To choose an assistant, a young man asks the candidates to perform simple tasks (eat bread, set off on a journey). The behaviour of the chosen candidate shows that he will take care of the hero, while the behaviour of the others shows that they will only think of themselves.

Title: Nesmeyana (the disguised tsar perishes).
Summary: The king takes or is about to take the poor man's wife. She suggests that the king put on clothes that are not his own (usually those that belonged to her husband). After that, the king is killed by his own soldiers (dogs), who believe him to be a poor man (jester, devil).

Title: A dog instead of a beauty in the chest.
Summary: In order to take possession of the girl, the antagonist creates a situation in which her relatives are forced to put her in a chest (barrel, sack, etc.) and leave her there. The girl is secretly replaced by a ferocious dog or other animal. When the antagonist opens the chest, the animal usually kills or mauls him.

Title: The father was persuaded to leave his daughter in a chest, ATU 896.
Summary: In order to take possession of the girl, the priest arranges for her father to agree to place her in a chest (barrel) and lower it into the river (leave it in a deserted area).

Title: Nesmeyana (bride, young man), ATU 559, (571).
Summary: A woman will marry the man who makes her laugh; a man promises a reward to anyone who makes his daughter, mother or son laugh.

Title: Making the silent speak.
Summary: A girl who is constantly silent is promised to the one who can make her speak; or a husband struggles to make his magical wife speak.

Title: Stuck Together, ATU 571, 571B.
Summary: The hero causes various people (and animals) to stick to each other (or to objects).

Title: Dancing against their will, ATU 592.
Summary: When a character plays a pipe (violin, horn, etc.), people and animals begin to dance against their will.

Title: To play before death.
Summary: A man sentenced to death asks to be given something from his possessions, usually a musical instrument. Once he has it, he gains power over those gathered and is saved.

Title: Two in bed with the princess, ATU 850.
Summary: The princess, lying between two suitors, must choose blindly the one she likes best. The suitor of low birth arranges things so that his noble rival emits a foul odour (while he himself emits a pleasant fragrance). The princess turns to him.

Title: The forbidden room, C611.
Summary: Upon leaving, the character allows another to take charge of the house, but not to look into a certain room or container. The other violates the prohibition.

Title: Portrait of an unknown beauty.
Summary: Upon seeing the portrait of a beauty, a man strives to meet her.

Title: Animal marries a princess, ATU 545B.
Summary: An animal promises to make a poor man rich (usually by marrying him to a rich bride; or by marrying a poor girl to a prince) and, resorting to deception, fulfils its promise.

Title: The Ungrateful Master.
Summary: An animal saves a human, does him a favour, and he humiliates or kills it. See motifs K119, M161.

Title: Animals as gifts to the king.
Summary: After tricking wild animals, the fox brings them to the king as a gift from her rich master.

Title: Tsar-Thunder and Tsarina-Lightning.
Summary: The antagonist believes that he has been attacked by the lord of thunder (the father of the bride, whom a zoomorphic assistant has tricked into marrying a poor young man, motif K119).

Title: Puss in Boots.
Summary: A cat helps a poor young man marry a princess (a girl marry a prince).

Title: The Miller: A Success Story.
Summary: The poor young man who was helped by an animal assistant, who presented him to the king as a rich man, is a miller or a miller's son.

Title: Prevented incest (daughter and father), (ATU 510B, 510B*), 706C.
Summary: The girl's father (rarely: stepfather) intends to marry her (since she is the only one who meets the requirements for a bride). Usually, the girl manages to avoid the marriage.

Title: Prevented incest (sister and brother), (ATU 313E).
Summary: A man is going to marry his sister (often it turns out that she is the only one who meets the requirements for a bride). Usually, the girl manages to avoid such a marriage.

Title: Three dresses, (ATU 510B).
Summary: To get rid of an unwanted suitor (her own father, brother, monster), a girl demands that he obtain a dress for her (usually three dresses in succession) made of unusual material (gold, fly wings, etc.), and when the condition is fulfilled, she runs away.

Title: Not by her mother, but by her mother-in-law.
Summary: Family members want to marry their daughter off to a man who is unacceptable to her (usually they want to marry her off to her own brother). The girl refuses to address her father, mother, etc. as close relatives, but calls them in-laws (mother-in-law, sister-in-law, etc.) or enemies; or the relatives themselves demand that the girl address them as in-laws.

Title: Dress in a nut.
Summary: The character receives a nut containing valuables (beautiful clothes, jewellery, animal helpers, etc.), or (Germans, Latvians) hides the valuables in the nut himself to use them later.

Title: Fill the vessel with tears.
Summary: The character must fill a vessel with tears (pour them on the floor).

Title: Luring a woman onto a ship.
Summary: To obtain a woman, a man lures her onto a ship (boat, flying machine, etc.) and takes her away.

Title: The knight at the crossroads.
Summary: At the crossroads, it is indicated that one road is safe, another is neutral, and the third is deadly dangerous. There can only be two roads – dangerous and safe. The hero travels along the dangerous road.

Title: The queen of the other world finds the hero (ATU 551).
Summary: Having penetrated the world of a powerful woman, unattainable without the support of supernatural helpers, the man returns. The deceiver tries to take credit for the feat. The woman whom the hero met in her world finds him and punishes (rejects) the deceiver.

Title: The old woman's curse.
Summary: A boy, a young man, or, less commonly, a girl deliberately or accidentally offends an elderly woman (or a cripple). She utters words that cause him or her to want to do something dangerous (most often to find a marriage partner).

Title: The broken jug.
Summary: A boy or young man accidentally, or more often out of mischief, breaks or overturns a vessel belonging to a woman or girl. This episode forms the basis of the rest of the story.

Title: Broken spinning wheel.
Summary: A boy or young man damages an elderly woman's spinning wheel or yarn. This episode forms the basis of the rest of the story.

Title: It's not a miracle!
Summary: An animal killed by a hunter runs away. The animal itself or someone else explains that this is not a miracle (or that it is not a tragedy), but that the real miracle (tragedy) happened somewhere else. A story about what happened follows.

Title: One of the subjects is a traitor.
Summary: The pursuer asks various objects where the hero is hiding or where he has run. Everyone remains silent, but one of the objects betrays the hero.

Title: The wolf pays for the horse it ate.
Summary: A predatory beast or demon eats the hero's horse, but in return is forced or voluntarily helps him.

Title: Animal brothers, ATU 451.
Summary: A girl has many brothers, who are turned into birds or animals (rarely: into plants; killed by witchcraft), then usually disenchanted (brought back to life; usually all of them, in the Georgian version – one). See motif K127A.

Title: The silent heroine.
Summary: The heroine must remain silent for a long time and therefore cannot respond to the accusations. They want to execute her, but at that moment the restrictions expire and she is saved.

Title: Brothers turned into oxen.
Summary: A group of brothers are turned into bulls (oxen) and then enchanted.

Title: Graze without loss.
Summary: A character orders the hero to graze animals (or birds) and promises to execute him (deprive him of his reward) if even one animal is lost. Cf. K128B (ATU 570).

Title: The best apples for the princess, ATU 610.
Summary: Each of the three brothers brings the princess (prince) a gift of fruit (less often fish, etc.) and encounters a character who punishes rudeness and rewards politeness. As a result (after additional trials), the youngest brother enters into the desired marriage.

Title: The Hare Shepherd, ATU 570.
Summary: The ruler will give his daughter to the one who can herd (gather, train) hares (squirrels, sheep, poultry, partridges) without loss. A poor young man accomplishes the task with the help of a magic device. To have an excuse to refuse, the ruler's family members try to buy one hare (a magic pipe, etc.) so that the suitor cannot fulfil his promise, but as a result they find themselves in a humiliating position.

Title: Enchanted and brought to life, ATU 709, 709A.
Summary: (Due to the intrigues of an antagonist) a girl falls into a deep swoon, but is not dead. A male character of high status (either the girl's spouse or blood relative) revives her. {In sub-Saharan Africa, except for Swahili, borrowing from Europeans is more likely than from Arabs}.

Title: Half-living in the tomb.
Summary: A young woman (lying in a tomb) comes back to life, then appears dead again, but is ultimately freed from the spell.

Title: Who is the sweetest in the world?
Summary: A woman (rarely: a man) asks who is the most beautiful of all and receives the answer that she (he) is. One day she (he) is told that someone else is more beautiful.

Title: The Girl in the Brothers' House, (ATU 709A).
Summary: Several young men (brothers) live far away from other people. A girl comes to them, or she is miraculously born in their house, and they treat her like a sister. After some time, the girl finds herself in danger, but is ultimately saved.

Title: Three Wonderful Objects, ATU 518.
Summary: Certain characters argue over the possession of magical objects, but the objects go to the hero. Usually, he suggests that the disputants race each other or asks them to let him try out the objects, after which he hides, taking the objects with him.

Title: The hero divides the carcass, ATU 159*.
Summary: Several animals (often a lion, a falcon, an ant) argue (usually over prey or habitat). The hero resolves their dispute, and they grant him the ability to take on their form (to possess their qualities).

Title: Magical objects exchanged and returned, ATU 569.
Summary: Having received and then lost a magical object, the hero returns it with the help of a new one (a club, a box with an army, etc.), received in exchange for the first or obtained by the hero's brother. The episode may be repeated several times.

Title: The kidnapped woman runs away while the archers compete.
Summary: A woman offers her captors to shoot arrows – she will marry the winner. While they are figuring out whose arrow flew farther, the kidnapped woman runs away.

Title: Seven-league boots.
Summary: Mention is made of footwear that allows the character to quickly cover enormous distances.

Title: The Invincible Rooster, ATU 715, 715A.
Summary: A small character (usually a rooster) comes to a powerful enemy. Thanks to creatures and objects that he encounters along the way and hides in his body or bag, the character remains unharmed after all attempts to destroy him. Cf. motif L126.

Title: The husband's rooster and the wife's hen, ATU 219E*, 715A.
Summary: The husband (rarely: the wife) sends the rooster out to earn money, and it brings back money. The wife (husband) sends the hen (cat, her half of the rooster, etc.) and receives only mice, filth, etc. Or, instead of money, the rooster brings the wife something bad or nothing at all.

Title: The exhausted horse.
Summary: A man notices that his horse (donkey) looks tired and learns that an animal or demonic creature is riding it. Cf. motif M182a.

Title: Found treasures.
Summary: A guest is planted with treasure in order to accuse him of theft.

Title: Seven with one blow, ATU 1640.
Summary: By accidentally defeating powerful opponents, a physically weak and timid person gains honour.

Title: The coward put out the door.
Summary: The coward or lazybones has become so tiresome to his family that they leave him outside. He sets off on a journey and defeats powerful enemies, thanks to chance or cunning.

Title: The young man and the cows.
Summary: The young man turns out to be the owner and leader of a herd of cattle, and with his herd of cows or buffaloes he is summoned to the king (usually after his hair is found by the princess).

Title: The girl's floating hair.
Summary: Seeing the girl's hair carried away by the water, the man decides to marry the girl to whom the hair belongs.

Title: The young man's hair carried away by the water.
Summary: Seeing the young man's hair carried away by the water, a woman decides to marry the owner of the hair.

Title: Rubies from the river, (ATU 467).
Summary: A character finds precious stones or unusual flowers (usually in a river) and learns where they come from.

Title: Sometimes alive, sometimes dead.
Summary: Upon leaving, the demon temporarily kills or puts the girl to sleep, and upon returning, revives her.

Title: Two flutes.
Summary: A young man receives two flutes (pipes, horns) from a cow (buffalo), which produce different effects when played (joy and sorrow, prosperity and a call for help, etc.).

Title: Sister brings women to revive her brother.
Summary: The brother is killed, the sister, dressed in her brother's clothes and disguised as a young man, finds women who are able to revive the dead, puts her brother's clothes back on his body, and the women who have come revive him. Or the sister is killed, the brother lures women capable of reviving the dead, puts his clothes on his dead sister, the women think it is their husband, and revive the girl.

Title: A girl disguised as a young man finds a wife for her brother.
Summary: The brother is killed. The sister, dressed in his clothes, finds a woman. The brother comes back to life, the sister puts on women's clothes again, and the woman believes that the girl's brother was the one who married her.

Title: Body swap (king and vizier), ATU 678.
Summary: A person gains the ability to revive the dead by incarnating in their body. While they remain in it, their own body is dead. Another person takes the body of the first, leaving them with the body of an animal.

Title: The burnt pheasant.
Summary: A servant is so struck by the beauty of a girl (rarely: a boy) that he lets the meat or bread intended for his master burn.

Title: Demonstratively ungrateful.
Summary: Travelling with his sister or brother, the young man regularly kills his saviours and helpers, exposing himself to ever new dangers.

Title: Tamed mischievous sisters.
Summary: Supernatural women harm people. The hero tames them and usually takes them as wives.

Title: Burying one dead man three times, ATU 1536B.
Summary: After killing several people, a man asks a gravedigger to bury the dead and each time says that the dead man has returned. The gravedigger buries everyone, but believes that there is only one dead man.

Title: The bird catcher hero.
Summary: The protagonist of the narrative is a bird catcher or bird hunter, or the son of a bird catcher (hunter).

Title: Predicted death by an animal, ATU 934A, 934B.
Summary: When the animal, object, or person that was supposed to cause the character's death has already died or is far away, the character's remains or images become the cause of death.

Title: Predicted death by a wolf, ATU 934B*.
Summary: A person is predicted to be torn apart by a wolf or to die during a wedding. The prediction turns out to be true. In the case of a wedding, the bride turns into a wolf and kills the groom.

Title: The image kills.
Summary: A person is predicted to die at the hands of an animal. He is killed (or attempted to be killed) by a living image of an animal or a statue in the form of an animal that falls on him.

Title: The newlywed eats her groom.
Summary: After a man and a woman are left alone (usually on their wedding night), the woman turns into a predator or monster and eats the man.

Title: The hero is revived by the remedy he was sent to fetch.
Summary: The hero is sent to fetch a remedy that can cure the sick or revive the dead. On the way back, a woman who is friendly to the hero keeps part of the remedy (or all of it, replacing it with a fake) and, when the hero is treacherously killed, revives him.

Title: The horse brings the hero's remains, and he is revived.
Summary: The enemy dismembers the hero's body. The remains are tied to the horse's saddle, or the horse itself picks them up and brings them to friendly characters. They revive the hero.

Title: Missing foals.
Summary: Every night or every year, a mare gives birth to a foal, and every time someone steals it.

Title: Three knots.
Summary: The character has a rope or reins with three knots, allowing him to move faster or slower. Usually, untying the first and second knots causes the character's ship to sail faster (thanks to the rising wind) or his horse to gallop faster; however, contrary to the warning, the character (when almost reaching the goal) also unties the third knot and as a result loses the ship, the horse, ends up not where he wanted to be, etc.

Title: The horse eats coals.
Summary: A magical horse (rarely: dog) eats (hot) coals, nails, etc., or attempts are made to feed these to the horse.

Title: The Golden Fish, ATU 555.
Summary: A magical helper grants a poor man's simple wish. The poor man or his wife ask for more and more. In the end, the helper punishes the beggar (usually by taking away everything that was given). {Many references to texts outside Europe in Uther 2004 are not related to the plot of ATU 555 and do not contain the K151 motif. This applies in particular to the Arabic and Ossetian variants}.

Title: The devil runs away in terror, ATU 1164.
Summary: A man saves a devil who is suffering from the proximity of a certain character or object. To reward his saviour, the devil promises to possess a princess and leave her when the man comes to treat her. The devil either breaks his promise or warns the man not to try to cure those whom the devil will possess later. The man informs the devil that the character or object he fears so much is approaching again. The devil flees and never returns.

Title: The Devil and His Wife in the Pit, ATU 1164.
Summary: A man saves a devil (snake, predator) suffering from the proximity of a certain character or object. To reward his saviour, the devil promises to possess a princess and leave her when the man comes to treat her. The devil either breaks his promise or warns the man not to try to cure those whom the devil will later possess. The man informs the devil that the character or object he fears so much is approaching again. The devil flees and never returns.

Title: Grateful animals and an evil man, ATU 160.
Summary: A man does a favour for several (potentially dangerous) animals and another man. The grateful animals help him, but the man betrays and harms him.

Title: Inscription on a skull.
Summary: A person finds a skull on which a mysterious and gloomy prophecy is written or which utters it. Then it becomes clear what it means.

Title: Men in the harem.
Summary: By solving a riddle, a boy or young man (rarely a girl) exposes the daughter, wife or assistants of an authoritative character: the daughter or wife has a lover; the assistant is plotting a conspiracy.

Title: The prince grew up in seclusion.
Summary: A person (usually a king) raises a son (daughter) in isolation. One day (usually by chance), the young man (woman) sees the outside world and leaves his (her) confinement.

Title: Bone in meat.
Summary: A man (usually a king) raises his daughter (less often his son) in a closed room, ordering her to be fed boneless meat. One day, a bone is found in the meat, and the girl (boy) uses it to make a hole in the wall and sees the outside world for the first time.

Title: A girl's hair serves as a rope to climb up (ATU 310).
Summary: A girl lets down her hair, which another character uses to climb up to her.

Title: The girl on the scales.
Summary: The father regularly weighs his daughter and learns of her pregnancy when she becomes heavier.

Title: Will the flowers under the pillow wilt?
Summary: A girl pretends to be a man. To determine who it really is, flowers are placed under the pillow or mattress. If a man is sleeping, they will remain fresh, but if a woman is sleeping, they will wilt by morning (or if a woman is sleeping, the milk left under the bed will sour).

Title: Trials: girl or boy?
Summary: People suspect that the young man is a girl in disguise. Tests are proposed to determine this, but the girl manages to avoid exposure (for a long time).

Title: A dog helps a girl remain unrecognised.
Summary: People suspect that the young man is a girl in disguise. She manages to avoid exposure thanks to a dog (rarely a cat) who learns how to determine his mistress's true gender and tells her about it.

Title: Robbers killed one by one, ATU 304.
Summary: The character lures his opponents out one by one and cuts off each one's head as soon as they appear. Less commonly, a multi-headed opponent sticks out its heads one by one, and the hero cuts them off.

Title: The tavern where they feed for free, ATU 425D, (ATU 304).
Summary: In order to find a missing husband (wife, saviour), the character regularly gathers random people to tell stories (usually keeping a shop, bathhouse, etc. for this purpose). From the conversations, it becomes clear that one of the visitors is the person they are looking for, or his story helps to find the missing person.

Title: Recognising the woman in the portrait, (ATU 881A).
Summary: In order to find her missing husband (and other men who helped her or caused her harm), a woman displays her image and calls to her those who, by their behaviour, show that they are familiar with the features in the portrait.

Title: Peas underfoot.
Summary: When two characters are fighting, someone nearby wants one of them to slip (while the other remains firmly on their feet) and throws something under their feet for this purpose.

Title: Getting Satan's Hair, ATU 461.
Summary: The hero is given the task of bringing back the hair, feathers, scales, etc. of a dangerous character. He does this with the help of the character's wife or mother.

Title: The demon's answers to his wife's questions, ATU 461.
Summary: A woman living in the house of a supernatural character hides a man who has come to her and asks the character questions, the answers to which the man must find out.

Title: The Released Dragon, (ATU 302C*).
Summary: A character who has deprived a dragon (demon, thunder) of its freedom orders others not to unlock the dungeon (not to enter a certain room, not to give the chained creature anything to drink, etc.). The prohibition is violated, the chained creature is freed, which leads to disaster. Cf. motif K100f1.

Title: The villain enters the bedroom (ATU 956B).
Summary: The antagonist (robber, sorcerer, witch) sneaks into the house of a girl or young woman, hiding inside a statue, in a wardrobe, etc., and/or putting her husband (guard, etc.) to sleep, but is destroyed at the last moment.

Title: Aladdin's Lamp, ATU 561.
Summary: A sorcerer orders a young man to retrieve a magical object (often a lamp) from a hard-to-reach place. The young man finds the object (but refuses to give it up), and the sorcerer grants his wishes.

Title: A wife is not a best friend, ATU 921B.
Summary: The person himself or someone else creates a situation in which he becomes convinced that his wife is not his best friend. Usually, the treacherous wife is contrasted with a loyal dog.

Title: Seeking to experience fear, ATU 326.
Summary: The young man has never experienced fear and wants to know what it is like. Robbers and evil spirits do not frighten him.

Title: Forty girls.
Summary: A group of girls forms a community or troop and acts independently of men. Cf. motif F39.

Title: The Child King.
Summary: A boy plays, pretending to be a king and demonstrating wisdom and/or magical abilities.

Title: The Tsarevich and the Blacksmith's Son, ATU 920.
Summary: The queen hates the son she is pregnant with and replaces him with the son (rarely – daughter) of a commoner, who raises the prince. The prince shows wisdom and becomes king.

Title: What is a lamb in the womb of a sheep?
Summary: A boy is able to determine the sex and colour of a young animal in the womb.

Title: Imaginary life in an instant, ATU 664*, 681.
Summary: A person experiences an eventful long period of life. Everything turns out to be an illusion, and he finds himself back in the same place and at the same moment in time from which the story began.

Title: Food turns into severed body parts, ATU 664*.
Summary: A person thinks that they are holding something intended for food (a calf's head, a melon, bread, etc.), but these objects turn into human heads or limbs. Cf. motif K80c1.

Title: The bewildered man became a bear.
Summary: A person makes another person believe that he has turned into a bear (wolf), found himself in the forest, etc. When he wakes up, the bewitched person finds himself where he was before.

Title: Pregnant doe.
Summary: The hunter spares the hunted animal, noticing that it is a pregnant female and remembering his own pregnant wife.

Title: Water without frogs, land without flies.
Summary: The character sets off in search of a place where there are no ordinary creatures that live everywhere (water without frogs, air without flies).

Title: The weaver creates an army.
Summary: The heroes fight, but the number of enemies does not decrease, because someone is constantly weaving (forging) new warriors.

Title: The deaf bride without arms and legs.
Summary: A man describes his daughter to a potential groom as ugly and crippled. The groom agrees to the marriage, and the bride turns out to be beautiful.

Title: It is better to suffer when young (Placidas), ATU 938.
Summary: A powerful and wealthy man loses everything, is separated from his wife and children, and they are separated from each other. The man regains his power and wealth, and the family is reunited.

Title: The thrown ring.
Summary: To signal their arrival, a person places, or more often discreetly throws, a ring or other small item of personal jewellery or toiletries into the jug of a maid or servant. Upon discovering it, the other person understands that the first is nearby.

Title: The wind blew away the flour, ATU 759C.
Summary: A man was carrying flour, but the wind blew it away. The man complains to an authoritative figure and usually receives compensation. Cf. motif M57d3 ("The Wind-Giver").

Title: Man in search of a woman, ATU 400.
Summary: A man sets out on a journey to find or bring back a bride or wife.

Title: The wind dries the laundry.
Summary: The hero searches for his magical wife who has left him. It turns out that one of the winds is flying to her to perform a certain task. The hero follows him.

Title: The wandering heroine.
Summary: A girl or woman sets off on a journey to find or return her fiancé or husband, or flees from danger, and her journey ends in a successful marriage.

Title: The enchanted husband drives away and finds his wife again, ATU 425E, 425L.
Summary: A girl descends into the underworld to her magical husband, and when she breaks the ban, he drives her away (sends her away with a task). She comes to live with other people, she has a child from her magical husband. Her husband finds her, the spouses are reunited, the spell is broken. {Motif in the work}

Title: As much gold as the bride weighs.
Summary: For an object (usually a girl), as much (or more) gold (silver) is given or promised as it weighs, or a pile of valuables as tall as the person being bought.

Title: The time of the wolf and the time of the fox.
Summary: The ruler demands an explanation of his dream. The snake tells the man that this dream signifies the coming of a time when people tend to behave in a certain way. This happens several times. Each time, the man's behaviour towards the snake confirms her words.

Title: The horse from the dungeon.
Summary: The hero finds a suitable horse in the dungeon (in the basement, in an empty castle, in deep mud, etc.), where it has stood for many years.

Title: Placing a hand on a horse's back.
Summary: When a person puts their hand on a horse's back, it bends over and falls. This is a sign of heroic strength.

Title: The deceived protector.
Summary: A supernatural defender comes to the rescue upon hearing the alarm, but stops doing so after the alarm has been raised in vain.

Title: The sleeping defender.
Summary: A mighty warrior residing in a cave (or crypt, etc.) will eventually emerge into the light (to assist his people), or he could emerge but chooses not to.

Title: Which fish swallowed it?
Summary: The character cuts open the bellies of aquatic creatures (birds of prey) or looks into their throats to find the swallowed person or part of their body.

Title: When the forest comes to life.
Summary: The character links the onset of an event that is impossible, in his view, with the time when the trees of the forest will start moving, as if they were people.

Title: Father fights son.
Summary: Not recognising his son, the father fights him and kills him. {In this formulation, the motif is rare, and in more general ones it has no clear boundaries}.

Title: The wise carving of the fowl
Summary: A poor man brings his master a chicken (goose, etc.) as a present. The master asks him to divide the bird appropriately among the members of his household. The poor man does it considering the symbolic meaning of particular parts (gives the master the head, his daughters the wings, etc.) and receives rich compensation. A neighbor brings the master five chickens but is unable to divide them approppriately. The first man does it again.

Title: The woman became a bear.
Summary: A young woman turns into a bear (in Asia, a tigress) and attacks her close relatives or husband.

Title: The Bear and Her Sister.
Summary: A young woman turns into a monstrous bear and kills most people except her younger sister (Ojibwa: the younger sister of her former husband). Their brothers (or one brother) return from hunting and kill the bear, or she dies while chasing them. Cf. motif L65D.

Title: The female demon and her brothers.
