Summary: The character invites aquatic creatures to count them, and to do this, form a chain; crosses it to the other side or climbs to land. See M3 motif.

Title: A severed rabbit tail
Summary: Trying to grab a hare, another animal tears off (bites) its tail. It's been short ever since.

Title: Careless step
Summary: When crossing a pond or descending from a tree, the character (usually despite a warning) steps at a specific animal or part of the animal's body . As a result, it falls into the water and often sinks.

Title: Provoked insult
Summary: Once in a situation where his life depends on the will of a demon or animal, the hero feels like insulting or hitting him. See M1 motif.

Title: The passengers of the sinking boat
Summary: Small animal characters sail in the boat, it sinks, everyone escapes as best they can.

Title: An Ungrateful Rat
Summary: rat drowns, has difficulty getting to the shore (usually an aquatic animal takes it), and mocks other animals (usually its savior).

Title: Hairy octopus
Summary: The octopus or star-fish was covered with hair but the rat had eaten it up

Title: Squirrel and fish
Summary: The squirrel and the creeping fish are smart and get medicines for each other

Title: Night with a partridge
Summary: A young man or girl spends night in the forest. The forest partridge (Tinamus sp.) provides him or her a fire, a shelter and/or a hammock but takes them away and flies away itself when the person does something wrong

Title: Journey to the end of the night
Waiting for transport
Summary: The character goes to the lower world, to the sky, to the country on the horizon, etc. and waits for someone to give him a ride to his goal. Usually, some animals/birds or celestial bodies follow by, and the last (often the Sun or Month) delivers.

Title: Thrown in the water
Summary: Birds or animals take the character into their boat, but take on a zoomorphic appearance and leave their passenger in the water (after he breaks a ban). (It is significant that the boat or raft only appears to be artifacts, but is actually the bodies of the corresponding birds or animals, or it is an ice floe; cf. Motive M31).

Title: The luminaries float above the hero
Summary: Person gets to a place from which he is unable to come out. Several (more than two) different celestial bodies rise and move near him or above him. He puts attention to them (and asks their help)

Title: The fox asks for help from people passing by
Summary: zoomorphic character (usually a fox) finds himself in a place he can't get out of, and consistently asks for help from animals (fish) passing by or approaching him. The latter helps.

Title: Fish help: offered and rejected
Summary: zoomorphic character is waiting to be transported across the water. Animals or fish consistently offer help. The character only accepts the latter's help - he was waiting for him to eat.

Title: A destroyed obstacle
Summary: Some characters (not humans) are struggling to break a strong barrier that prevents access to the desired location or to a high-value object. See also M8A - M8D motifs; they are included in the M8 motif in the correlation tables.

Title: Birds are hammering the rock: release from the trap
Summary: Animals, and more often birds, find it difficult to break through a rock from the outside or inside, make a hole in the tree, in the body of an absorber creature, tear fetters, etc., to help a character or get out of the confined space by yourself. The list includes groups whose texts deal with the exit of the first ancestors to earth from a confined space.

Title: Birds are hammering the rock: extracting water
Summary: Animals, and often birds, struggle to break through the rock to get water or honey hidden inside it.

Title: Cleaned eyes
Summary: Birds pierce through a layer of clay, wax, resin, etc., that covers the character's eyes or anus.

Title: Extend the hole in the body
Summary: Birds break through the hard cover on the character's body to reach his entrails.

Title: Trapped in a hollow
Summary: The character puts his head or hand in a hollow or (rarely) another hole), gets stuck in it, or falls into a hollow. Usually, as a result, the character dies or undergoes a metamorphosis.

Title: Turning into a tree frog
Summary: A character who eagerly sucks honey from a hollow and/or gets stuck in a hollow turns into a tree frog. See M9 motif.

Title: The girl and the honey.
Summary: A girl or woman gets stuck in a hollow while extracting honey, or greedily sucks honey in some other way and as a result dies or undergoes a metamorphosis; a woman stuck in a narrow passage turns into honey, into a honey bee.

Title: Unclean food.
Summary: The character gives others food extracted from his or someone else's body or contaminated with bodily secretions, without revealing the source of the food.

Title: Fish extracted from the body.
Summary: The character gives others the fish extracted from his body.

Title: Meat extracted from the body.
Summary: A woman feeds a man with good-quality meat or fat, which she cuts from her own flesh or extracts from her body, and stops doing so when he learns about the source of the food.

Title: Removes fat from the body.
Summary: Without harming himself, a male character cuts off, pierces, roasts, holds over a fire, etc. a part of his body (or his wife's body). The character cooks the meat, fat, etc. obtained in this way and treats his guest to it. This food is not perceived as unclean (cf. motifs M11B and M38).

Title: Salt from bodily secretions.
Summary: The character makes food taste good by adding salt to it. Another character learns that the cook extracts this salt from his own body (it is contained in his bodily secretions).

Title: The unlucky hunter.
Summary: Unable, unwilling or unable to obtain game (fish), the hunter (fisherman) cuts flesh from his own body, removes his own entrails and collects his blood. He usually offers this to others under the guise of animal meat or fish. Alternatively, a woman cuts flesh from her own leg to feed her husband.

Title: God does as he is asked, ATU 750A, 775.
Summary: A person appeals to higher powers with a request, without considering that his words may have a different meaning than he intended. Either a person accidentally utters the wrong word or accidentally and hastily expresses an empty or absurd desire. As a result, something happens that he did not want at all. Cf. motifs I58B and M13A.Most of the references in ATU 775 (Midas' short-sighted wish) are either incorrect or impossible to verify. In connection with this plot, the reference to Uther 2000 is taken into account only for the Lithuanian variant, since there is a summary of the Latvian one, and for the Greek one, since the motif exists in Ancient Greece and among the neighbouring South Slavs. For ATU 750A, the reference to Bäcker 1988 in connection with the "Chinese" is incorrect; these are Manchus, not Chinese, and the stated motif is not present in the text.

Title: Turned into stone.
Summary: A deity and a human meet so that the former can fulfil the latter's request. As a result, the human is turned to stone. Usually (except for the Squamish), one of the supplicants wants eternal life and is turned to stone. See motif M13.

Title: Sausage sticks to the nose.
Summary: People are promised the fulfilment of two (three, four) wishes. Without thinking, they wish for something they do not want at all. The last wish is spent on returning to the original state.

Title: Brutal murder of wife or son.
Summary: A man brutally murders his wife (rarely: children, fiancée, sister) and/or eats her flesh himself, or brings her flesh to her relatives (if he kills children, he brings the flesh to his wife).

Title: Roasted alive.
Summary: To take revenge on his wife or her relatives for (allegedly) causing him offence, the husband roasts his wife alive. See motif M14.

Title: Tied to a tree.
Summary: A man ties a girl or young woman to the top of a tree or places her on the treetop as if on a stake. People try to rescue her.

Title: The healed cripple.
Summary: The wife or relatives (often the mother) of the sick person do not care for him. He recovers, and those who treated him badly are punished. Cf. motifs F62 and F96.

Title: Gains sight by diving.
Summary: A character (usually a loon) restores a person's sight and/or health by diving into the water with them. See motif M16.

Title: A woman lies, pretending that a man has missed his target.
Summary: A wife, mother or grandmother directs the arrow of a blind man or boy at game, lies that he missed, cooks and eats the meat herself. See motif M16 (man is blind, K333.1).

Title: Mother or grandmother deceives a blind man.
Summary: The mother or grandmother of a blind man or boy secretly eats (the meat or fish he has caught), pretending that there is no food in the house.

Title: Wife deceives blind man.
Summary: The wife directs the blind man's arrow at game, lies that he has missed, and eats the meat herself.

Title: Stolen tackle, D657.1.
Summary: The character turns into an object of fishing or hunting and presents himself as a target. The fisherman or hunter does not harm them, but they take away what they use: arrows, darts, harpoons, hooks, bait; or they catch fish, having turned themselves into hooks; or they are caught but escape death by taking on human form again.

Title: Obtaining arrows.
Summary: The character becomes the object of fishing or hunting, presenting himself as a target for enemies. Numerous arrows, darts, and harpoons stick into his body without causing harm, and he carries them away. See motif M18.

Title: Obtaining a hook, spear.
Summary: The character turns into a fishing object in order to carry away the hook with which he is caught or the spear with which they try to harpoon him, or he turns into a hook to catch fish. See motif M18.

Title: Bait man.
Summary: The character ties another person (usually a child) to the end of a line, using them as bait or forcing them to catch fish with their hands.

Title: Severed beak, J2138.
Summary: The character does something unacceptable, is caught, and his beak or jaw is damaged. Usually (except for the Koryaks), people keep the torn-off beak (jaw) in their homes, and the character comes and takes it back.

Title: The fugitive hides with his protector.
Summary: The character runs away from his pursuer. The person, animal or object that the character asks for help hides him (and kills the pursuer).

Title: Under the pretext of illness.
Summary: The character is pursued by an enemy. An animal hides the fugitive in its mouth or on its body, and when the pursuer appears, it refuses to open its mouth or expose part of its body. (Usually simulates illness – toothache, etc.). Cf. motif i87ad.

Title: Every deception is the beginning of the next.
Summary: The character consistently harms others in such a way that each person who has been deceived is used as a tool to harm the next.

Title: The crane as saviour.
Summary: A long-necked bird living near water (crane, heron, bittern, swan) helps a fugitive escape from his pursuer (indicated in brackets). See motifs J44-J46 (a long-legged bird helps cross the river, drowns the pursuer; the pursuer is most often a bear).

Title: The crane as a watchman.
Summary: In a foreign house, in a foreign country, where the hero finds himself, the crane or heron is a watchman who must raise the alarm in case of strangers appearing.

Title: Feigned fear of imaginary danger, ATU 1310–1310C; K581.
Summary: The character pretends to be afraid of only one method of killing, which in reality is not dangerous for him (K581: turtle: If you throw me into the water, I will drown! ). {All American variants with a rabbit are most likely of African origin and are not included in the correlation table}.

Title: The turtle asks to be soaked, ATU 122G(2).
Summary: The turtle says that before eating it, it must be properly soaked in water, but once in the water, it swims away.

Title: The turtle is going to war
Summary: turtle goes to war and/or is captured. See M23 motif. Cf. motif K77 “Verlioka”.

Title: Kills a woman, captured
Summary: turtle man goes to war, kills people (usually a woman). He gets caught or killed. In his animal form, he continues to live on. See M24 motif.

Title: A holiday in heaven, K1041
Summary: To take part in a festival in heaven or visit a deity, a flightless character manages to climb high into the sky. He usually cannot go down the same way, falls and as a result dies, maims or metamorphoses.

Title: Ducks carry the catcher (grabbed by the legs)
Summary: The character dives under waterfowl and ties a rope to their legs to catch them. Birds soar into the air, lifting the catcher with them. It later falls.

Title: Ducks carry the catcher (strung on a rope), ATU 1881
Summary: The character catches birds by feeding them bait tied to a rope, which they swallow one by one, or by shooting several birds with one bullet, or by soldering birds drunk and tying up. Birds usually take off and carry away a catcher holding a rope.

Title: Returning from Heaven
Summary: The tree or staircase that people took to heaven collapses; on the way back, people fall down. Usually some stay in the sky forever or longer than others.

Title: Icarus(failed flight on artificial wings), K1041.1.
Summary: When able to take off, the character takes off but falls or stays in a remote place from where he can no longer take off.

Title: Trickster: identification with birds and animals
Summary: trickster is defined as a protagonist in the following characteristic episodes.

Title: Trickster - Raven (a)
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Raven(s) - main trickster
Summary: In three or more different episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is raven (crow)

Title: Trickster - Fox, Jackal, Coyote
Summary: Fox (a), Jackal, Coyote (or Wolf when, apparently, we mean a steppenwolf, i.e. the same coyote). See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The wolf is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of his stupidity or antisocial behavior, the wolf dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The bear is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of its stupidity or antisocial behavior, the bear dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The fox (jackal, coyote) is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of its stupidity or antisocial behavior, the fox (jackal) dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets. If it is not specified that a “jackal”, then the protagonist is a fox.

Title: Trickster - Jay
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Mink
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Skunk
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Wolverine is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of its stupidity or antisocial behavior, the wolverine dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Hare, Rabbit
Summary: See the motives in square brackets. They include traditions in which the hare/rabbit appears only as a trickster, and another trickster (usually a fox or jackal) often occurs.

Title: Trickster - Hare, Rabbit (main trickster)
Summary: In episodes involving deception, ridiculous, obscene, or antisocial behavior, the hare or rabbit is the main trickster. Traditions in which 1) a hare or rabbit occurs only once as a trickster, and another trickster (usually a fox/jackal/coyote) is typical; 2) Mesoamerican traditions in which a small rabbit is associated with a small a set of episodes and a high probability of recent African influences. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Cancer is a cunning winner
Summary: Cancer (crab) defeats or deceives strong opponents by cunning.

Title: The hedgehog is a cunning winner
Summary: hedgehog defeats or deceives strong opponents by cunning.

Title: Trickster - Owl
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Hawk
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: A trickster is a waterfowl or marsh bird
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The turtle (toad, frog) is a cunning winner
Summary: A turtle (toad, frog) defeats strong opponents by cunning or perseverance. See the motives in square brackets. The character is named if it is a toad or frog; otherwise, a turtle.

Title: Turtle, Toad, Frog are a loser trickster
Summary: A turtle (toad, frog) gets into unpleasant situations due to its own stupidity or carelessness. See the motives in square brackets. The character is named if it is a toad or frog; otherwise, a turtle.

Title: Trickster - Possum
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The Trickster is the Rat
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Mouse
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Earth Squirrel (Xerus inauris)
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Monkey
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: A monkey is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of its stupidity or antisocial behavior, the monkey dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster vs Spider
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Raccoon
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Anteater
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Porcupine
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Crane
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Armadillo
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The dwarf deer is a cunning winner
Summary: The character defeats or deceives strong opponents using cunning. The protagonists are dwarf ungulates, usually duker or deer - taxonomically distant from each other, but similar in appearance. In some publications on African traditions, it is difficult to determine which animal we are talking about, but it is certain that these are small cloven-hoofed animals, usually (always?) dukers. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Jaguar (ocelot, puma) is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of their stupidity or antisocial behavior, a jaguar (puma, ocelot) dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets. The character is named if it is a puma or ocelot; otherwise, a jaguar.

Title: The leopard is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of their stupidity or antisocial behavior, the leopard (panther, leopard) dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The tiger is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of its stupidity or antisocial behavior, the tiger dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Leo is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of its stupidity or antisocial behavior, the lion dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: The hyena is a loser and a loser
Summary: As a result of its stupidity or antisocial behavior, the hyena dies or suffers damage. See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Badger
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster _x0096_ other creatures
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Trickster - Wren
Summary: See the motives in square brackets.

Title: Beardless (Aldarkose)
Summary: hero of the story is a character named “Beardless” or Aldar-Kose (Aldar is a “deceiver”, a braid is “beardless”).

Title: Anthropomorphic trickster (miscellaneous).
Summary: purely anthropomorphic character, or a character who bears the name of an animal or plant but does not act zoomorphic in the course of his adventures. See the motives in square brackets. {Data not fully entered}

Title: Gypsy - a cunning winner
Summary: Being smart and witty, the Gipsy overcomes strong adversaries

Title: Gypsy - opponent and loser
Summary: The Gipsy (more often a female than a male) is an enemy overcome by the hero (heroine) or (rare) a weak failure

Title: The trickster falls, (ATU 225, 225A)
Summary: character who has no natural wings or can't fly long distances rises into the air, but falls or, having lost its wings, stays where he can't return from. (The motive includes several options, but even when taken together, they don't cover the whole world. Texts with M25 and M28 motifs are counted as including the M30 motif).

Title: They relieve the need for a fallen person
Summary: The character flying over the village falls, is tied up, and defecated on him.

Title: Birds take the feathers they have given
Summary: Birds give a non-flying or ugly character feathers so that he can fly or become beautiful, but then take them away.

Title: He falls, breaking the ban
Summary: A character flying through the air falls, violating the ban on talking, looking down, flying over villages, etc. (The character is not dropped by the person carrying it and flies above the ground, not descends from the sky or rises to the sky).

Title: Holds to a stick carried by birds, ATU 225A
Summary: To get into the air, a character without wings (usually a turtle or a frog) grabs a stick with the ends held in their beaks by two birds.

Title: Discharged into water
Summary: A character who can't swim asks another to take him by water. He agrees, but throws the rider into the water.

Title: Indigestion
Summary: The character swallows food or water, or his own entrails, pieces of flesh flow out and fall out of his ass.

Title: Eats what falls out
Summary: character's insides or pieces of flesh fall out of his back. He eats them, mistaking them for regular meat and fat.

Title: Sealed anus
Summary: The character plugs or seals his anus tightly (with wax, clay, grass, etc.), or someone else does it. See M32 motif.

Title: An attached tail
Summary: An object is thrown at the character, which turns into a tail, and the character himself into a corresponding animal.

Title: Who won't freeze?
Summary: Two zoomorphic characters compete to see which of them will spend the whole night in the cold and stay alive. By morning, one of them dies. Cf. K27A motif (the cold test does not involve a two-animal competition).

Title: Disassembled into pieces fits into the hole
Summary: The character finds himself inside wood, stone, ice, etc. He or someone else makes a hole, but it's too small. Then he disassembles himself (or turns into fog), pushes these parts into the hole and reassembles it.

Title: Shattered with an axe
Summary: Although the character's head or entire body is cut in two with an ax or split with a stick, the character remains unharmed. Cf. motive J22.

Title: Inept imitation
Summary: Person sees how others act using magic or according to their animal nature. He or she imitates their actions and gets into trouble. Actions are not heroic deeds, competitions or tests and refer to everyday activity, mostly to providing and cooking food

Title: Inept imitation: visiting, Th J2425
Summary: On a visit, the character sees how the owner acts with magic or techniques that suit his nature (in Africa, too, deception). He imitates their actions but fails. Actions are not tests or competitions and are not related to performing feats. This is mainly getting or preparing food.

Title: Imitates relatives or wives, ATU 552B, J2411.3.
Summary: The character imitates the sisters' sons-in-law or husbands, or the wife's brothers (shoshone's) or wives (comox and chalkomel). {ATU combines a motive with another}.

Title: The hen boils eggs
Summary: The hen (other bird) cooks her own eggs and serves them to other animal persons (who imitated her with disastrous consequences)

Title: Silly wives imitate a sorceress, ATU 898
Summary: The first wife, rejected or taken later than others, performs certain actions with the help of magic. Other wives try to imitate her but are killed, maimed, or disgraced.

Title: The young woman is waiting for her husband to guess
Summary: After the wedding, the wife is silent until her husband says certain words that indicate her origin. {In North Africa, the Pyrenees and the Arabs of Western Asia, the motive is very popular, which suggests that the list of traditions in which it is known may include some records that have so far been supported only with links to pointers, but not by the texts themselves}.

Title: Three daughters-in-law at the king's feast
Summary: Each of the three brothers comes to his father with his wife (fiancée). The younger brother or his fiancée is considered worthless, but the girl turns out to be a sorceress and surpasses the brides of her older brothers in everything.

Title: Hero warms and covers the nestlings
Summary: Mighty bird (more rare other creature/mythological person) helps a man (rare: a woman) because he (she) warms/covers from bad weather its/hers nestlings (children)

Title: Converting old to young, ATU 753
Summary: blacksmith (supposedly) forges a person, rejuvenating or revitalizing him.

Title: Converting old to young: an unsuccessful imitation, ATU 753
Summary: The character (supposedly) forges a person, rejuvenating or reviving him, the other unsuccessfully tries to imitate him.

Title: He cuts off a horse's leg to shove it
Summary: To shove a horse or donkey, Jesus (the saint) cuts off his leg, nails a horseshoe to his hoof, and attaches his leg back. The other character tries to imitate in vain.

Title: An old woman was turned into a monkey
Summary: A conceited smith attempts to rejuvenate an old woman (man). His magic helper tries to save the victim but all that he do is to transform the woman into an animal, usually a monkey

Title: Item characters die one after another, ATU 85, 295
Summary: Two or more characters, which are small objects or small animals, live or travel together and die one by one while committing protozoa actions.

Title: Hair neck
Summary: bubble-head, the straw leg, the hair-neck are successively dying, trying to act like ordinary people.

Title: Coal, straw, bob by the river, ATU 295
Summary: Several characters (usually three), which are small objects, go traveling and must cross the river. This fails.

Title: A blurred lump of earth
Summary: The character, who is a lump of earth (oatmeal, salt), blurred in the rain or after going to get water.

Title: The Hunting Needle, ATU 90
Summary: Several characters that embody small objects (and a squirrel with them) travel together. The needle penetrates the body of a large animal and kills it. (In the Baltic-Finnish texts, the needle first finds items that others find useless, but after the animal was caught, everything found turned out to be in demand for cooking meat).

Title: Cereals talking to each other, ATU 293E*
Summary: Two or three types of cereals talk to each other, act together, etc.

Title: Bursts with laughter
Summary: Several characters embody small objects and die one at a time. The last one left laughs and rejoices so much that he bursts with laughter (breaks his head, etc.).

Title: Sausage makes soup, (ATU 85)
Summary: Person who represents something fat (a sausage, a piece of fat, etc.) prepares a rich soup adding to it its own fat. Another person tries to repeat the trick and dies

Title: Mushroom and oak, ATU 293B*
Summary: mushroom (pumpkin) thinks that it is as durable as a tree.

Title: Misunderstood instructions
Summary: After receiving instructions, the character understands (or pretends to understand) them incorrectly or too literally, committing absurdly ridiculous or violent acts.

Title: Deer don't want to wet their shoes
Summary: fool lives with his brother (and mother), is sent on business, does ridiculous things (all or part of the above): releases animals from the trap, kills (trapped) mother ; cuts off the pet's legs or skins; takes the fontanel on the baby's skull for a boil and squeezes it out; tears a large piece of cloth and ties the pieces to swaying reeds; hearing the murmur of water, throws food into the water; puts the plague in the water; wants to salt the water and pours all the salt into the river. (There are other common episodes as well).

Title: Misunderstood instructions: one step behind, ATU 1696
Summary: character misunderstands the first instruction, promises to do the right thing next time; literally follows a memorized rule that does not correspond to the new situation; so multiple times.

Title: Misunderstood instructions: a sharp object
Summary: The character does ridiculous things, understanding the instructions too literally or one episode late (i.e., doing what was relevant to the previous episode). One episode involves improper handling of a needle and other sharp objects.

Title: A fool buys spoons and a table
Summary: fool buys spoons and/or a table, tells the table to go on its own feet, throws away spoons because they rattle. The two episodes are usually combined.

Title: A fool salts the river
Summary: After buying salt or sugar, a fool pours them into a pond to salt or sweeten the water.

Title: Salt is sown ATU 1200, J1932.3.
Summary: A fool (or a character pretending to be crazy) sows salt (small objects) like a grain.

Title: Meat is planted
Summary: Fools plant meat, horns, or bones in the hope of raising animals.

Title: Forgotten name
Summary: Forgetting his name, a fool remembers it when he accidentally hears a word.

Title: Did he have horns? ATU (1381B), 1600
Summary: fool kills a man, throws him into a pond, well, etc. A clever man throws a goat there. A fool searches for a corpse in the pond, asks if the victim had horns, etc. Everyone is obviously crazy, and the murder charge has been denied. {The Buryat and Yakut versions may be recent Russian borrowings. The ATU 1581B definition also includes an episode where a human corpse was replaced with a goat carcass, but most of the texts that have been verified do not contain this motive}.

Title: Oiled soil
Summary: fool sees cracked objects (stumps, earth, ice), sympathizes with them and oils them.

Title: A fool takes care of stumps
Summary: fool decides that stumps need hats, puts pots on the stumps.

Title: A fool turns to the shadow, (ATU 1681A)
Summary: fool takes his own shadow for a character chasing him and gives her his property.

Title: Sells a lizard a cow, ATU 1643
Summary: fool sells or gives an animal (plant, statue) meat, pet, cloth, etc., believing that the buyer will pay; or the fool works where no one asked him to, and takes the animal for its owner. When he comes for money, he beats an animal (a tree, a statue, follows an animal) and as a result finds a treasure.

Title: Frog strands
Summary: foolish woman thinks that frogs will make yarn or cloth for her, or buy yarn and throw the material into the water.

Title: A foolish woman throws away her yarn
Summary: Foolish woman throws her yarn ways (into the water, into the bush) and believes that somebody with weave it

Title: The fool sells his property to the birds
Summary: Fool sells property to birds and believes that they will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

Title: A fool sells property to a lizard
Summary: Fool sells property a lizard and believes it will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

Title: A fool sells property to a tree
Summary: Fool sells property to a tree (stump, pole, a cross in the countryside) and believes that it will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

Title: Fool sells property to statue
Summary: Fool sells property to the statue and believes that it will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

Title: A fool sells property to dogs
Summary: Fool sells property to the dogs and believes that they will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

Title: Kills goats that have eaten pears
Summary: fool led the goats to the fruit tree and killed them because they ate the fruit he had thrown.

Title: Pancakes on trees, ATU 1381, 1381B
Summary: Realizing that a stupid son, wife or (rarely) husband, after telling the truth, will cause trouble for the family, the mother or husband (wife) adjusts that the son, wife or husband describes events that They obviously couldn't have happened. They're mistaken for crazy, the message is ignored.

Title: Chicken Army
Summary: Realizing that a son or wife, by telling the truth, will cause trouble for the family, the mother or husband makes them believe in the invasion of chickens (geese, crows), in the rain of stones, in the rain, from which they go blind, etc. In all cases, gullible people are planted in a hole covered with skin, in a barrel, etc., and let in the skin of poultry pecking grain (in Kyurins, chickens bite grain in the yard). See M39a5a motif.

Title: The screaming judge
Summary: My husband found a treasure. He knows his wife will talk about it. In order not to believe her, her husband says, and the wife then repeats, that the judge suffered from the hail that fell at that time (soup spilled from the sky) (lost an eye, ulcers on his face). The judge furiously drives the woman away, the treasure remains with her husband.

Title: The master's devils were beaten
Summary: Realizing that a wife telling the truth will cause trouble for the family, the husband says that the sounds she hears are the screams of her master (official, etc.) who is beaten, dragged to hell, etc. She repeats this to the master (official), who declares her insane.

Title: Fish in the furrow, ATU 1381A
Summary: The wife throws fish into the furrows or into the beds. My husband believes that the fish ended up there on its own, he is mistaken for a madman.

Title: Misunderstood instructions: shorten the road
Summary: During the journey, a person allegorically asks someone else to say something, sing, etc., so that time on the road passes faster. He understands instructions literally by doing ridiculous actions.

Title: Clever daughter-in-law and captive khan
Summary: After a long search, the ruler finds an intelligent wife for his son. At the mercy of his enemies, he sends a message with one of them, the true content of which is understood only by his daughter-in-law. She destroys enemies and frees her father-in-law. (The boys have a younger wife instead of an intelligent daughter-in-law).

Title: The Crooked Tower and the Master's Daughter-in-law
Summary: The ruler, to whom the master builder went to work, is going to kill or maim him. The master asks to send a person to his house asking him to bring a forgotten instrument or something else. The daughter-in-law understands the true meaning of the request, captivates the messenger and saves her father-in-law.

Title: The Tsar Craftsman
Summary: The poor girl agrees to marry the prince only if he learns a craft. The prince fulfills the condition, then falls into the hands of enemies. He promises to make them an expensive item, let them sell it. His wife or (father, vizier) learns the job, the prisoner is released, the attackers are executed.

Title: Encrypted message
Summary: One of the relatives or spouses transfers a text or object to the other through third parties. Only the recipient understands the meaning of the words or the item handed over, saves the sender and/or destroys his enemies.

Title: Basket Maker, ATU 888A*
Summary: A person learns a craft (weaving, painting) in order to earn a living for the family. His wife is kidnapped (separated if he is with him). The wife finds out that her husband is there when she sees baskets or other items he has made.

Title: Sell and return the sheep
Summary: The father tells his son to sell the sheep (goat) and return it along with the proceeds. Usually a girl teaches how to sell trimmed wool.

Title: Six loaves (four coins), ATU 921A, Th H585.1.
Summary: person explains that he lends part of his earnings, and pays the debt in the other part, i.e. raises children and supports parents.

Title: Pluck a goose, ATU 921F*
Summary: The king tells the commoner to pluck a goose (geese, shear a ram, etc.). He understands correctly: to rob the vizier.

Title: The servant hid part of the gift, ATU 875A
Summary: A person sends food or things to another and tells the messenger to give the recipient some words that the messenger does not understand. On the way, he stole or ate some of what he was supposed to bring. From the messenger's words, the recipient understands what exactly was transferred and accuses him of stealing.

Title: Misunderstood instructions: washing with boiling water, ATU 1013
Summary: When instructed to wash the old man with warm water, the fool steams him with boiling water.

Title: Drops a door from a tree, (ATU 1653)
Summary: A fool drags the door from the house with him (usually raises it to a tree and drops it, scaring the crowd under the tree).

Title: Drops a heavy object from a tree
Summary: A fool or buffoon climbs a tree taking a heavy objects with him and then drops it frightening those who are under the tree

Title: Tongueless Robber
Summary: Using a stratagem, someone who hides in a tree cuts (bits) off the tongue of a dangerous person and the latter is unable to describe situation to his partners

Title: Misunderstood instructions: a play on words
Summary: The character asks a member of his family to bring vegetable products, cook food, and feed someone. He understands words as if he must kill a child (dog, etc.) and serve his meat. [section incomplete]

Title: Misunderstood instructions: a play on words
He attacks his own plague
Summary: A person does not notice that he turned and swam back on the way, so he takes his home for enemies, kills his own relatives.

Title: They row in both directions, ATU 1276
Summary: Once in the boat, some people row in one direction and others in the opposite direction, the boat remains in place.

Title: Horse egg, ATU 1319
Summary: A fool is told that a round fruit is a mare's egg (donkeys, elephants, etc.). A fool buys fruit for a lot of money. When he throws it or drops it, a small animal (usually a hare) jumps out of the thickets. A person believes that this is a foal (donkey, etc.) that has hatched.

Title: Shemyakin Court, ATU 1534
Summary: A person consistently and unintentionally harms others. The victims take him to a judge. He saves a person from punishment by making a formally logical but clearly unacceptable decision in each case.

Title: Under which tree? ATU 1543D*
Summary: When reviewing the dispute, the judge asks about the secondary circumstances of the case. The offender is exposed by showing that he knows (or, on the contrary, does not know) about them.

Title: Iron eaten and boy kidnapped, ATU 1592, 1592A
Summary: A person appropriates property. The owner or his assistant puts the kidnapper in such a position that he is forced to return everything (usually the victim kidnaps the child of the deceiver). {Apparently, all references in Ting 1978 do not refer to Chinese, but to Tibetans; Uther 2004 refers to the Dagestan text in Levin 1978, No. 52, but it is not clear which group we are talking about; there is also a deaf reference to the “Code of Japanese fairy tales - Tsukan”, it needs to be checked}.

Title: Mice ate iron, ATU 1592, 1592A
Summary: The character claims that the mice ate iron (gold).

Title: Oracle tree, ATU 1543E*
Summary: Two people hid their valuables together, and one of them secretly took them. He suggests asking the tree that grew in this place for clarification and hides his father in a hollow to broadcast from there. The tree is set on fire and the deception comes out.

Title: There was a hat, a head - I don't remember, ATU 1225
Summary: A fool is left headless (usually trying to get into a bear's den). When asked whether the deceased had a head, wife or someone else, they say that there was a hat (beard), but they definitely do not remember the head.

Title: Crying for an unborn child, ATU 1450
Summary: The girl weeps, imagining the dangers that threaten her future child; remembering an incident that could end badly; jealous of the fiancé she does not have; distracted from urgent matters, considering the name of the future child instead of meeting the groom.

Title: Jump into pants, ATU 1286
Summary: fool does not pull pants or boots over his feet, but jumps in them from above.

Title: To rake nuts with a pitchfork, ATU 1229*
Summary: Numskulls try to shovel nuts with a pitchfork. F stranger shows them how to do this work more easily with a shovel (a basket)

Title: Husband pretended to be blind, ATU 1380
Summary: The wife wants to get rid of her husband and usually asks the spirit to blind him. The husband hides in a hollow, behind an altar, etc., and answers on behalf of the spirit (usually advises to kill her husband with good food), or the husband tells his wife that delicious food can make you blind. Pretending to be blind, the husband kills his lover (and wife).

Title: The Hangman's Treasure, ATU 910D
Summary: After going broke, a person decides to hang himself, but finds gold (specially put by the father where his son hangs).

Title: Distorted instructions
Summary: The character is sent to get something relatively low in value. He asks for something else and shouts to whoever sent him to confirm the assignment. Usually, a weaker character comes to a stronger wife or son and tells her (him) that her husband (his father) told him to surrender to him, feed him, marry him, etc. {It is highly likely that American versions are borrowed after Columbus}.

Title: Eye juggling, J2423
Summary: The character throws his eyes (an inhaler has a tooth) up or into the distance. At first they return to the eye sockets, but then they disappear.

Title: Eyes taken out and lost, E781
Summary: The character takes his eyes out of his orbits and loses them. He usually regains his eyes later, makes new ones, takes away from another character, etc. See the M41 motif.

Title: Berry eyes
Summary: The character (usually after losing his own eyes) inserts seeds or berries into his eye sockets and sees again.

Title: Resin eyes
Summary: After losing his eyes, the character makes new ones out of resin or wax, sees again (often this is an episode on the way to finding good eyes, while tar eyes do not see well).

Title: When it falls off a cliff, it eats its bone marrow
Summary: Falling off a cliff and breaking his leg, the character eats his bone marrow.

Title: Bait figure
Summary: To kill or catch a monster, he sees a figure made of wood or clay or a living person. Most often, a monster's claws or sharp leg get stuck when they pierce a tree.

Title: Food thieves are the first humans
Summary: The character discovers that someone is stealing game or fish from his trap, mountain, etc. or ravages his garden, field; he or his messengers wait and catch the thief [magical tales clearly of European origin (e.g. Chamacoco, Wilbert, Simoneau 1987a, No. 121) are not included]. The kidnappers are the first people to get out of the ground, the first men.

Title: Food thieves are women
Summary: The character discovers that someone is stealing game or fish from his trap, mountain, etc. or ravages his garden, vegetable garden, field; he or his messengers wait and catch the thief. The kidnappers are women, or the aquatic animal is the kidnapper, but when caught, it gives the hero a woman.

Title: Food thieves are a young hero
Summary: A young hero steals the older character's food. He is usually caught, but not punished, but invited into the house.

Title: The predator pretends to be dead
Summary: When a zoomorphic character falls asleep or pretends to be dead (seriously ill), the animals he usually hunts gather to meet him. He catches or kills them, or they run away at the last minute.

Title: The old man and the beasts
Summary: A person is sleeping or pretending to be asleep or dead. Animals take him for a dead man - they mourn him, carry him to bury him, they are going to eat it, etc. A person beats the crowd and/or obtains benefits.

Title: Animals at the trough, ATU 179B*
Summary: The old man carries a trough and lies down to rest, covered with it. The animals take the trough to the table and bring food. The old man gets up, the animals run away, the old man gets the food.

Title: Plant boiled tubers
Summary: The character advises the other person to plant or sow boiled or roasted seeds or tubers, who follows the advice.

Title: An imaginary baby
Summary: Some creatures steal or own valuables. To return (get) them, the character turns into a small object, from contact with which a woman becomes pregnant, or into a baby. A picked up or born baby takes on its true appearance and steals valuables (including making the girl who picked it up pregnant, if that was his goal).

Title: A picked up baby
Summary: The character turns into a baby, is picked up by the owners of valuables, and then steals valuables or converges with a woman. The baby is not a demonic creature and does not intend to kill those who pick it up (cf. Motive L60).

Title: A born infant
Summary: The character turns into a tiny object or creature, swallowing or touching which a woman (usually a virgin) becomes pregnant and gives birth to a boy. He steals valuables or gets along with a woman. See M46 motif.

Title: Swallowed needle
Summary: The character turns into a needle, a garbage, a small insect. A woman swallows it and becomes pregnant. See M46B motif.

Title: The child asks for a toy
Summary: A small child cries and calms down only after being given a valuable item hidden in the house to play with. After receiving an item, a child or an associated character takes it away.

Title: The Sun is a Toy
Summary: They (promise to) give a child the Sun (and or the Moon) to play with

Title: The head is attached to the rear
Summary: When punishing a person or animal or restoring a dismembered body, a character intentionally or accidentally puts his head to his ass.

Title: The trickster turns into a bison
Summary: Trickster asks another zoomorphic character to turn him into a creature of his kind, but if he breaks the condition for transformation, he becomes himself again. Usually, a trickster asks a bison or elk to turn it into a bison or elk. The bison (elk) rushes to the trickster, which bounces off in fear. The next time the trickster stays in place, metamorphoses, but regains its former appearance after trying to turn another trickster into a bison, etc.

Title: A hero in someone else's skin
Summary: The hero meets a character from the enemy camp and, taking on his form, penetrates enemies. Usually, the hero kills the person he meets and puts on his skin.

Title: A substituted shaman
Summary: hero needs to penetrate unnoticed into the locus of dangerous creatures; he meets an old woman (usually a shaman, a doctor) going there, puts on her skin, and penetrates into dangerous ones in her guise creatures.

Title: Next to the stars
Summary: The character tries to join a group of stars (usually the Pleiades) or catch up with characters who run away from him and turn into stars; the goal of the persecution is sexual contact or the desire to be reunited with family.

Title: The meat is on the tree
Summary: One of the two characters gets meat. The weaker deceives the stronger one, hiding the meat in his absence to eat alone later.

Title: Mascara fresheners
Summary: The character (by deception) kills an ungulates. He asks another to refresh the carcass, looks for a knife to do it, or a fire to fry the meat. The other freshens the carcass, gives fire or a knife, but takes or tries to take all the meat for himself.

Title: Game dances around the hunter, K826
Summary: The character invites others to gather around him, focusing on an activity (usually dancing with their eyes closed or lowered), and then kills the crowd (usually one at a time).

Title: Crows and seals
Summary: raven gathers seals or other marine mammals around and deceives them into killing them.

Title: A bag with songs
Summary: Trickster claims he's carrying songs in his bag. See M53 motif.

Title: Reddened eyes
Summary: trickster, inviting birds to dance around him with their eyes closed, kills them one at a time and threatens to turn red at the one that opens their eyes; this is an empty threat, or for a bird that opens eyes and eyes have really turned red ever since.

Title: Imaginary enemies
Summary: The character pretends to be enemies coming; when people run away in fear, the character takes what the deceived people owned.

Title: Allegedly inedible whale
Summary: A character (always a raven) kills a whale and points others to imaginary signs that whale meat is not suitable for food. People believe and all the meat goes to the deceiver.

Title: Pretending to be a monster, it eats supplies
Summary: The character is involved in preparing food supplies. After leaving under some pretext, he returns in the form of a monster or predator. Everyone runs away, the deceiver eats supplies, and then returns as usual. As a result, it was exposed.

Title: The runaway wakes up in the same place
Summary: The character lives or stays at someone else's house; then goes far away, falls asleep, but wakes up again in the same house.

Title: Dangerous overnight stay
Summary: A human or weaker animal character takes a stronger character to sleep in a supposedly dangerous place where hot coals, sticks, etc. can fall on those lying at night; when A strong character falls asleep, his companion burns or hits him, pretending that both of them have suffered equally.

Title: The crocodile's secret
Summary: A weak character hits a crocodile, but the crocodile is safe. He says he would be killed if the attack hit a specific location. Next time, the same character hits this place and kills a crocodile.

Title: Bring tears and skins
Summary: A weak character is tasked with bringing the skin (paw, tears, etc.) of animals that are stronger than him or are difficult to catch. He cunningly performs the task. Usually a rabbit or hare completes the task, but does not receive the reward he expected. {In the New World, the motive is from African Americans}.

Title: Try on a snake
Summary: The character promises to bring a snake. The snake agrees to have the character measure its length. He ties the snake to a stick or, while measuring, finds out where to hit it to kill it.

Title: Fill the vessel with flies
Summary: The character promises to fill the vessel with small flying living creatures. He bets with them that they will not be able to fill the vessel. Creatures climb inside, the character closes the lid. Cf. K60B motif.

Title: Beads are like body secretions
Summary: Instead of the usual secretions from the human body, beads, flowers, gold and other valuables pour in.

Title: Where it comes, there's gold
Summary: When a beautiful woman walks on the ground, jewels appear under her feet, flowers bloom, etc.

Title: The male character exudes values
Summary: Instead of common body discharges a a man urinates, spits, etc. beads, flowers, gold and other valuables; valuables are produced by the very presence of particular male person. See motif m57a

Title: The female character exudes values
Summary: Instead of common body discharges a a woman urinates, spits, etc. beads, flowers, gold and other valuables; valuables are produced by the very presence of particular female person. See motif m57a

Title: The sweat of the Sun and the tears of the Moon
Summary: Beads or metals are the bodily secretions of a deity.

Title: The animal defecates with gold
Summary: An animal (donkey, bull, horse, goat, bear, leopard) or inanimate object makes gold or food stand out, or a character makes others believe that this is the case.

Title: Gold-producing bear
Summary: A man fights a bear or (Malayali) leopard and makes another person believe that this animal is defecating with gold.

Title: Bay, baton, ATU 563, 564
Summary: A person consistently receives magical items that bring wealth. Others replace them or take them away. A person returns what has been taken - usually by receiving another wonderful object (baton, whip) that hits the kidnappers.

Title: Donor Bird
Summary: bird consistently gives a person magical objects (or gives one, with which he receives the rest) or consistently fulfills his wishes.

Title: The tree makes wishes come true
Summary: The man was about to cut down a tree. It himself, or the creature living on it or in it, asks not to do so and fulfills the person's wishes.

Title: Wind donor
Summary: A person receives a reward from a character who is associated with the wind. Cf. Motive K175 (“The wind carried away the flour”).

Title: Frost donor
Summary: A person receives a reward from a character who is associated with frost.

Title: A trail or bush saves you from the heat
Summary: The earth is burning, the fire is chasing the character. A number of elements and objects refuse to cover him, saying they will burn or heat up; the last in the row shelters him. The earth cools down, the character leaves the shelter.

Title: An insidious passenger kills a carrier, K952.1.
Summary: A small animal asks a large one to transport it across the river; consistently rejects all the seats on the carrier's body that he offers; climbs to where the carrier is You can kill when the crossing is over.

Title: Porcupine at the crossing
Summary: After asking a large animal to transport it across the river, a porcupine kills or damages it. See M59 motif.

Title: Imaginary physician: finished off enemy, K824, K1955
Summary: After injuring a demon (robber), the hero goes to his locus. There he, or (rarely) his assistant, pretends to be a doctor and finishes off an opponent.

Title: The hunter comes to the one he wounded
Summary: The creature/character runs away or swims away with a hook, harpoon, arrow, or other object thrown by the hero in his body. Local shamans can't heal an existence/character. The hero or his friend comes to the wounded man's village, takes out the object that caused the injury, or drives him even deeper into the body. The patient recovers or dies accordingly. See L105 and M60 motifs.

Title: The shepherd explains how to cross
Summary: The hero meets a servant (usually a shepherd) and takes his form, after asking how he acts, how he talks to the hostess (usually finds out what to say in order transport the herd across the river).

Title: The imaginary servant licks his heels
Summary: The servant must lick the master or mistress's feet or wound. The hero comes disguised as a servant and instead of licking his heels, touches them with the animal's cut off tongue.

Title: The Imaginary Physician: Punishing a Scoundrel
Summary: Avenging the seized property (a pet or a bird), the hero repeatedly comes to the offender in different guises (girl, doctor, etc.) and brutally mocks him.

Title: Imaginary doctor: finishing off the victim
Summary: The deceiver, promising to cure a wounded or sick person, finishes him off and eats him or offers a remedy that is only worse for him.

Title: The crow eats fish
Summary: The crow promises to cure the fish, and eats it herself.

Title: To make the bear beautiful, ATU 8
Summary: A large predator asks (agrees with the proposal) to make his skin beautiful (variegated). The deceiver burns it (scalds it, burns his eyes, etc.).

Title: Incitement to quarrel (by words), K1084, ATU 1577
Summary: The character provokes a quarrel by telling each of his opponents how one of them allegedly used hostile or offensive language towards the other.

Title: Owners quarrel to get valuables
Summary: To get valuables, the character provokes a quarrel between their owners. When they start fighting each other, valuables fall out of their bodies and end up at the character's disposal.

Title: The character quarrels birds
Summary: The character (always a raven) provokes a seagull to quarrel with another bird, telling each one that the other was hostile or offensive towards her.

Title: The character quarrels stones
Summary: The character provokes a quarrel between two stones of different breeds. To do this, he told everyone how the other supposedly spoke hostile or offensive towards the former.

Title: The character fights fish
Summary: The character tells each of two different species of fish how the other allegedly used to be hostile or offensive towards the former. Fish kill each other and the character prepares them to eat.

Title: He tells everyone that the other is dying
Summary: character lies to each of the spouses as if the other had a misfortune. They run to each other in panic.

Title: Incitement to quarrel (action)
Summary: The hero quietly damages each of the two characters; they accuse each other, quarrel, fight.

Title: When aiming at a hero, they hit each other
Summary: Two or more characters aim their weapons at the hero in between, but they hit each other.

Title: Tug of war, ATU 291
Summary: A weak character takes turns negotiating with two strong ones to compete in a tug of war. They don't know they're pulling each other's rope or that they're tied to a tree.

Title: A hare in rotten skin
Summary: trickster wears rotten skin, pretends to be another animal, and says that the name (i.e. himself) has caused him to get sick. The animals are frightened, they do not dare to take revenge on the trickster for his tricks. See M62C motif.

Title: One field and two employees
Summary: A weak character alternately negotiates with two strong ones to cultivate the site. Each of the strong works in due time and does not know about the existence of the other. As a result, a weak character takes the entire crop.

Title: One assistant eats another
Summary: The character asks others to come to him (to help him with his work or get a debt). Those called come, each next one is stronger than the previous one and eats it (or the previous one runs away when they see him), the last two die when they fight each other.

Title: An enumeration of body members
Summary: Before reaching the part of the body that is most suitable for certain purposes, others are named or tried. (Cf. Motive F22: The enumeration is related to finding the partner's genitals).

Title: He pretends to own valuables
Summary: The character comes to the owner of valuables (food, fire) and pretends that he already owns them. As a result, valuables are made available (littoral is exposed at low tide, salmon spreads in waters, etc.).

Title: The trickster was pinched and the meat was eaten
Summary: trickster bakes meat obtained by trick, deception; immobilized by sticking to a tree, ground, or stone; at this time, another character (fox, wolf, coyote, birds) eats all the meat. See M53 motif.

Title: A squeaky tree
Summary: The trees are creaking in the wind. Hearing a creak, the character climbs a tree and gets stuck. See M65 motif.

Title: Lost loot
Summary: Having resorted to deception, the character kills the game, but the thieves take the loot. See M53 motif.

Title: The root eaten, J2154
Summary: After eating certain foods frivolously or rubbing his body with his spine, the character suffers from itching, diarrhea, or an irrepressible eruption of intestinal gases.

Title: A mountain of excrement
Summary: After eating a certain food, the trickster leaves a mountain of excrement that is larger than himself.

Title: The trickster was blown away by the wind
Summary: By stupidity or carelessness, the character causes a wind that blows him away. See the M66 motif (The Trickster emits a stream of intestinal gases).

Title: When the winds blow, it scares the game
Summary: Because of his own stubbornness, the character suffers from an irrepressible gas eruption and scares away the game with a loud sound. Almost starves to death.

Title: The head gets stuck in the skull
Summary: character is attracted by the inside of a large animal's skull (small animals or insects are dancing or feasting inside, or eating some meat); he sticks his head inside , it gets stuck.

Title: The elder poisons the younger ones with intestinal gases
Summary: The oldest character poisons the youngest with his intestinal gases.

Title: A pierced old woman
Summary: A character on whom an old woman defecates or whose face blows the winds pierces her from below with a sharp object. See M70 motif.

Title: Selected piece of wood
Summary: A character (usually carried away by a river or fallen from a height) turns into a piece of wood. Someone is picking it up. The character then takes on his true form, usually in the absence of the hosts.

Title: Hand in the back of the tapir
Summary: The character puts his hand into the anus of a tapir or other large herbivore and is unable to pull it out. The animal rushes to run and drags a person with it for a long time.

Title: Excretion substitution: who is stronger, K1721
Summary: Two characters compare their excrement or vomit to learn about each other's diet and decide which of them is the more powerful beast. One of them manages to replace the selections. (Traditions in which vomiting is substituted are greasy).

Title: Substitution of feces
Summary: Two (animal) persons compare their feces (with different purpose). One of them gets to exchange them

Title: Regurgitated food
Summary: A weak character regurgitates previously swallowed unusual food, or replaces his belching with a strong character's belching, or interprets his secretions as remains strong animals he ate. The strong believe that the weak are strong or have unusual abilities.

Title: Strange newborn names, ATU 15
Summary: The character pretends to be invited to visit several times in connection with the birth of a child, or gives names to various tracts that the boat passes by. The names and titles sound strange, but they become clear when it turns out that the character ate supplies.

Title: An imaginary visit
Summary: The character (several times) pretends to be his name (that he is going to visit), and eats up supplies himself. See M74A motif.

Title: The fox is in the boat
Summary: Travelling in a boat or on a sledge, animal person (always the fox) steals food supplies or ruins objects and accordingly to his deeds, names different places. These names seem strange to the person’s companions (“River of broken arrows” and the like)

Title: Who ate the fat?
Summary: The character adjusts so that the sign that identifies the thief who ate supplies or who should be eaten is not on him, but on another character (smears with leftovers or with the secretions of your body of another, replaces secretions, etc.).

Title: Handsome as a woodpecker
Summary: Having noticed the woodpecker's beautiful plumage, the wolf or bear believes that the fox painted it and asks the fox to make him just as beautiful. The fox burns it alive.

Title: Who ate the kidneys? ATU 785
Summary: God (the saint) travels with his companion. When he leaves, he eats the kidneys (heart, etc.) and says that the animal did not have kidneys. He continues to persist (even in the face of death), but confesses when he is promised wealth.

Title: Divides by biting off piece by piece
Summary: Two characters ask the third to share something edible between them. He bites off a little bit from each of the halves, because one or the other is slightly larger. As a result, it eats everything.

Title: Taken from vultures
Summary: The character attracts and catches corpse eaters (usually birds) and as a result obtains valuables or returns something valuable (fire, woman, animals, etc.).

Title: Revenge for falling from heaven
Summary: The character lures a veteran to avenge his fall from the sky. Either the (potauatomi) shovel drops the character or leaves him on top to avenge being lured and caught.

Title: The animal in the carcass was carried away by a bird
Summary: A person hides in the skin or carcass of a large animal. A bird brings a skin or carcass to the nest without knowing what it brought the person.

Title: Marco Rich, ATU 930
Summary: A person (usually of high status) learns that a poor boy who is born will inherit his property or become king. He tries to stop it, but what he predicted comes true.

Title: Intended wife, ATU 930A
Summary: A high-ranking person finds out that a (just born) poor or ugly girl is intended for him, or the girl herself finds out that she is destined to become a man's wife of high origin. A betrothed or someone else tries to kill a girl, but only hurts her and the prediction is fulfilled; if the girl is ugly, she becomes beautiful.

Title: Predetermined marriage: a bird tries to prevent
Summary: bird tries in vain to prevent the marriage, which she learned was inevitable when the future spouses were still children.

Title: Trojan horse: victory over enemies
Summary: Enemies are shown a life-size or larger image of a horse or bull. Not realizing that this is a ruse, they bring the figure to their own territory and are defeated as a result.

Title: The Trojan horse: getting a woman
Summary: To master a woman, the hero hides inside the hollow figure of a horse (bull, deer) or in an animal carcass. The character guarding the woman takes her to her. The hero gets outside and becomes a woman's lover. Or a woman hides inside the figure of a horse, which is taken to the man's chambers.

Title: Treasures on the mountain, ATU 936
Summary: A person is offered to climb a rock or tree to get treasures. A return descent is not possible. Doomed to death, the hero remains alive.

Title: Vulture knife
Summary: A man bereaves vultures of their hunting weapons or amulets

Title: A person climbing a tree has his leg cut off
Summary: A woman cuts off a man's leg when he climbs a tree; a man cuts off a woman's leg when she climbs a tree. See K13A motif.

Title: Soiled bed
Summary: The character stains another's clothes or bed with sewage or something that looks like sewage, threatens to ruin the air and accuse the other, etc.; taking advantage of the victim's confusion, achieves the goal.

Title: Tiny boy, ATU 700
Summary: A tiny little man performs a series of tricks, mocks people he meets and opponents.

Title: The tail boy
Summary: A tiny little man emerges from the severed tail of a goat or sheep.

Title: Too many kids
Summary: Wishing a baby, a childless woman gives birth to many tiny boys. She or her husband kill them or throw them away, but she stays alone and helps their parents.

Title: The boy is a severed finger
Summary: A tiny little man emerges from a severed finger.

Title: Pea child
Summary: A tiny boy (rarely a girl) comes from a pea (bean, seed) or from a spool of goat droppings, he is almost as tall as a pea. Or he was born after his mother ate a pea.

Title: Baby ear
Summary: A tiny boy comes from an animal's ear, compared in size to an ear, his name is “ear”.

Title: Substituted embryo
Summary: When a woman falls asleep, a joker (usually a tiny boy) places an embryo or the entrails of an animal or something similar next to her to make the woman herself or others think she has a miscarriage or that her viscera has fallen out.

Title: Sleep-related
Summary: When the inhabitants of the house fall asleep, a joker (usually a tiny boy) ties them together in pairs so that when they wake up, they quarrel.

Title: Reed Dancer, J1883
Summary: A person joins the dancers; it turns out that the dancers are reeds or trees in the wind.

Title: The partridge scares the offender, K932
Summary: The character insults a partridge bird, kills or offends its chickens; the partridge suddenly takes off in front of the offender, he falls (usually into a lake or river).

Title: Blind people
Summary: Wandering, the hero finds himself in a place where blind or blind (two or more) live.

Title: Vivid female ducks
Summary: The hero meets two blind women and makes them sighted. These women are birds (geese, ducks, hazel grouses, partridges).

Title: Don't go after a stuck arrow
Summary: The character is warned not to try to reach an arrow if it gets stuck in a tree. He breaks the ban and gets into trouble.

Title: Blind people in the sky
Summary: A person goes to heaven or (rarely) to the lower world, where he meets blind people (one or two), usually makes them sighted, and returns to earth himself.

Title: Healed blind people
Summary: A person meets (most often in the sky) one or two blind people and restores their sight.

Title: Don't herd cattle on giant land, ATU 314A, 321
Summary: young man undertakes to herd cattle and is warned not to cross the borders of a giant, dragon, witch, etc. The young man violates the ban and kills a giant.

Title: A young man returns sight to old people, ATU 321
Summary: A young man lives with an old man whose eyes or eyes were carried away by a giant. The young man goes to the giant, kills him, brings his eyes, the old man sees the light.

Title: It attracts people and animals
Summary: By playing an instrument or otherwise, a character is able to attract an animal or person far away from him.

Title: A blind liar is robbed, ATU 1577
Summary: blind beggar robs an honest man. He watches him and, when he enters the house, takes everything the blind man has accumulated. He often takes money accumulated by other blind people as well.

Title: Tail bells: tied voluntarily, J2155
Summary: The character sees that something is tied to the other's tail. He also wants such a tail for himself, and as a result he suffers damage.

Title: Tail bells: tied unnoticed
Summary: One animal person inconspicuously ties rattles to the tail of another. The latter thinks that he is pursued and runs in panic

Title: Who's older? ATU 80A*
Summary: Each character claims that he is older and appeared before this world or (Ingush) that his father was cosmic in size.

Title: He cries for dead children
Summary: The characters are arguing which one is older. After some people tell us how long they were born, the latter says that this and that happened in his memory at that time.

Title: Whose sleep better? ATU 1626
Summary: Two (or more) characters agree to give food to whoever has the best dream. One talks about a feast he went to in a dream (or says he was in a different world), the second admits that he ate everything alone - he was sure that after the feast, the first one would not qualify for food (which someone who finds himself in a different world does not need food).

Title: Who gets drunk faster
Summary: Animals argue who of them gets drunk easier. The last one falls down because he becomes drunk as soon as somebody talks about alcohol

Title: Revived from bones, E32, E33
Summary: A person, animal, fish, or (rarely) a large fruit is killed and eaten. After a meal, what is eaten revives, usually after the bones (seeds) are put together. Cf. motive C16.

Title: A revived goat
Summary: After supernatural characters put the bones of a dead and eaten deer, cow, ram, or goat in its skin, the animal is whole (and usually comes to life). See M84 motif.

Title: The dice are thrown into the water
Summary: An animal, bird or fish that is killed and eaten comes to life after its bones are thrown into the water. See M84 motif.

Title: A trip to the land of fish
Summary: A person enters a country from where fish come to people (and comes back).

Title: Birds eaten and animated
Summary: The character carefully preserves the bones of migratory birds eaten (not fish or animals) and the birds come to life again. (Episodes of reviving a domestic goose or rooster are not taken into account in everyday tales).

Title: Spirit Guest
Summary: Sleeping in a deserted place, a person finds himself among spirits. One of them explains that he has a guest, that is the same person.

Title: A sick tree
Summary: A person hears trees talking, one of which is (fatally) ill and suffers.

Title: Fox is bluffing, ATU 56A
Summary: character unable to climb a tree threatens to knock it down or climb a trunk if a bird or squirrel does not drop a cub or egg. The third character explains that the threat is untenable.

Title: The boulder punishes the offender
Summary: A rock stalks or otherwise punishes a character when he unfairly insults her (usually takes away her property, see motive L33).

Title: In a house where you can't see the owners
Summary: The character comes to a place that is abandoned or seems to have been abandoned by the inhabitants. He tries to take or touch things, but invisible owners prevent him from doing so, or the things themselves hurt him.

Title: Involved in a dance
Summary: The character follows the dancing girls and dies.

Title: Melted wax
Summary: A character is humiliated after an object or creature made of wax, resin, or excrement that he made himself or that he thought was strong melts warmly, the present.

Title: Horned hyena
Summary: Only horned animals are allowed to attend the festival. The hyena makes fake horns for itself, exposed.

Title: The snake guesses the material, ATU 857
Summary: Someone asks a riddle about the material from which a particular item is made or originated. It is almost impossible to guess, but the character learns the secret, forcing the hero or heroine to fulfill the conditions set. (Usually requires a girl to marry him).

Title: Marry a guesser
Summary: The girl will marry the person who guessed her name, or someone who will fit the ring, or someone who says what material a particular object is made of or originated, etc. The deceiver fulfills the condition.

Title: Lice skin, H522.I.I,ATU857.
Summary: It is required to sew clothes from the skin of lice (fleas) or guess the origin of a large animal, a large skin, the contents of the box; the animal (skin) arose from lice (fleas), in the box - louse.

Title: What did the tree grow from?
Summary: It should be guessed that the plant grew from a part of the body of a man or a snake or from dirt scraped off from the body

Title: The tree grew out of a snake
Summary: plant grows from a killed snake or part of a snake's body.

Title: The jewel tree
Summary: A tree is described on which jewelry or ornaments hang instead of fruits; individual parts of the tree are made of different metals or (semi) precious stones.

Title: Golden apples
Summary: The story mentions the golden fruits (rarely leaves) of a tree, usually golden apples.

Title: Rejuvenating apples
Summary: Owning some apples ensures eternal youth.

Title: The sun is rising from the west
Summary: The character was wrong when he claimed that the sun would never rise in the west or go down after midnight.

Title: Stepladder instead of wife
Summary: man agreed with another that he could take the first thing he touched from his house. The visitor is going to take his wife, but when he takes up the stepladder to go up to the woman, he is told to pick up the stepladder and leave.

Title: Dead twice, ATU 1537
Summary: Pretending that the deceased has just been alive for a relatively long time, the character accuses others of his death, receives a ransom and gifts.

Title: Imaginary murder (blood bubble)
Summary: The character pierces a container of animal blood or other red liquid, simulating murder or suicide. Cf. motifs K10C (wrapped in giblets) and M199H (Giant's ripped belly).

Title: Ash sold, (ATU 1535)
Summary: A person manages to fraudulently sell or exchange ash for gold and money. Others are unsuccessfully offering ash for sale.

Title: Leather sold, (ATU 1535)
Summary: A man is going to sell a pet skin. On the way, he gets big money by deception or by chance. Usually, upon return, a person says that he received money for the skin, after which others slaughter their livestock and try unsuccessfully to sell the skins for money they are not worth. (In India, the hero sometimes supposedly sells not skin, but beef, which is forbidden to brahmanas).

Title: The herd from the bottom
Summary: The character (pretends to) take possession of someone's property (usually setting the owner to be killed instead of him), says that he got everything at the bottom of the river, in the abyss, etc., to him they believe.

Title: Seated in a bag
Summary: character is placed in a bag or chest, locked in a cage, tied, etc., to drown, burn, etc. When left for a while, the character pretends to be in the bag voluntarily or because he does not want to become a chief, marry, etc.; the other agrees to take his place. See M91c1 motif.

Title: The postman hare
Summary: A person releases an animal or a bird - supposedly with his wife instructing his wife to cook food, etc. Another does not understand deception and buys an animal.

Title: The pot cooks by itself
Summary: A person removes the pot from the fire, its contents continue to boil, or the person prepares food in advance, puts it in a pot or pit. Another believes that the pot cooks without fire or incredibly fast (or that a stick, if it hits the ground or the pot, creates food), buys a pot (stick).

Title: Unprofitable sale, ATU 1551
Summary: The person himself or his little son goes to the bazaar to sell a cow (or another large pet). The crook convinces him that it is a sheep (or another animal that is smaller and cheaper). Each of the crook's friends confirms the score or gives an even lower grade. A man at a loss sells a cow for the price of a sheep.

Title: The hat pays the bills, (ATU 1539)
Summary: A person sells a hat to others, convincing them that it pays the bill, you just have to lift it up (throw it on the floor, etc.). He actually paid the innkeeper in advance.

Title: Tell them I'm dead
Summary: When enemies come to kill a person, he pretends to be dead.

Title: The drowned shaman
Summary: The character deceives others by passing off the dead as alive, directing suspicions of murder to innocent people, etc. When a shaman (less often a shaman) is ready to discover the truth, he succeeds in it kill and avoid being charged with murder.

Title: The Tsar orders himself to be burned
Summary: The ruler, the leader, believes that a man who escaped death by cunning returned from the world where he received benefits. It tells you to burn, drown, etc. yourself or your close associates.

Title: Glued lashes
Summary: Something red is glued to the character's eyelashes, he thinks it's a fire.

Title: Part of the body as a watchman
Summary: When falling asleep or going to do something else, the character tells a certain part of his body to wake him up in case of danger. The organ did not give a signal or the character himself did not listen to it, as a result, the misfortune happened.

Title: The guard was punished
Summary: The character punishes a part of his body (burns his ass, breaks his eyes) for not sounding the alarm. See Motive M93; cf. Motive M142.

Title: Mountain riding
Summary: One character invites the other to roll down the mountain to destroy him. Cf. Motive L42C.

Title: Mountain riding: antagonist victims
Summary: The demonic character kills his victims, provoking them to slide down the mountain.

Title: Mountain riding: trickster animals
Summary: By stupidity or negligence, a zoomorphic character rolls down a mountain and as a result dies or suffers damage (attacks the edge, falls into the water, etc.).

Title: The wolf under the mill wheel
Summary: The character is lured to look under the mill wheel, he dies or is maimed.

Title: The wolf under the mill wheel
Summary: The character is lured to look under the mill wheel, he dies or is maimed.

Title: Take the gift home, ATU 311
Summary: weaker character asks a stronger character to take the gift to his family and climbs into a basket, bag, etc. A strong character brings and leaves a gift without knowing that brought whoever sent this gift. Usually a girl hides her sisters in a bag (chest), and next time she sits there herself, and the cannibal believes that there are gifts for the girls' parents in the bag and carries the bag.

Title: Imaginary guests
Summary: In order not to share with family members, the character pretends to have guests and eats everything himself.

Title: A blind man asks trees, D1313.4.
