Title: The insides are visible
Summary: A girl is described, through whose body you can see her internal organs or the food she has swallowed. This is a sign of beauty.

Title: Like snow and blood, (ATU 709)
Summary: The character wants to have a child or spouse who is as white and blush as snow (milk) and blood.

Title: Beard cloak
Summary: A powerful character makes or tells you to make a cloak or fur coat from human beards and/or mustaches.

Title: Girl with scissors
Summary: A girl, a girl is associated with scissors (and a boy, a boy with a knife or an ax).

Title: A storyteller at a wedding
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula stating that the narrator attended a feast and/or wedding arranged by the characters of the fairy tale.

Title: It flowed down the mustache, but did not get into the mouth
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula that says that the narrator ate food and/or drinks, but they did not get into his mouth.

Title: Ice horse
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula stating that the narrator had a horse and/or harness made of wax, ice, linen, vegetables, etc. In most cases, the narrator loses them (they melt, they are taken away, eaten, etc.).

Title: Paper suit, X1853
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula stating that the narrator met with the characters described and that he wore clothes made of paper, glass, oil, etc.

Title: Selected gifts
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula stating that the narrator received food, drinks, money or other real world items from the characters described, but lost them against their own free will because of meeting dogs or people (robbers, boys, children or a neighbor).

Title: It's still lame
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula stating that one or two people who met the narrator after the fabulous feast or were present directly at it at the festival, became bald/lame as a result of hot food and/or a bone or bowl thrown on the head.

Title: We have achieved our wishes
Summary: fairy tale text ends with a formula that says that the characters have achieved their desires, goals and/or happiness, or that God has fulfilled their wishes.

Title: Hero dough
Summary: The warrior-hero was made of dough and then became alive (his name is “The Dough”)

Title: Pea-bogatyr
Summary: After swallowing a pea, a woman gives birth to a mighty hero.

Title: Alive if they didn't die
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula that says that if the characters are not dead, they are still alive. {Motive at work, more data}.

Title: They stayed there and I came back here
Summary: fairy-tale text ends with a formula that says that the characters stayed or left where the action took place, and the narrator returned home and/or came to the place fairy tale performances.

Title: Like the second moon
Summary: You can see a light that resembles a second moon or a second sun. It comes from a pretty girl.

Title: The path is a needle long
Summary: said that characters spend a long time (days, weeks, months, years) on the road, but end up walking a journey as long as a grain, needle, or other small object.

Title: When wheat grew on ice
Summary: said that the action took place when cultivated plants (wheat, cotton) grew on ice or salt.

Title: Bird's milk
Summary: Bird milk (variant: chicken, pigeon, hawkish, etc.) milk is mentioned in fairy tales, riddles, paroemias and conspiracies as something very rare and difficult to obtain or non-existent actually.

Title: There is even bird milk
Summary: It is said that somewhere there is (or was) even bird’s milk

Title: But there's no bird's milk
Summary: It is said that someone is only lacking bird’s milk or that somewhere the only thing missing is bird’s milk

Title: The bird does not have milk
Summary: It is claimed that the bird has no milk and/or breasts

Title: The roots of mountain
Summary: The roots (belt) of mountains or stones are mentioned in myths, riddles, spells, and songs as something that does not really exist.

Title: Stairway to Heaven
Summary: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a ladder or stairway to the sky (variant: a ladder in the sky) is mentioned

Title: Sky support
Summary: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a pillar of the sky is mentioned

Title: Sea cover
Summary: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a lid or covering for the sea, ocean or river are mentioned

Title: The bridge across the sea
Summary: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a bridge across the sea, ocean or lake is mentioned

Title: The water has no knots
Summary: It is said that water has no boughs or twigs

Title: A horse has no bile
Summary: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a gall of horse or ass is mentioned

Title: A horse doesn't have horns
Summary: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, horns of the horse are mentioned

Title: Until the boiler boils
Summary: time required to perform an action or elapsed since the event described is estimated by comparing it with the time it takes for water to boil and/ or food has been prepared.

Title: He looks one way, cries, looks the other way, laughs
Summary: formula that describes the confusion of feelings: when a character looks in one direction, he cries, and when he laughs or smiles in the other direction.

Title: The departure of birds
Summary: Late autumn and then winter sets in line with the departure of two or three species of birds flying in a wedge (Zugvogel).

Title: Sitting on three oaks
Summary: The ornithomorphic character is said to be sitting on several trees.

Title: Drives the enemy into the ground
Summary: hero drives the enemy into the ground, or he and the enemy alternately drive each other into the ground (ankle-deep, waist-deep, etc.).

Title: Trampled into the ground
Summary: The character's opponents trample him into the ground.

Title: Honey and oil
Summary: Streams (jets) that consist not of water but of honey (honey and butter, butter and milk, milk and blood) are mentioned as signs of generosity and abundance. Cf. H16 motives - H16B, K33F.

Title: Jelly shores
Summary: Somewhere milk rivers flow with banks made of jelly (porridge) - a sign of abundance (impossible in reality). Cf. H16B motive.

Title: Above the forest, below the clouds
Summary: is said about the horse that it jumps above trees (grass, the surface of the earth) and below the sky (clouds, clouds).

Title: Sheltered in the sky
Summary: The character is said to sleep under the sky (like a blanket).

Title: Which key is better
Summary: The character asks others which key is better - lost and found or new. This refers to a forgotten and newfound marriage partner (less often a direct question is asked about this).

Title: Three-fold twisted rope
Summary: The image of a three-ply rope is used to describe the invincibility of two close-knit friends

Title: The liver drowned and the lungs swam away
Summary: The fabulous or epic text ends with a formula stating that the liver has drowned and the lungs have swam away (surfaced, stayed, etc.).
